paras: The writing of the Mathnavi is delayed for a long time. A long time is required for blood to convert into milk. So long as your fortune does not bring about a new child, blood does not convert into sweet milk. Know this fact well. Until Zai-ul-Huq Husmuddin turned towards me from his highly elevated heaven, the truths had gone high above and beyond search. The buds had not blossomed into flowers of the spring. When he came up on the bank of the river, the verses of the Mathnavi became rhythmic, like the tunes of music. The process of the writing of Mathnavi, which is a polish for the souls, started pouring itself and opened its doors like the day of Istiftah (Fifteenth day of the month of Rajab on which the doors of the Ka’aba are opened for the pilgrims). The first verse of this second volume of Masnavi came about in the year 662 AH. This is a year of business and profit making for the seekers of spiritual matters.

Husamuddin, like a bulbul had left my company and later returned with greater enthusiasm like a falcon, to catch the preys of esoteric meanings. May God be pleased to provide the wrist of the king to sit upon, so that the door of the secrets that the Mathnavi intends to propagate may remain open till the doomsday. To reach this door of the other worlds, one has to crush the obstacles caused by sensual or carnal desires as, once after reaching it, there are plenty of varieties of pleasing syrups. If you want to see the pleasures of that world, you will have to keep your mouth shut to keep away the pleasing foods of this world that pass through your gullet. Mouth and eyes, as well, are the obstacles to know the meanings of that world. Eating gluttonously without caring to know of the means through which the food has come, legitimately or otherwise, is a gate to hell, in which case, this world acts as a barrier (barzakh) between paradise and hell, which has the markings of both paradise and hell. This world contains a light in its borders along with its vices just as the stream of clean milk flows along with the stream of blood (as in the body of females). If you take a wrong step in it, you will get mixed up, and your milk gets converted into blood in the reverse process.

sections.heading: Impacts of Sensual Desires:
paras: To meet the demand of this desire Adam took one wrong step to eat the forbidden fruit for which he got separated from paradise, which became the yoke of his neck forever. He became such a victim of shame, that angels ran away from him like from devils. For the sake of a little food, how many tears he had to shed. The sin that he committed was just of the size of a hair, but it was like a hair that grew in both the eyes. (Imagine the discomfort a hair, falling into eye causes. How much troublesome it would be, if it grows in the eye itself, rather in both the eyes). H.Adam from the beginning itself was an eye with all brightness, but hair in it became large like a mountain.

sections.heading: Seek Guidance from Elders:
paras: Had H.Adam consulted his wisdom, he would have not fallen into shame. If we also consult others in our affairs, we shall be protected from vicious results as coming together of our wisdom with that of others is a great protector from bad results. Similarly, if passions of one go along with those of others, immature wisdom gets suspended and becomes useless. If you are bright like Venus in your loveliness, you will become brighter like sun, under the shade of an elderly wise man. Therefore, go fast in search of a friend of God; and if you do so, God will become your friend. Even if you resort to seclusion as your guide, the methods of seclusion also have to be learnt from an elderly guide. Seclusion does not require to be resorted to with wise friends, but with strangers, just as a you do not wear warm clothes in spring season but only in winter. Wisdom, upon mixing with other wisdom becomes twice blessed resulting in greater brightness making the path clearer. Passion mixed up with passions of others, doubles up, increasing the darkness, hiding the right path altogether.

O hunter, your eyes are your friends. You cannot do anything without them. Keep them protected from all dust and dirt. Being in search of esoteric sciences, do not spread dust on your guides who are your eyes, with the lashes of your tongue. Do not give a scrap as gift to the eyes. When the face of the faithful is a mirror for another faithful, keep your face clean of dust and dirt, as your mirror should not show a dirty face. The guide is a mirror when your soul is in sorrows and shows you well. Do not blow your air on it with your mouth as it would become blur and hide your face from itself. You should always be holding your breath. You should not make yourself lowlier than mud, as mud never fails to pick up hundreds of thousands of flowers in one spring season.

sections.heading: Act as per Demands of Times:
paras: A tree that befriends the spring season, becomes happier with its friendship by becoming green and fresh from top to bottom. And during autumn, when it sees that its friendly air has turned its face from it, drags its head and feet under the blanket of deprivation. It says: a bad friend is a provider of calamities, and when it arrives, it is better to go to sleep. If I go to sleep, I become one among the companions of the cave (Ashab-e-Kahaf), who slept for a very long time to avoid all troubles, until there was a regime change in that country. Sleeping in the cave is better than remaining in the company of Dasinus, the cruel emperor, who was inimical to them for their beliefs. Had they not gone into sleep, their time would have been spent in cleaning harmful effects upon them. Therefore, their sleep was for a very profitable matter for them. Sleeping with lively wisdom is like waking; and as against it, remaining awake with sleeping wisdom is regrettable. Similarly, it is regrettable for one to be in the company of the ignorant. As crows have taken possession of the garden, bulbuls have stopped singing and hidden themselves. Just as the bulbul remains silent due to the absence of the garden, sun’s setting also causes sleep to wakefulness.

The sun sets upon this garden in order to rise and brighten the other side of the earth. Similarly, for an elderly wise person well aware of the gnosis of God (facts of life), there is no setting. He is absent somewhere but present elsewhere. Whenever he rises, as the sun in the east, he becomes the cause of nothing but the brightening of the souls and wisdom of the people, wherever they go. Particularly, God as the perfect sun and cause of light, keeps everything bright in both days and nights. If you are like Zulqarnain, dominant and wise in both east and west, start your journey from the east like the sun and become the cause of greatness everywhere on your journey. Then, wherever you go, that place becomes bright like the east, and your dominance will be such that the heights on the west will fall in love with your east and wait upon it like lovers waiting for the beloved.

sections.heading: External and Internal Senses:
paras: But, unfortunately, your sense of seeing is like that of a bat. It drags you along with your five external senses seeing, hearing, tasting, touching and smelling towards the darkness of the west. And your pearl-like-internal-subtleties will go in search of the brightness of the east with all heart. These internal subtleties are human soul. Desire of high achievements and hidden secrets, which upon becoming clear, lead you to the understanding of God and thereby everything of the world. But beware: the way to seek knowledge through the five external senses is the way of donkeys; but shamelessly, you are engaged with those senses only.

There are other five senses of a different nature apart from those of your apparent senses. These are radiant like real gold as against the former which are like copper. It is only these latter five senses which are valuable in the market of the other world. Such of those, who have seen the truths and realities of all the facts of the other world, seeing them from this world itself, are the people of the other world They will never purchase the copper like senses in exchange for gold like senses. Senses of the body purchase the food of dark senses for the body and apparent achievements; and those with the sense of soul, seek the food for their soul from the godly light, comparable for convenience sake, with the light of the sun.

That essence of God took this apparent sense of H.Musa towards the hidden world, entitling his hand to come out of his lapel with radiance. This radiant hand was meant to provide guidance to men like you to search for the brightest sun, like the light of God, though you can find out that sun the brightest object in the world, receives its light from the brightest light of God.

sections.heading: Different Conceptions of God:
paras: O God, sometimes, Your attributes are bright like sun and sometimes vast like the ocean. Sometimes large like the Qaaf (Caucasus) mountain and sometimes small like the bird Anqa. In your essence, you are neither this nor that, but something much ahead of imagination, rather ahead of the ahead as well. Soul goes along with wisdom and knowledge, even though it is imprisoned in the material body. It does not have anything to be with the Arab or Turk. It has no physical attributes.

You have no shape but so many shapes come about because of You, that many consider you to have a shape like humans (anthropomorphists). And, those who consider You to be unique and uncomparable, having only attributes, are wonderstruck. Sometimes You make an anthropomorphist into a believer of uniqueness and sometimes You misguide one of uniqueness as anthropomorphist. Sometimes even a scholar of the standard, Abul Hasan, H. Ali in a state of inebriation calls You as young child and sometimes as frail bodied. Sometimes a believer of uniqueness destroys his physical qualities and gets lost in your attributes to such an extent that he is virtually dead in the state of Your absolute purity, and he sees nothing other than You alone as existing.

sections.heading: Sighting of God:
paras: But the Mu’tazalite goes only by the sensory eye as the only seeing factor and that You can never be seen, even after the rebirth on the doomsday, as against the followers of Sunnism, who say that God can be seen only by the internal, non-physical eye. Many a times the Mu’tazalite gets confused and falls in line with sunnis. Yet there are many Sunnis who also believe that God can be seen by the external physical eyes, thus falling in line with the Mu’tazalites. That is to say: as per mere belief Mu’tazalites have a different faith, but in reality, they follow the Sunnis in actual practical belief that they can see God. The simple fact to explain is that, one who is entangled in sensory observation is a Mu’tazilite even if he proclaims himself as a Sunni (That is to say: no one can hold on to a particular line of thinking in the matter of observation of God. Their thoughts and beliefs are not constant but fluctuating, how much ever they may argue over the matter).

The truth of the matter is: whoever happens to see any mark of God through the light of God (other than through arguments, wisdom and physical observation) remains at His service all the time. One who goes beyond senses is a Sunni and closes the eyes of wisdom and follows the path of the men of sighters of God (Ahl-e-Nazar). He sees with his heart and not with his eyes.

sections.heading: You Cannot See God with Eyes:
paras: If the biological sense could see God, then cows and donkeys also could see Him. Had there been no sense superior to the animal sense, being special to man, other than biological and sensory and sensual, men would not have had the status of the honoured creatures and shareholders of both physical and spiritual senses. They would not be sharer of the secrets of God. As has been said in the Quran: “Walaqad Karramna Bani Adam”: (Surah Al-Isra: 17: 70). They became so because of their possession of both the senses. Your calling God as one with shape or without it, is meaningless until you do not go beyond shape. This question has to be raised by one who is the pulp or essence of the fruit, having gone beyond the concern for the rind. These questions do not arise for a blind as there is no question of seeing apparently for him. He is excused from all this anxiety. Otherwise it is required that you should patiently struggle to go to the essence, as patience is the key of expansion of everything including the heart. The medicine for all kinds of curtains for the eyes in patience only, which sets fire to the curtains and opens up the breast for visibility of all matters.

sections.heading: Creatures as Means to Know God:
paras: When the mirror of the heart is cleansed and polished, it sees such signs which are beyond the material world and external senses. It will see the signs as well as the Maker of signs. It will see the carpet of the palace as well as the master of the carpet. When the thought of H.Ibrahim come to my mind, I found that his saying upon seeing the star, moon and sun, in a step by step manner, that each of them was: ‘He is my Lord’, apparently admits of idolatry, but internally it was to break these, as he concluded finally: I do not love those that set: “La Uhibbul Aafilin”: (Surah An’aam: 6: 76). His accepting them as Lords initially was a prelude to denials. These became the means to lead him to God. Similarly, a guide is considered as everything (as a lord) as he is apparently with godly attributes and leading towards Him. Imagining him in the mind leads to God. Thanks to the grantor, that thinking about him and his grants lead to the thanksgiving to God. He and his imaginations become like the lords for some time until the real Lord is found out as was in the case of Ibrahim in respect of the star, moon and sun.

sections.heading: Good Things Go with Good:
paras: The dust of your abode made me fall in love with it. That is the dust, that made me careless about your dust. If I am good, God will accept me, and if I am ugly in thinking, He will laugh at my meaningless efforts. It is required of us that we should know whether we are worthy or not. He is beautiful and He likes the beautiful. It is quite clear that a young man will not fall in love with old women. Clean ladies are for the clean men, as stated in the Quran: and women of purity are for men of purity, and men of purity are for women of purity: ‘Wa attayyibatu Littayyibina, Wa al tayyibuuna littayyibaati’: (Surah Nur: 24: 26). Good things absorb good things within themselves. Try to understand the meaning of women of purity and men of purity. Whatever things you look at, you will see that they are of your own genus.

You will see in the world, everything has got mixed up with something. Heat has dragged heat toward it and cold has dragged cold. People of indecent and vicious character drag people of indecent and vicious character. Those of good character go with those with good character. Those on the way to hell drag similar ones toward them, and those of the bright light of heaven attract similar ones. Clean people pull clean people, and the unclean people go after the left over residue when clean things are filtered. Black people befriend the black. Romans develop connection with Romans. You feel very uncomfortable by shutting your eyes as eyes cannot have satisfaction when they are only half open, because eyes get pleased only upon being open in full. Your discomfort upon shutting the eyes is due to lack of absorption of light as by the open eyes. Eyes desire to be open to enjoy the light of the day. In case your open eyes also feel uncomfortable, it means that the eyes of the heart are shut. Know that the displeasure is due to not meeting of the demand of the eyes of the heart as they crave for unlimited light. Therefore, when you feel that these two types of eyes are uncomfortable, it becomes unnecessary for you to open your eyes in full and see the realities at least then. Be careful always not to keep the two sets of eyes away from light as per their needs. Be careful to see the type of discomfort each set of them feels.

sections.heading: Self-Introspection Takes to Truth:
paras: I start thinking when I am called upon, whether I am worthy of being called upon? I am acceptable or ugly? Because, if a beautiful person goes after an ugly one, there is every possibility that he does so for teasing and fun. Very rarely it happens that one looks at one's face critically to be able to say as to of what colour and face one is, whether bright like the day or dark like the night. As far as I am concerned, I tried to find out the worth of my soul very much, but it could not be revealed to me by anyone. I concluded that the purpose of the mirror is to make one know about one’s self. The mirror made out of steel is for the showing of the bodies, but the mirror to show the soul is very precious. The mirror of the soul is nothing but the face of the true competent guide: a face with its connections with the world of angels. I told my heart to go in search of the perfect mirror of the perfect guide! Go in search of an ocean-like guide, one of the small size of a stream is not sufficient. This desire has brought your servant upto your abode, O perfect shaikh. Labour pain of H.Maryam took her towards the date palm, under which she got the fruit, cold water and the face of her baby (Jesus). When your light became the light of my heart, hundreds of hitherto unseen hearts penetrated into it. I have taken out the mirror from out of smoke and then I found your face in it as my guide. I had always considered you to be a perfect mirror and I found myself in your eyes. Then at last, I said: “I have found myself in you’.

I found the straight path in his two eyes. But my suspicions warned me: be careful, this is only your imagination. Consider yourself also as your own imagination”. My own face (suspicion) has called you out from your eyes: “I am you, you are me and both are mingled into one”. My suspicion further told me: “Mere thoughts cannot find out their path in the ever-bright eyes of the master. Seeing one’s own face in the eyes of anyone else other than mine, is just a false presumption and requires to be rejected. If you happen to see your reflection in the eyes of others, you may consider it to be false and reject it outright, as this reflection puts the eyeblack of nullity and annihilation in your eyes and gives the tastes of the devilish-wine through his image. His eyes are a house of the feeling of nullity and non-existence, and inevitably makes you see them as real and existing.

My eyes have seen the eyeblack of the Lord of Majesty and Grandeur Whose house is a house of existence and reality and not imagination. So long as even a single hair of yours subsists in this material world, the taste of life will be lost into your imaginary-petty-thoughts. So long as even a single hair of yours is important in your view, the pearls of your thoughts will remain as petty worthless stones. You will get the capacity to distinguish between the pearl and ordinary stone, only when you get out of your own personally-involved-thoughts. O the one, who wants to identify the pearl, hear this narrative, so that you may learn to differentiate between reality and imagination.

The month of Ramadhan arrived during the days of H.Umar and every one reached the top of the hillocks, so as to see the crescent of Ramadhan as a mark of good omen. One among them said: “O Umar, see the moon here”. When H.Umar looked at the sky, he did not see the moon, and told him: “the moon is shining in your imagination; as otherwise, I am a better person to see the heavens. How can I remain without seeing the clear moon. Moisten your hand, and your eyebrows with it and then turn your eyes toward the moon”. When he did as advised, he did not see the moon, it was not observable. Then H.Umar said: ‘Yes, the arch of the hair covering the ridge of your eyebrow had become a bow for you, which shot the arrow of imagination toward you.’

When a single hair from his eyebrow fell on the wrong line, it gave the appearance of the new moon (crescent). One single hair going out of its way, misled the person to such an extent that he made an arrogant claim of seeing the moon. When a single hair became a curtain to see the sky, think as to what will happen when all parts of your body go out of the way. Try to pull all the parts on the right path with the guidance of those on the straight path and never lift your head from the doors of their abodes.
Only a balance can set aright another balance and also expose its defects. He who gets himself weighed by the misled ones, puts himself into loss and gets his wisdom spoiled.

sections.heading: Outer and Inner Enemies:
paras: Go and be strong against the unbelievers: and do not go to please the strangers: “Ashidda’u ‘alal kuffari”: (Al-Fath: 48: 29). Be a sharp sword for the enemies. But be careful to be straight like the lion and not treacherous like a fox so that your friends may not go away from you out of disgustion, as treacheries are like thorns in the gardens of friendship. Destroy your enemies as they are like wolves. Wolves were attributed by the brothers of H.Yusuf to be his killers, whereas, infact, his brothers were after his life. They had thrown H.Yusuf in the well, but told their father H.Yakub that H.Yusuf was eaten away by the wolf. Be careful, Iblis calls you with great affection to cheat you, just as he had cheated your great-grandfather, H.Adam. With his treacheries, he had defeated H.Adam. This black crow sits upon the chessboard of your life with all care and attention; and therefore, be smart and careful. Do not go into drowsiness, as he is well aware of defeating the bishop (the chesspiece of your game) and also penetrating into your throat like a scrap of grass. Be careful to know that the scrap of grass remains in your throat for years together; and know that this scrap is nothing but your love for great status and wealth. As wealth is destructible, it is just a scrap of grass, which by remaining in your throat becomes the cause of obstructing the flow of the life-giving-water (Aab-e-Hayat) into your body. Wealth also acts as a dacoit and enemy for you to take away your wealth. One dacoit loots the other dacoit.

A snake charmer stole the snake of another snake charmer, and foolishly thought that he got a fortune. Its earlier owner was saved of the snake’s bite, but the thief who stole it was severely bitten and got killed. The owner upon looking at the snake said: “That was my snake and that other fellow was killed by it. I was praying to God that I should get back my snake, take hold of it and re-possess it. It was a great grace of God that my prayer was rejected. What I had thought as bad for me was in fact good for me.”

Many of our prayers are causes of loss and are bad for us, but God rejects them as a matter of His grace. He is a benefactor and knows what is good for us, and therefore returns our prayers to us. But the one who prayed starts grumbling and takes this as bad. Thus, such suspicions become wrong. He was not aware that what he prayed for was a calamity for him and out of His grace, God did not grant.

A foolish companion of H.Isa on a journey said: “I have seen bones in the depth of a grave. O companion of mine, in the name of the great One with whose name you make the dead alive, teach me that art, so that I may do good acts and make the bones get back to life”. H.Isa said: “Keep quiet. This is not your job. Your breaths and words are not fit for that. That name requires that tongue which should be cleaner than rain-water and faster than the angels in speech. Many generations of living is required for the breaths to become so clean, and be the trustee of the wealth of heavens. You hold a staff in your right hand, but where do you have the right hand of H.Mūsa, which can exhibit the miracles”.

That man said: “If I am not capable of reciting those secret commands, you may yourself recite then on those bones”. H.Isa said to God: “What is this secret my Lord that this foolish fellow’s inclinations are towards this kind of talk? This sick fellow has no concern for his own sickness but is so much sorrowful for that dead man. His body itself is like a dead body and he is not bothered about it but is bothered to do good to that dead man?”
God said: “He is an unfortunate fellow that he is after seeking misfortune. He does not know that the crop he will get from his farming is thorny”.

The fellow who sowed the seeds of thorns in the world may not be searched at all in the garden. If he holds a flower in his hand, it becomes a snake for him. This hard-hearted fellow has a chemical like the snake poison, which is quite the opposite of what a pious person possesses. Be careful, never to trust his words and acts. He is like a rotten plant which never gives fruit.

A Sufi travelled around the world and one night became a guest in a guesthouse. He tied his donkey in the stable and sat down with his friends in a corner and engaged with them in discussions. Company of friends is a cause of large number of topics to discuss. A sufi’s record is not one of words and writings. It is nothing but a heart clear like ice. The assets of a wise man are the marks made by the pen, but of a Sufi’s are the light of God. He goes after prey just like a hunter for deers by looking at their footprints. After going for some distance, he does not need to search for footprints. Thereafter, the fragrance of the deer’s navel becomes his guide. Initially as, he valued the footprints up to some distance, he reached the destination. His master guides him initially, but later, he guides himself.

Going upto one mid-way station with the help of the fragrance is better than going around a hundred stations without it. Similarly, a man in search of God goes upto some distance with efforts and later the destination itself drags him towards it. In the initial stage, there are possibilities of his not finding the true path and falling into misguidance, but later on God Himself drags him. Therefore, it is better that one takes the help of even a non-coherently speaking Sufi than to go alone. That heart that has become the place of sunrise is like the saying: behold, when they arrive there, heaven’s gates will be opened: “Hattha iza ja’uu, ha wa futihat abwabuha”: (Surah Az-Zumar: 39: 73). What is wall for you is a door for them. There are stones for you which are pearls for them. What you see in the mirror is seen by the guide well behind the mirror, much before you. They are elevated, well-informed ones from that time when this material-lowly-world (Nasoot) had not yet come into existence, when their souls were swimming in the ocean of all Truths of God. They had spent long periods of time before taking the shape of the bodies. They had collected the crop even before resorting to farming. They had got the soul well before formation of their bodies and had collected and stringed the pearls of the gnosis of God even before the ocean with pearls was formed.

There were consultations regarding the creation of the world when souls of the creatures were already sunk upto their necks in the ocean of nature. When the angels came in the way of creation, opposing it, the saints clapped their hands silently to caution the angels. They were quite well informed of everything that came into existence, when the things were put into the prison of the shapes formed with clay. They had seen planet Saturn even before the sky came into existence and seen the bread well before the food grains. They were full of thoughts and designs without the heart and brain. They had won their victory (on the devil) without any army and battle. The observation of things yet to come in the material world is beyond the thinking of the common people who have lower grades of observation. But their observation was not in thoughts and imagination but actual observation. Thinking is related to past and future, but they are not bound by time. This is the difference between seeing things through thought process and actual observation. Everything is right before them. There is no thinking at all. They had seen all the effects without their causes; and the pure and impure products of the mines well before the mines. They had tasted the wine and its intoxication well before the creation of grapes. They used to see the coolness of winter in hot summer and shadows in the brightness of the sun. They saw wine in the heart of grapes and existence in the ‘adam (non-existence). It were their souls that saw the wine in grapes and existence in non-existences.

sections.heading: One Great Soul in Many Bodies:
paras: Sky is a drinker of wine from their gathering and the sky wears the yellow dress gifted by them. If you see two of them together, they are not two but one and also six hundred thousand at the same time. Their numbers are like the waves, which become countable with the blow of winds, while in reality they are only one ocean. The souls of all the saints are one in the Great Soul, just as the sun’s soul, which is one. Their souls become different in the holes of different bodies. When you look at the sun, it is only one, but its light gets scattered on the bodies and makes them different and distinct. When there is no light of the sun, everything is the same and one unseen in the darkness.

The difference of the soul is seen in the animal soul which dies along with the body; but the human soul is one and the same for all humans, which never dies. Human soul is a single unit of activity like God’s, but the animal soul is like a hard-burnt-earthen pot. God directed for the sprinkling of His light upon man and it fell unto him; and God’s light cannot be different on different things. Man’s wisdom being imperfect and partial, cannot comprehend this secret and no one is aware of it except God. That apart, wisdom has got nothing to do in this matter, just as a born-deaf has nothing to do with the tunes of the musical instruments.

Spend some time without anxieties, so that I may speak a little of the beauty of the mole on His face. The greatness of His beauty cannot be expressed in words. What are these two worlds? They are just a reflection of His mole. As I try to explain the beauty of His mole, my speaking capacity tries to tear off my body. What can I do? There is no scope for opening of the mouth. Therefore, the only way left for you is to put your own efforts to see His beauty. However, I am quite happy like the ant in the heap of this matter, carrying a weight beyond my strength to bear.

The one envious to the explanation of the secrets does not allow me to do my duty of doing the same. The ocean brings forth froth on its shore and puts an end to the motion of the waves. It drags the waves back and pushes their froth to create more froth. Now, you may hear as to what happened in this matter. The heart of the hearer went away from the place of hearing. His heart went towards the sufi guest and the matter of hospitality, he sank upto his neck. People are interested in stories. Now, it has become necessary to turn away from this talk and go towards that story to explain the matter. My dear, do not take the sufi as one, only in appearance and not at heart, like children who are interested in currants and apricots. Our body is of course like dry grapes and apricots, but if you are a worthy man, bypass the grapes and apricots to go to reality. And if you cannot do it with your efforts, be hopeful of the grace of God which would take you beyond the heavens. Now, you may hear this in the form of a story; but be careful to separate the grains from the chaff.

When the state of joy and ecstasy of the circle of those sufis came to an end, they brought food for the guest and then the sufi thought of his animal. He told the servant to go to the stable and prepare the millet and grass for it. The servant said: “Great God (Laa Howla). This direction is excessive. This is the job that I have always been doing”.The sufi said: “first puts the millet in water and soften it as the donkey is old and has weak teeth”. The servant said: “La Howla, what strange things do you say to me, sir. These are the jobs that People learn from me!”

The sufi said: “Remove its saddle cloth and apply balm on it's wound”. The servant said: “Laa Howla! keep this wisdom for youself. Thousands of guests have come to my place. All of them have gone much pleased with my service. A guest is as dear to me as my own life and soul.” The sufi said: “Make it drink water, but it should be lukewarm.” The servant said: “Laa Howla! I am feeling ashamed of you”. The sufi said: ‘mix a little grass with millet.’ ‘The servant said: ‘La Howl! Reduce your talks’. The sufi told him: “Clean its place of stones and its dung, and if it is wet, spread dry mud upon it”. The servant said: “La Howla! I regret, O elderly gentleman! Take God’s name on all this. Do not talk too much to a competent massager”. This sufi said: “Use comb and remove the thorns from the donkey's back”. The servant said: “Great man, enough of all this. Have a sense of shame to tell all this.” The sufi said: “Keep the donkey's backside with a small rope, so that it may not hold back when it has to turn back.” The servant said: “O fatherly man! Do not bother about the donkey so much. Do not cry over it”. The sufi said: “Put the saddle cloth on its back soon, as it is a cold winter night.” The servant said: “Laa Howla! Enough of all this. There is no bone in milk and do not search for it. I am a greater master than you in this job. Good and bad guests come to me and I know how to deal with them. I give appropriate service to them and for this service, I am like a valuable flower for them.”

So saying the servant readied himself and left saying: “First I shall get millet and grass for it.” He left and did not remember anything about the stable. And the sufi went into sleep. The servant went to some vagabond fellows and made fun of the sufi’s talks. The sufi was very tired of the journey, went into sleep fast and went on seeing dreams with closed eyes. He saw that the donkey was held up in the grip of a wolf and it’s back and thighs were being torne to pieces. He said to himself: “What is this madness? How strange, the servant is not to be seen.” Then he saw that his donkey was walking weakly on the way, sometimes falling into a well and another time into a pit. He was seeing strange incidents one after another and reciting Surah Alhamd and Surah Al Qaari‘a: The day of noise and clamour: (Surah Al Qaari‘a: 101: 1). He said: “What can be done! All friends are tired. All have gone away and shut the door.” Then he would say again: “That useless servant? Did he not become one with us in food and drinks. I have shown him nothing but love and regard. But why does he keep enmity for me. Enmity requires some reasons. Otherwise, being as one of the same tribe that teaches to be one, there is no escape from it”. Then he would again say to himself: “Adam had shown only concern and generosity to Iblees and never troubled him. What harm has man made to snakes and scorpions that they trouble him and desire for his death. Tearing is in the instinct of the wolf. And this jealousy for the creatures is well known to all men.” Then he would again say: “No! This kind of bad suspicion is not good. Why do I suspect like this with a brother?” Then, he would again say: “No this suspicion is a product of long experience of life. One who cannot suspect cannot protect himself.” The sufi was held up in these insinuations and the donkey was in such a state as would be of the enemies.

The poor donkey had fallen in dust and stones, with broken ropes and torne up saddle cloth. Tired of a long journey without any food, it was at times, as the one nearer to death or in death itself. It was calling upon God for the whole night saying: “My God, though I have given up the desire for millet, at least, I should have had a morsel of grass.” With its body language it was saying: “O great men!Have pity on me. I am burnt out at the hands of this incompetent caretaker. The troubles that this donkey faced are those that the birds of land see in flowing water.”

For the whole night it suffered. The poor donkey suffered from hunger as a man with the sickness of Ju’ul baqar suffers in which a man never gets satisfied with hunger, how much ever, he might eat. It cried for its separation from millet and grass and became crazy to this food. In this manner, it cried with pain and burns for the whole night till the morning.

In the morning, the servant came and put the saddle cloth on its back and gave two-three beatings, as the donkey-sellers do. He did with the donkey what is done with the dog. With the pain of the beatings, the donkey started jumping up. Where was a tongue for the donkey to speak of its pains?

When the sufi sat on the donkey and left, the donkey started falling on its face. Every co-traveller would make it stand up, thinking it as sick. Some would twist its ear hard and another would search for pebbles under its feet. Another would search for sharp stones in its hoofs and another into its eyes to test its colour. They would ask the sufi: “O’ shaikh what has happened to it. Yesterday, you were telling that it is quite healthy.” The shaikh said: “The donkey’s food was “Laa Howla” in the night. It cannot walk now, other than in this way. For the whole night it was saying praises of God and falling into prostration during the day.”

sections.heading: How to Deal with Well-Wishers?
paras: O man in distress, when nobody is interested in your job, it is required that you do it yourself. Most of the men are man-eaters, and do not remain satisfied with their assalamu alaikum (may peace be upon you). The hearts of all of them are the residing places of the devils. Be careful, not to be cheated by the manly devils. One cheated by the magical breaths of such devils falls with one’s head down in the battles of worldly life like the donkey. One who gets cheated by the mischief of the devil gets pleased with the false praises bestowed upon one by the treacherous devil. By these means, he falls down foolishly, like the donkey on the bridge of Sirat (Pul Siraat, as per the beliefs of Islamic faith). Be careful, never to fall into the net laid by the befooling attitudes of friends. Walk on the ground carefully and watch out for nets.

Keep in view a hundred thousand devils, always taking the name of God saying: “La Howla”, now and then. O son of Adam! Look for the Iblis in the serpent. He would say: “O my dear friend”, and make you remain content so as to pull out the skin from your body like the butcher. He will cheat you to pull out your skin, but the tragedy is with the fellow who eats opium given by enemies. He keeps his head upon your feet and makes a fool of you to shed your blood. Go for hunting alone by yourself like a lion and protect yourself from your friend’s showiness. Consider the concern and recommendations shown by the mean fellows as those of the servant. It is better to remain helpless than to see showiness of the incompetents. Do not build your house on another’s land and attend to your own job and not of other’s.

sections.heading: Your Body Is Your Enemy:
paras: Who is this other one?, it is none other than your own body made of mud, about which you are so worried. So long as you provide morsels of sweet and delicious food to your body, you will not make the contents of your soul stronger. You keep your body fragrant with musk ignoring the fact that after death it rots with a foul smell. Smear the musk not on the body but on the soul. What is this musk? It is the clean name of the One, Mighty and Majestic. It is the hypocrites who smear bodies with musk and despatch souls to the depths of the furnace of hell. He has the name of God in the mouth, but in his soul lies in the filth of infidelity. His recitations of the names of God are like the green grass on the garbage pit and flowers are spread over his filth. Such greenery in such places is only temporary. In reality flowers ought to be in the gathering of pleasures. Clean things are for clean people and unclean things are for unclean.

Do not have ill will, as those with ill will have their graves alongside of those misguided by ill will. The root of ill will is hell and your ill will is a part of hell and an enemy of your faith. This makes you a part of the hell; and as such the part seeks comfort only with the whole.

sections.heading: Those Alike Go Together:
paras: On the contrary, if you are part of heaven, your life will be everlasting due to the impacts of heaven. Bitter things get mixed up with bitter ones. Such being the case, vicious and wrong matters cannot get mixed up with truth. Such men with ill will go with their likes. Your being connected with heaven or hell is as per your thoughts and mind, while the rest of your body is just muscles and bones. Good and bad, and right and wrong qualities are related basically to the mind from where they pass on to the physical parts and muscles. If your thoughts are like the thorns, you are like fuel for a furnace. If you are like rose oil, you will be applied on the head and body. As against this, if you are like urine, you will be thrown out.

Look at the perfumer, who keeps the bottles of the perfumes of similar type together. He keeps together those of the same quality. This keeping together of those of similar qualities makes them graceful. Therefore, try to keep yourselves away from those who are not of your type. Company of one of a different type is like a grave. Remaining together with the ignoble is like a prison for the good people. Sugar and aloes-wood if put together in one container, do not mix up and remain distinct. So long as the souls were in the world of souls, the good and bad ones were distinct and separate and upon entering into the world of materials (Nasoot) they got mixed up.

sections.heading: Why Were Prophets Sent?
paras: God sent the prophets with their books, and their contents were spread out on the plates like grains in different positions according to their meanings and states. He sent the prophets to the world so that faith may be differentiated from infidelity. All faithful, infidels, Muslims and Jews, appeared alike. Before this, we were all alike and nobody knew who amongst them were good or bad. Both genuine and non-genuine were going together. The entire world was in darkness and we were all travellers in the night. This went on until the sun of prophets started rising and telling the people to go away from wrongs and become righteous.

Eyes can see the differences of colours. They can differentiate between the ruby and stone. They can recognise the pearl and a scrap of grass. That is why a scrap of grass causes discomfort to the eyes. Makers of counterfeit coins are inimical to daylight, whereas gold from the mines is friendly to daylight for the reason that daylight is a mirror for finding out genuineness, so that the noble one’s may attain higher status.

sections.heading: Why Doomsday and Not Dooms Night:
paras: It may be noted that Allah has called the doomsday to be on a day (not on a night), as day time has the capacity to show the beauty and colours of everything. [In the jargons of the sufis, the truth and reality of things are called Haqiiqat (Truth) and the container of this reality is called Zaahir (exponent, or form of things). The entire universe with all its contents is an exponent of all the names of God; and these names are both truth and exponents. And man is the most perfect exponent among all creations. The hearts of the sufis contain the truth of the doomsday, as they are the exponents of the name “Muqsit” (Equitable) of God. The day of the testing of the genuine and non-genuine is the doomsday and the hearts of sufis also test genuineness or otherwise of the realities of men and acts.

Thus, truth and reality of that day are in the hearts of the sufis; and against the moonlike brightness of their nights, days are dark as nights. As their hearts are the exposers of the good and bad of men, they also have the capacity to hide them. A day may be considered as the reflection of the inside of man and the night which makes the eyes unseeing as the reflection of their hiding capacity.

sections.heading: Wadhdhuhaa (Morning Light) of the Prophet:
paras: It is for this reason that God swore upon the glorious morning light: Wa al Dhuhaa (Surah Al-Dhuhaa: 93: 1). This al Dhuhaa refers to the conscious light of the heart of Hazrat Muhammad. Some others say that it simply means morning light which is loved by God, and does not refer to the light of Prophet’s heart. Even if it is taken simply as morning light, as they say, the base for its being sworn upon is for the reason, that though it simply means light, yet it is light from the reflection of the heart of the Prophet. God cannot swear upon something that is mortal as the light of the sun is.

sections.heading: H. Ibrahim’s Example:
paras: The statement of H.Ibrahim is that he does not love the things that set, which he referred to star, moon and sun, whom he had mistakenly called: ‘My Lord’ respectively at different times. And finally, when he found them set: he said: I do not love those that set: “La uhibbul aafilin”: (Al Anaam: 6: 76). Then how can God, the Lord of the worlds, love the mortals? When H.Ibrahim did not love the mortals, how can the Lord of Majesty love the mortals? Thus, this Wa aldhuhaa is in respect of exposition of matters by the light of the heart of the Prophet. Then, there is another factor of God as the hider of things (Sattar); so also the Prophet ought to be. Therefore, God also swore upon the darkness of night which hides by saying: by the night conceals: “Wa allaili iza yaghsha”: (al Lail: 92: 1). This is His hiding action (Sattari). Further the Prophet’s physical body also is hider.

When the Prophet, like the sun appearing on the Sky, appeared from the heaven of godliness, God warned the dark night of his body, saying: The Guardian Lord has not forsaken you, nor he is displeased: Ma wadda’ka, Rubbuka wa maa qala (Al Dhuha, 93: 3). The troubles and trials that the Prophet had undergone at the hands of his own People brought God closer to him by telling him: neither I have forsaken you nor I am displeased. This statement was a matter of great consolation for the Prophet. The phrase ‘Maa qalaa’: not displeased is to stress and eliminate the disappointment that the Prophet felt during the period of trial.

sections.heading: Connections of Hand and Tools:
paras: Every article and statement speaks of a particular situation. The situation is like the connection between the hand and the article made or the statement made. It is like the tool. The tools of a goldsmith in the hands of a cobbler are like the seeds sown in sand. The tools of the cobbler kept before a farmer are like keeping grass in front of a dog and bones in front of a donkey. The words ‘Anal haq’(I am the truth) were a light on the lips of Mansoor; and saying: I am God (Anallah) on the lips of Pharaoh were false. The staff in the hand of H.Mūsa was an evidence of prophethood and was just useless in the hands of the magicians. It is for this reason that Hazrat Isa did not teach the great name (Ism-e-azam) to his companion, for the reason that he will not accept his deficiency but blame the great formula. You cannot strike flint on mud and get sparks. Hands and tools are like flint and steel. A couple( of male and female) is required for the birth of a baby.

sections.heading: Eyes to Be Cured Through Ears:
paras: The one who has no consort and tools is God, the One and Only. There is certainty in His being One, but His plurality is full of doubts. Those who say that He is two, three or more are also certain and agreeable on His oneness (the other numbers are riders to one). They think Him to be more than one due to their being cross-eyed; and if they become normal, the speakers of His being two or three will become one to consider Him to be One. If you say that God is one in His playground, you should play with His ball. The good ball is that which is perfect and free of defects, which should dance upon the hitting of the player. The believer of one God should also play properly in the field of fate. O cross-eyed one, your eye is defective; and therefore, hear with your ears to get the treatment of the eye through the channel of the ear and set aright your belief. There are many clear statements which do not find a place in blind hearts, to lead them to the base of light. The magic spells of the devil penetrate into twisted hearts just as a twisted foot penetrates into a twisted shoe. Even though you may repeatedly speak of the statements of wisdom, their meanings remain away from you because of your incapacity. Even if you write them down and try hard to understand, those statements will turn their faces away from you. They will snap all the chains that keep them with you, and run away from you. Even if you do not acquire apparent sciences, but have enthusiasm to know, knowledge will become like a pet bird tutored by you. This will be of no use to you, as its reality cannot be gained without a teacher, just as a royal falcon cannot remain in the house of a villager.

Knowledge is that falcon that flew away from a king. An old woman, out of her foolishness, put grass before it. Consider knowledge as that falcon that flew away from the king and reached an old woman who was sifting her flour to prepare harira for the children. She looked at this beautiful falcon of good pedigree. She tied its legs and cut off its feathers. She cut off its nails and gave grass to it to eat. And she said to it: “Foolish people have not set you aright. Your feathers have gone beyond limit in size and the nails have also become long. Hands of every incompetent person have caused sickness to you. Come to the mother so that she may rid you of sickness”.

My dear friend, consider the love and grace of the ignorant to be like this. The ignorant always go on the wrong side of the road. The ignorant show sympathy for you, but ultimately cause injury to you.

The king searched for the falcon here and there for the whole day and ultimately reached the tent of the old woman. Suddenly he saw the falcon surrounded by dust and smoke. The king cried at this and lamented very much and said: “Certainly, it is the punishment for your own act, as you were not content with our love and concern for you. Why did you run away from paradise and enter into hell, ignoring this statement in the Quran: not equal are the companions of the fire and companions of the garden: “La yastavii As-habunnaari wa as-haabul jannati”: (Surah Al-Hashr: 59: 20). This is the punishment for the one who runs away from a king well informed of the rights of the people, to the house of an old woman.”

The world is old, mean, ignorant and worshiper of the ignorant one. One who turned towards it is foolish and disgraced. The wise is one who seeks refuge from this ignorant. Whoever becomes a sharer of this ignorance gets what the royal falcon got. The falcon rubbed its feathers on the wrist of the king telling without the tongue that it committed a mistake.

sections.heading: Arrogance of Prayers:
paras: Where else can a poor fellow cry and shed tears, O generous God, Where can a cruel, shameful head keep itself other than at Your door, if You are not to accept the prayers of those other than the noble one’s. Generosity of the king makes a man inclined towards sins thinking that the king converts all evil acts into good acts. Do not commit wrongs on this hope, as even our good acts will come before Him as vicious acts. You considered your prayers to be very good and valuable, only because, being a vicious fellow, you raised the flags of your vices in the form of your prayers. As you have become accustomed to your recitations and prayers, your supplications put your heart into illusion and guile. You considered God to be in talks with you. You should know that many persons have gone far away from Him for this reason. You should not consider the humility of great men and take them as your equal. The king sits with you on the ground out of his greatness of character. This should not make you forget your own lowly worth. Sit down with due respect before the King.

sections.heading: Convictions and Commitments: Greatest Weapons:
paras: The falcon said: “O king I am ashamed of my act, I repent for my mistake and become obedient to you once again as a neo-Muslim. You may consider the infirm steps of the person who is intoxicated with the wine of your companionship and accept his excuses and pardon him. Though I have lost my nails, I am yet capable of uprooting the flag of the sun, if you become mine once again. Though my feathers have been lost, yet if you put your graces upon me, I assure you, that the sky cannot beat me out in its revolutions. If you grant me the waistband, I shall uproot the mountains; and if you give me the nib of a pen, I shall pull down the flags of the enemies. My body, after all, is not lesser than that of the mosquito which turned upside down the empire of Nimrod (Nimrod, a great king during the time of H.Ibrahim, was killed by a mosquito which had penetrated into his brain through his nose). With all my weaknesses, I may be considered as the bird ababil, and every enemy of mine as the elephant. (Ababil had killed the elephants by throwing pebbles upon elephants tearing their bodies). I shall shoot small pebbles like fruits with my catapult which will be as effective in the impacts as the huge slingshots. Even though my stone is as small as a peanut; its hits will not leave any head and helmet unaffected in the battlefield.

sections.heading: H.Musa and H.Muhammad Compared
paras: H.Musa went for battle with just one staff, making it move upon the swords of Pharaoh’s army. Every prophet went alone on the battlefield. He was victorious upon the world from horizons to horizons. When H.Noah sought a sword from God, he made the waves of the sea act as swords. O Muhammad, of what account are these soldiers on earth? Look at the moon in the sky and tear off its forehead so that every good-natured and ignorant-superstitious fellow may know that it is your period now; not of the moon and stars. They do not play any role in the fate of men. It is your period. It is so great that H.Musa Kaleem had a desire to be alive during it. This was because, H.Musa during his lifetime itself, had seen the grandeur of your period that had the radiance of the Lord in all its mornings. He had said; O God, what a great period of Your mercy is that period, which has gone far above mercy itself, and that is the period when You can be seen, which seeing was denied to me by You, telling: Lan tarani: by no means you can see (Surah Al-A’raf: 7: 143). You had said O Musa! Dive down into the oceans and bring out your head during the period of Muhammad. I have shown you that period of Muhammad. I have opened for you the path that leads you to his companionship. O Kaleem, though you are far away from the time of Muhammad, yet you are in it. You may be there in it and wait and rest under the blanket of Muhammad as it is large enough to accommodate you.

I am graceful and generous, and therefore, show the bread to my servant so that he may crave for it to lead life. A mother smoothly rubs upon the nose of the child so that he may wake up and demand food. If the child is in deep sleep without informations around him, milk starts to driple from the nipples with all love and affection. “As per a hadith(s), the Prophet said: God said: “I was a hidden treasure. I desired that I should exhibit Myself and as such, I created all things. Then, I brought forth a well guided community of Muhammad”, (which was provided with the knowledge of my essence, attributes and actions). All the grants that you desire with all your heart and soul have been shown to you by his community, so that you may crave for them.

sections.heading: H.Muhammad Broke Outer and Inner Idols:
paras: Muhammad has broken some idols in the world making all other communities to call upon God. O my listener, had there been no efforts by Muhammad, you would have been worshiping the idols like your fathers and grandfathers (This is the grace of Ahmed that people stopped falling before all inferior creatures as he called man as the noblest of all creatures). Remember, your head got rid of falling before idols. Thanks for this is his right due from all the communities. If you want to thank him for this, you may do so, so that, thereafter, you may get rid of the inner idle hidden within yourself.

Just as he has rid your head of the dishonour of falling before idols, make use of this power and freedom bestowed upon you to rid your head of ignominy of worshiping this inner idol. But you have turned your head from thanksgiving for this as you got this wealth (of freedom) without efforts, but from your father. One who inherits wealth from ancestors does not value it, but one’s children get it without effort.

sections.heading: Cries Responded by Mercy:
paras: When I make My bondsmen cry, My mercy rises up and cries out to respond to him. The crier hears my response: “I am a granter; I am coming to you”. It is for the purpose of giving him that I make him cry to show My waiting grants. I show him My grants to give him. If my intention is not to give him, why would I show My grants to him. I narrow down his heart first, and then I expand it. My mercy comes upon much crying and after this, the river of My mercy starts flowing. So long as the child does not cry, milk does not spring up to feed. Until the clouds do not cry and drop tears as rain drops, the garden does not bloom and laugh.

The Shaikh was always in debts because of the generosity for which he was well known. He used to borrow in thousands from the rich and spend upon poor. He had got constructed a Khanqah with borrowings. His house and other things were also under debts. His name was Ahmed Khizrowiah. Serving the lovers of God was his profession. God used to get him rid of his debts by some source or the other. It should be known that God had converted sand into flour. (H.Ibrahim had sent his servant to borrow some wheat for feeding his guests. Having failed in his attempt, the servant out of shyness to go with empty bags, filled them with sand and returned. When he reached home; H.Ibrahim said: “Instead of wheat you have brought wheat flour”. When the servant opened the bags, there was flour in them).

The Prophet said: “Every day two angels pray in the bazaars. O God, return its equal to the expenders what they expend; and finish off the misers”. In particular that expender H.Ismail, who offered his throat for sacrifice in the name of God. He offered his throat for slaughter, but God did not allow the knife to do its job. That is how the Shaheeds live in happiness and do not die. Do not look at the bodies like an infidel. God returns to them in exchange an ever-lasting-life against their mortal life after death: a life that is without any sorrow, pain and misfortune.

The Shaikh thus borrowed for many years with full confidence. He would sow seeds of virtuous acts upto his last days so that, on the day of death he should be a leader. When he reached the last days of his life, he found the signs of death on his body. His creditors came over and surrounded him and in their midst, he was melting like a burning candle. The creditors were unhappy, losing hopes of getting back their money. The pains of their hearts had joined with the pains of the lungs. The Shaikh said to himself: “Look at these suspicious people. Does not God have four hundred dinars with Him”.

A boy shouted from the street about the sweets he was selling with praises of the sweets. The Shaikh gave a signal to his servant with his head to buy all of the sweets, thinking, if the money-lenders eat the sweets, for some time at least, they will not look at me with scornful eyes. The servant went out of the house to buy all the sweets. He asked him about the price of all the sweets. The boy said: “A little more than half a dinar”. The servant said: “Do not demand more from the sufis. I shall give only half dinar. Do not say any more than this”.

He brought the pan of sweets in front of the Shaikh. Now, the observer of the secrets of the Shaikh may look at what happened. He signaled all the creditors to eat the sweets. “This is a good Tabarruk (food full of prosperity) obtained from permissible earnings. Eat well to your full satisfaction”. As per direction, they all sat around the pan and ate the pleasing tasty sweets. When the pan was empty, the boy lifted it up and said: “Please give my dinar, O elderly father”. The Shaikh said: “Where am I to get the dinar from? I am already in debts and I am on my way to the world of non-material existence (‘Adam)”. The boy felt highly aggrieved and threw down the pan and started wailing and crying. He cried saying: “Both of my legs are broken. It would have been better if I had been moving around the furnace. I would not have had the occasion to come near this door. sufis swallow huge quantities of food. Searching for food makes their bellies like drums. They have the heart of dogs and mouths of cats. Cats always cleans lips with saliva”.

Upon the crying and shouting of the boy, good and bad people from the neighbourhood assembled around the boy. He came before the Shaikh and said: “O hard-hearted Shaikh! Be sure that my master has already killed me at this. If I go to him with empty hands, he is sure to kill me. Do you like this to happen?”. The creditors were also feeling unhappy of the situation and regretted at the Shaikh and turned toward him and said: “What is the strange fun? You have eaten away our commodities and going away from our rights. That apart, what is this cruelty?” The boy went on crying upto the time of ‘Asr prayer. The Shaikh kept his eyes shut and did not even look at the boy.

The Shaikh was absolutely free of cruelties and quarrels. He had kept his moon-like face hidden in his coverings. He was quite contented with the decisions of God made in the beginning of the world itself and quite satisfied and happy with the happenings of the next world after death. He was totally unconcerned with the remarks and comments of the big and small men. How could one whose soul is making sugar like smiles on his face be concerned with losses caused by the people? The eyes which are kissed by the soul have no care for the sorrows and wraths caused by the sky. What fear can the moon having reached its fourteenth station in the heaven, of the barking dog?

sections.heading: All Engaged in Allotted Jobs
paras: The dog is doing its regular allotted job. So also the moon is engaged in its regular job of shedding light on faces. Everyone is engaged in his routine job. Water does not give up its cleanliness just because a scrap of grass has fallen on it. The scrap is riding like a proud mean fellow on the face of water; and clean water is flowing in its way without any care and anxiety. H.Mustafa is splitting the moon and Abu Lahab, out of jealousy, is blabbering nonsense. That Masiha was making the dead alive and the Jews, out of anger were plucking their moustaches. Has the barking sound of dogs ever reached the moon and in particular that moon which is chosen by God. The king sits drinking wine by the side of the stream till the morning. And while hearing songs, he has no care whatsoever for the frog’s croaking.

A little money payable to the boy could be paid by anyone by collecting as donations. But the Shaikh’s inner sight had come in the way of their generosity too, that nobody should pay anything to him. The might of the great men is even above that.

The ‘Asr prayer was over, when a servant came in with a tray from some generous man. A man of heart and state, aware of the situation, sent a present in the service of the saint. There were four hundred dinars in the tray and a half dinar wrapped up in paper. The servant came forward, bowed to the Shaikh and placed the tray before the exceptional personality of the Shaikh. When the covering from the tray was lifted, people around him saw this marvel. All of them started sighing and wailing, saying: “What is it that has happened, O leader of great men and kings! What is this and what kind of kingdom is this, O master of the secret bearers! We did not know your great worth. Please forgive us for all the senseless things we have done to you. We are the ones who blindly turn our sticks all around, and certainly break the chandeliers. We are like the deaf who without hearing give their senseless replies.

“We did not learn any lesson from the events of H.Mūsa who found objections in the actions of H.Khizr, and thereafter felt ashamed. Saints like you look beyond the highest levels through their eyes of insight which tear off the sky and see beyond. O Khizrviah (Like H.Mūsa), we have given fanatical treatment to your eyes, with our foolishness arising from the eyes of the rats of the flour mill.”

sections.heading: God Loves Your Cries
paras: The Shaikh said: “I forgive you of all these denials, talks and quarrels. The secret behind this was that, as I had prayed to God, He showed me the right path. God had told me that these are a few dinars, but their coming to you is dependent upon the boy’s cries. Until the boy selling sweets does not cry, the ocean of My grants will not spill over. O brother, a child is your eye. Consider the reaching of your object to be dependent upon the shedding of tears from the eyes. All achievements of your objects are dependent upon your cries. Unless you cry and wail before God, success will not come to you. If you desire that your problems must be solved, you will have to convert the thorn of your deprivation into a flower with the water of your tears. If you want to get the royal apparel, you must make the child of your eyes cry to provide dress to your body”.

A God-searching pious man was told by his friend to cry less as it would cause damage to his eyes. The pious man said: “My state would not be other than one of the two consequences. My eyes would see that great beauty of God or not. If they see that light of God, there is no need for any sorrow. Two eyes will not be of any worth before His light. And if they do not see His light, it is better that they go blind.”

Do not worry. Your God is the provider of medicine to your eyes as H.Isa was for other people. Do not go wrong so that He may grant proper eyes to you. The provider of medicine for your soul being God, is with you. Seek help from Him as He is the best of the supporters. But never keep the free service of the bones of your body as something for His use, like that fool whose narrative, we have already made for the sake of the seekers of Truth. Do not pray to the provider of your medicine for the life of your body as people used to seek from H.‘Īsa. Do not seek the objective of Pharaoh from the Lord of H.Mūsa, who is (your Lord too). Do not keep the worries of livelihood in your heart. Let them be a little. But seek for your presence in His court. This body is just a tent for the soul just as the ark was for H.Noah. When a soldier enters into the service of the king, he certainly gets a tent for him and in particular, when he holds a respectable status.

As H.‘Īsa found that his foolish companion was not aware of anything other than arguments, and not prepared to take any advice thinking that H.‘Īsa is not teaching the great name (Ism-e-A’zam) to him because of his miserliness, H.‘Īsa recited the great name upon the skeleton to get rid of that fellow’s persistence. In order to take that man to his end, God gave life to the skeleton. And from that pit, instantly, a black lion jumped out which struck upon the head of that fellow and smashed it. It shattered his skull to pieces and splashed out the brain, like an empty apricot without seed. If he had the wisdom in the brain, he would have found loss only to the body, his wisdom remaining intact. H.‘Īsa asked the lion: “Why did you pounce upon him so fast to punish him?”. The lion said: “Because, you were in much trouble and mental tension, due to his putting senseless demands upon you”. H.‘Īsa asked it: “Why did you not drink his blood?’. The lion said:” Because there was no food meant for me in my fate”.

sections.heading: People Earn, but Do Not Eat:
paras: Many people like that ferocious lion left the world without eating the hunts made by them. They did not have a scrap worth in their fate, but their greed was as large as a mountain, searching for gains by all good and bad means from all types of people. They collected plenty of wealth and entered into their graves and their enemies and friends organised feasts in their sorrow.

O God! You have made this worldly life easy and comfortable for us. Protect us from this kind of free labour which gives us nothing. We saw morsels of food appearing for us, but they were the baits attached to fish-hooks. Show us the things as they really are (and not as tasty poison).

The lion continued: “O ‘Īsa, this hunt for me was for the sake of a lesson for others. Had there been provision for me in the world, I would not have died and joined the company of the dead. This is the punishment for the fellow who finds clean water but passes urine in it like a foolish donkey. If that donkey were to know the stream's worth, it would have kept its head in it instead of legs. That man like a donkey did not realise that you were a worthy prophet with life-giving-water. Instead of nourishing his soul from your life-inspiring message, he sought something unworthy from you. He should have lost himself in God, the commander of the command of Kun, with which everything came into existence, and sought another life for himself with another command from Him. But he went after the life of the dog of his vicious self, which was after his life. The noble Prophet has said: “Your greatest enemy is your vicious self which is between your shoulders” [Hadith(s)]. Fie upon that body of bones and flesh, which prevents one from hunting and controlling that dog of vicious self.

You are not a dog to be in love with bones, nor a leech in love with blood. What is the value of the eye that cannot see? It has nothing but disgrace for itself in times of trial. Many a times, there will be mistakes in our doubts. But what is this kind of doubt that is blind from the beginning itself?

sections.heading: Rewards of Weeping and Crying:
paras: You have wept upon others on many occasions. For once, you may sit down for some time to weep upon yourself. Trees become green and fresh with the weeping clouds just as weeping candles become brighter in light. Visit the places where there are people in pain and cries, as crying is more rewarding for you. Cry upon yourself too, as it refreshes your soul as it happens with clouds and weeping candles.

sections.heading: Bling Followership: Uncritical Faith (Taqliid):
paras: There are many who cry upon the separation by death of their dear ones, who are also mortals like themselves. They are not aware of the mines of the rubies of everlastingness. This is because of the fact that the impressions of imitations and blind followership have blocked their hearts. There is a scope to wipe off their impressions with tears. Blind followership (uncritical faith) destroys all good acts. Even if it is as strong as a mountain, it's worth is only of a scrap. Mourning upon the dead is prohibited for the reason that it is blind followership. Mourners look at each other and cry in an imitative manner. Even if a blind man is very well-built and ferocious, he is just a lump of flesh because he does not have the eyes. This is the example of a blind follower (Muqallid). Even if he talks of very subtle and fine matters, his head fails to grasp. He alone is intoxicated with his own statements. His intoxication does not have any impact upon others just as wine intoxicates all. He is like a stream, which does not drink water. Its water goes upto those who need it. The stream does not drink water, as it is not thirsty. It does not need water and therefore, its water flows away. This is like the flute that cries and laments, but it does not serve itself but renders free service to its buyer. Similar is the case of the blind-following preacher without practising what he preaches.

sections.heading: Blind Follower: Like a Mourner:
paras: A professional mourner is a blind follower of the money paid for mourning. He does not have anything other than money in his view. He speaks of many grief-causing statements from his mouth, but does not have the burning of the heart and a torne lapel.

There is great difference between a blind follower of faith and one who has searched and reached on matters of faith. The researcher is like Hazrat Dawood upon whose singing, birds and animals used to go in ecstasy, and the blind follower is like the echo. The former is a source of soul inspiring passions and the latter is only a repeater of words. Do not fall into confusion because of his repetitive words. They are like the rattling sounds of the cart wheels. The burden of the load falls on the oxen.

Yet a blind follower is not deprived of reward just like the professional mourner. Both the faithful and infidel say: “O my God''. Yet there is a vast difference in their saying. The beggar says “O my God” for the sake of bread, but the pious says so in his heart with a state of the soul. You also say “O God” repeatedly with the physical force of the lungs. Give up all greed and go forward to call God’s names. If the beggar were to know the value of what he says, he would not bother so much about the world, either less or more. For years together, that searcher of bread says: “O my God”. He carries the Quran like a donkey. There is a reference in the Qur'ān about the carriers of the Torah without following it, as donkeys which carry books. (The similitude of those who were charged with the obligations of the Mosaic law, who subsequently failed in those obligations is that of a donkey which carries tonnes of books but does not understand them): “Math(s)alul lazina hummilutawrata, th(s)umma lam yahmiluuha kamath(s)a lil himaari yahmilu asfaran”: (Al Jum’a: 62: 5).

They carry the Qurān like a donkey for the sake of grass. If the name of God were to cast light on their heart, their bodies would have been torne to pieces. Name of the devil is taken in magical performances, but you take the name of God on your lips for a penny.

A villager tied his cow in the cowshed and a lion killed and ate it and put its skin on itself and sat in its place. The villager went near the cow’s place searching for it in the darkness of the night. He was spreading his hand with affection on its limbs, waist, sides and sometimes up and down. The lion said: “If the light had been sufficient, it would have torne his gallbladder; and his heart would have become blood out of fear. Without any fear, he spreads his hand on me, as he is thinking of me as a cow in the darkness”.

God puts the question to such fellows: “You being under the wrong impression forget that Mount Tur had shattered into pieces due to the impact of My name. Had We sent the book on the mountain, you would have seen it humble itself and cleave asunder for fear of God: “Lau anzalnaa haza alquran 'alaa jabalin la-araitahu khashi’an, mutasaddi’an, min khashi yatallahi” (Al-Hashar: 59: 21).

“If the mount of Uhud were to know Me, it would have broken into pieces and its heart would have turned into blood. You have heard of this from your father and mother, yet you are involved in this ignorance. If you come to know of this without just hearing from others as a blind follower, you would become one without any marks like angel Hatif (whose sounds alone are heard, but who would not be seen). As a warning, hear this story so that you may become aware of the dangers of blind followership.

A sufi reached a khanqah on the way of his long journey. He took his donkey and tied it in the stable. He gave water to it with his own hands and provided grains, unlike the other sufi whose incident we have already narrated. He took all the care required for his donkey and avoided any carelessness and forgetfulness. But what is the good of all care and attention, when fate comes to play its role. There were other sufis in that khanqah, who were in extreme poverty.” Extreme poverty is very near to a great infidelity”, as stated by the noble Prophet.

O rich fellow, you are belly-full. Do not laugh at the wrong acts of a destitute in distress. Those sufis, out of their wrong doings resorted to sell the donkey of this newly arrived sufi. Because they thought that in an extreme situation of need a dead animal is permitted to be eaten. Many wrongs become right in extreme situations of distress. They sold the donkey and bought tasty dishes and brightened the lamp to organise a music session. There was a loud cry of merriment in the khanqah. There was a delicious dinner that night and a great enjoyment of a music session. They had thought: “How much patience and starvation of three days? How long to carry the begging bowl and begging. We are also creatures like others and we too have life. Tonight, wealth is our guest”. They had sowed the seed of illegality, thinking the vicious self as their life which, in fact, is not.

The newly arrived sufi was much tired of a long journey and he looked at this arrangement of pleasures and merriment. Every Sufi came to him and honoured him and resorted to all types of tricks to keep him pleased. One pressed his feet and the other dusted his seating place to sit, eat and stay. Another dusted his goods and materials, and another kissed his hands and face. When he saw all these pleasing inclinations he said to himself: “When else can I have a situation of pleasure and comfort if not on this day?”. All of them finished their dinner and started the music session. The khanqah got filled up with the smoke of the kitchen and dust of the ground due to their dancing and thumping steps. Sometimes they used to spread their hands and beat their feet and sometimes fell on the platform and wiped it with their faces.

Sufi gets his food from this world after a long time. Therefore, he is a good eater. Except that sufi, who fills his belly with the light of God not being in need of the disgrace of tapping the doors of others. A few, out of thousands, are of this type, but the rest live upon these things.

When the music session was about to reach the end, the qawwal started singing a very exciting song. He started this song with the words: “The donkey went away; the donkey went away”, in a very exciting tune. Its heat made all of them go into ecstasy and all started singing these words together. In their enthusiasm, they were beating their feet on the ground and dancing and clapping their hands and singing: “the donkey went away my son; the donkey went away”. As a matter of blind followership, this sufi also joined them in chorus, singing in a crying voice: “the donkey went away; the donkey went away”.

When that eating, drinking, enthusiasm and music session came to the end, it was the daytime and all the sufis had left. The khanqah was empty and only this sufi on journey was left alone and he started dusting his materials.
