paras: The prophets see what comes later; that is, the doomsday, whereas the man of ordinary sight sees only the present day: He does not see the treasure but sees a penny. The noble Prophet was a treasure, but Abu jahl saw only a penny in him. He was such a great sun that if the sun were to receive a particle from him, it would turn as a slave to that particle.

He was only a drop from the ocean of the oneness of God, but came as His messenger with such great merit that all the seven oceans became obedient to that drop. If a fistful of his clay were to command obedience, the heavens would have kept their heads upon it in obedience. The clay of H.Adam commanded obedience and all other creatures of God kept their heads upon it. What do you consider the meaning of the statement: When the sky is rented asunder: “Iza alsamaa’u an shaqqat”: (Inshiqaq: 86: 1).
That was for that eye which the clay opened.

sections.heading: God Alters Qualities of Elements:
paras: Mud being mixed in muddy water, upon filtration settles down at the bottom as residue under water. That is the quality of mud, one of the two of the four fundamental elements that goes down, because of its heaviness( so also water); as against the two other elements: fire and air that go up because of being light in weight. But look at the mud of H.Muhammad, it went high up very swiftly even beyond the heavens. (This reference is to the incident of the ascension, Mi’raaj). In this case you may note that this subtlety was not of mud and water (of which man is made). It was nothing but the special grant of God that became so light in weight. (rather, had no weight at all). If God makes the light elements, air and fire that go upwards, and bring down as heavy elements; and increase the worth of thorns against flowers, there is nothing to wonder at, because He is the King and commander as God does what He wills: “Yaf ‘alu Allaha maa yashaa’u”: (Ibrahim: 14: 27)

God does what He wills: “Yaf‘alul laahu maa yashaa‘u”: (Ibrahim 14: 27). He makes medicine out of sickness. If He makes the heavy elements − mud and water light in weight to go up, He would make them pass through the paths of heavens. And if He makes the light elements – air and fire to go heavy in weight, He would make them dark, heavy and residual. None dare ask: 'why'. Many hard-hearted persons have found no answer to this question and miserably failed in this path. This question makes it certain: ‘You exalt and honor whoever You will’: “Tu’izzu man tashaaa’u”: (Al-imran 3: 26). He told the earthly creature to open its wings, and it opened. He told the fire: ‘Go and become Iblees and be treacherous up to the seventh layer of the earth, it became". He told the material clayish heavyweight body of man to go up on the sky; and told fiery weightless Iblees to go down to the earth.

sections.heading: God’s Absolute Powers
paras: He said: "I am not of the four elements and not the first cause (as some philosophers say). I am the One to have control of everything forever. My job is straight and without cause. You are sick of mind. Whatever I do is according to My power. It does not require any cause other than My intention. It is only man who needs a cause to bring about. It is wrong to say that I created the first intelligence and it does everything and I do not have a job now to perform and everything goes according to the command of the first intelligence. According to My wish, I change the normal course of action and remove the overshadowing dust upon them. I make an ocean become full of fire and make fire of a garden. I make a mountain become lightweight like corded wool. I make the sky come down in the eyes of everyone. I make the sun mingle with the moon and make both of them go dark like a cloud. ‘When the sun is overthrown’: “Izash shamsu kuwwirat”: (At-takwir: 81: 1). I make the fountains of the forces of the light of the sun to go dry. I make a fount of blood to become musk (as in the case of certain deers). I not only change the qualities of the things but even their very substance. I make the sun and the moon become like two black oxen tied together by the yoke on their necks.

A reciter of the Quran was reading the ayat: “Say, have you thought: if all your water were to disappear into the earth, who could then bring you gushing water?”: “Qul ara’aytum in asbaha maa’ukum ghowran faman ya’teekum bimaa’in ma‘een”: (Al-mulk: 67: 30). That is, if I sink water into the depths of the earth, dry up the fountains and convert them into the desert, who else can bring water into the fountains other than the Unmatchable, Excellent and Great like Me?

A lowly rationalist philosopher was passing by the school. When he heard this verse of the Quran, he said: 'We shall extract water with the pickaxes. With the help of fast-moving spades and pokers, we shall drag the water upward”.

sections.heading: Repentance: No Fortune of All:
paras: At night he went into sleep and saw in the dream that a strong man punched him on his face and blinded both his eyes and told him: 'O hard-hearted fellow, if you are true, bring out light into the fountains of your eyes with the help of pokers’. When day arrived, he found his eyes blinded. He did not find the light in his eyes. Had he wept and repented, he could have got back his sight with God’s blessings. But repentance is also not in everyone’s fate. The taste of repentance is not the snack of everyone drinking wine. Wrong acts and determined misfortune of rejection had shut the door of repentance upon him. His heart had become hard like a rock and as such, there was no scope for clefting it with repentance to make it worthy of farming just as a rocky land had become worthy of farming upon the supplication of H. Shu’aib. Where is such Shu’aib now with whose prayer a rocky bed would become a farmland. With his humility and faith in God, H. Ibrahim had made possible a difficult and impossible task. Or (to give another example), as upon the request of Muqwaqas (king of Abyssinia), with the prayer of the Prophet Mohammad, a barren rocky land had become fertile.

sections.heading: Repentance: Not Mere Words:
paras: As against this a man’s rejection of truth brings about adverse results. It turns gold into copper and peace into war. Callings of disbelief distort things and convert fertile land into rocky infertile. There is no provision that every heart should have an inclination towards submission to God. Every workman does not have a share of mercy along with his wages. Be careful never to commit wrongs and sins in the hope of pardon with repentance. Repentance requires the pains of a burnt heart and tears. It requires clouds of remorse and lightnings to be effective. Heat and water are required for fruit to ripen and these come about with clouds and lightnings. Until and unless heart provides the heat of lightning and both the eyes shed tears, the fire of anger and warnings does not go cold. Until the cloud does not wail and cry and cause rain through its tears, and the lightning laughs at it, the grass of the taste of meeting with the beloved does not grow and the streams of water do not flow. The garden will not speak of its secret to the varieties of flowers like banafsha (violet flower) and saman (white jasmine), they do not enjoy the friendship of each other. Chinar (tree found in the landscape of Kashmir) will not spread its hand-shaped leaves in supplication and the trees will not raise their heads and dance along with the blowing wind. The days of spring season will not shake off their sleeves full of flowers.

sections.heading: Impacts of Rain:
paras: The face of lilac, red like blood will not shine and the flowers will not spill out the gold-colored stamens from their corollas. Bulbul will not come near the flower to catch its fragrance. The dove will not cackle “koove-koove” like the lover. Water birds (Storks) will not utter “lak-lak” with their hearts and souls. (The word “lak” in Arabic means “Yours”, you may see “lak” as an address ‘for you’ to God). This is how the water birds express their thanks to God saying: “The entire world is yours” to God. How can the earth speak of its hidden secrets making the gardens bright like the sky? From where can the dresses of all trees, birds and others come about, other than from the merciful and generous God.

All these fineries as the exposition of the One are the symbols of the Great Lord, which support a searcher and worshiper of God to know Him better. Symbols please him very well, who has seen the Lord and for the one who has not seen Him, informations do not pass. The soul of the one, who has seen God at the time of ‘alastu bi rabbikum’ (Am I not your lord) gets intoxicated and forgets itself. [‘Alastu bi rabbikum’ (Am I not your lord) was the question by God to all the souls collected before Him. When they had all seen Him, they said: ‘Yes, You are’: “Qālu balaa”].

sections.heading: Signs and Symbols and Their Impacts:
paras: He only recognizes the fragrance of wine, who has already tasted it. The one who has not tasted it cannot know the worth of its fragrance. The noble Prophet has said: “Wisdom is the lost possession of the faithful; wherever he finds it, he takes it back”. It is a guide for the great men and kings. If you see a beautiful person in your dream who gives you some promise supported by some signs, telling you that your object will be achieved through a person who will come before you. One sign of that person is: he will come riding on a horse, another that he will hug you; then he will laugh before you, then again, he will stand before you with folded hands; he will also tell you that you will not be able to speak of this dream to anyone. Such were the signs that were told to H. Zakariah (Zacharius), father of H. Yahya (John), upon a condition that he should not communicate to anyone for three days except in signs.

sections.heading: Instruction Through a Dream:
paras: That beautiful person in your dream will further tell you that you shall not speak of this to any one for three days. This silence of yours is a further sign of the meeting of your object. He warns you: “Beware! You should not tell this to anyone and keep it as a guarded secret. If you keep this secret for three nights, your object will come to you just as H. Yahya was born to H. Zakariah”. He will tell you about further signs sweet like sugar; as many as hundred signs. This will be his further sign that you will get from God the rulership and status that you are craving for, for which you cry for the whole night and burn in this desire in all humility in the morning. Your desire is such that it has darkened your days and made your neck thin like the spokes of the spinning wheel. That is a thing for which you have sacrificed all your possessions, just as the noble people give away everything to the poor as charity.

Your possessions were given up, the charm of your face and pleasure of sleep lost, your head sacrificed, and you became thin like hair to achieve your object. You have burnt yourself in the fire like aloeswood and faced like a shield to meet the attacks of swords for so many times. You have undergone many such difficulties just as lovers face which cannot be counted.

sections.heading: Dream Comes True:
paras: And you saw in your dream what you have been craving for years and woke up in the morning with pleasure. You turned on the left and right side of yours to see those signs. You were trembling like a leaf fearing that the day may pass off and the sign may not appear. You were running about to see that in the streets, bazaars, and lodges like a person who has lost his heifer. People would ask you: “What is wrong with you, sir? Why are you running about like this? How are you related to what you are searching for?” You would say: “I am alright. My being alright is something which can be known to me alone and to no one else. If I tell one of the points I am running after, the whole thing would be lost and if that is lost, it means the time of death has arrived”.

You would look at the face of everyone on the horse. That man would tell you: “Do not look at me like a madman”. You tell him: “I have lost a friend. I am searching for him. O man on the horse, may your fortune be safe, have pity on the lovers. Consider them to be helpless!”

When you struggled so much, your object was visible. The noble Prophet has said: “Efforts do not go waste”. Suddenly a noble rider came before you and he hugged you with great enthusiasm. You became unconscious and fell down on the road. A stranger said: “This is treachery and hypocrisy”. How could that man know as to what was behind this happening? He could not know as to what was the sign of this meeting. This sign is for him alone, who knows its object. How can this sign be important for others? As and when the desiring person sees a sign, he gets into a new life. Water came before a helpless fish and the fish thought that this sign is as true as the ayat of the Quran: “They are the symbols of the perspicuous book”: “Tilka aayaatul kitaabil mubeen” (Yusuf: 12: 1).

sections.heading: Uncountable Symbols of the Prophets
paras: These symbols are those that are in the prophets. These are understood by those who are aware of the matters. There are so many symbols in the prophets that I am not capable of explaining. They are innumerable. As I cannot tell all that, consider me to be helpless and disabled. Who can count the particles? And in particular, the fellow whose wisdom has been overtaken by love. Can I count the leaves of the trees of the garden? Can I count the crying tunes of the chakores and the crows? These cannot be counted; but I can speak of a few of them for the sake of one curious about them. The ill-effects of Saturn and the good impacts of Jupiter also cannot be counted even if you put great efforts to count them. But a part of the impacts of these two ought to be explained to the people to know their gain and loss, so that they may know of the fate caused by God. Some to those who are fortunate and to some others who are in distress. One under the impact of Jupiter will be happy with success and honor. One under the influence of Saturn will be a victim of all kinds of troubles. He requires to be very cautious in his dealings. If I do not warn him of his dangers, he will be burnt out under its influence.

sections.heading: Fate Caused by God, Not Stars:
paras: Stop all this discourse! What all you are talking is nonsense. It is not proper to speak of the signs of God’s essence. Lest a part of the sun’s radiance may not flash all of a sudden. Uncountable stars in the boundaryless space do not either have power or light or any signs, which would cause any effect. Do not engage yourself in these discussions. Stars have no role to play in anybody’s life. Everything is dependent upon God’s wish. Engage yourself in things which have sure consequences. Motions of the stars are like those of sick persons who move with the support of others. They are entirely caused by that benevolent and merciful God. Engage yourself in the thoughts of God, which He has permitted to do even though we are not fully aware of His greatness and grandeur. Yet, He has permitted to do this as He has seen us in the fire of ignorance and as such given us some light of wisdom to see Him.

sections.heading: Comparisons with God Are Defective, yet Needed:
paras: He has said: Though I am absolutely unconcerned about your understanding Me or praising Me, yet I speak of some signs from the material world as my signs, as you are capable of seeing and understanding them to some extent. Signs and examples are fit to be referred to Me. Humble creatures cannot understand anything other than through examples and projections of ideas through imaginary pictures. They are accustomed and habituated to this system. They cannot understand Our essence without the help of physical examples, even though these examples speak in no way of Our essence, which is absolutely devoid of material concern. Thinking of physical powers is defective as they cannot speak fully of Our might, but only as comparisons in view of man’s weakness. It is as uncomparable and defective as saying that, a king is not a weaver. There is no comparison between the king and the weaver. This cannot be a praise for the king. So also, any comparison of anything with God is defective. Yet God should be praised in whatever manner you can, as per your capacities.

While going on his way, H. Mūsā saw a shepherd who was telling: “O generous God! Where do You reside, so that I may attend to Your service? I may stitch shoes for You and comb the hair on Your head. If I know Your place, I can come and serve You and stitch your light and warm clothes. I may wash Your clothes and pick the lice from Your head; and O You honorable, I may offer You milk. And if You fall sick, I may attend to You and treat as a close relative would do. I may kiss Your hands and press Your feet and dress up the bed for You to sleep. O my God: I sacrifice for You my life, my entire family and house. If I get to know Your address, I shall bring milk and butter in the morning and in the evening; and also bread and pots of curd. I shall prepare food for You to eat both in the morning and night. I shall sacrifice all my sheep for You. I wail and cry in Your remembrance, my Lord”

sections.heading: Physical Attributes to God:
paras: In this manner, the shepherd was talking nonsense. H. Musa asked him as to whom he was addressing all this. He said: “I am talking to the One who has created us all and upon Whose command this earth and sky have come about.” H. Musa said; “Oh, your head has gone mad! It is so regrettable. By saying all this, you have ceased to be a Muslim and resorted to infidelity. What is this blabbering of yours? It is nonsense and infidelity. Stop all this and stuff cotton pad in your mouth. The foul smell of your mouth has fouled the entire world; your infidelity has turned the silken mantle of faith into a torne blanket. Slippers and shoes are required for you; they are not meant for the sun. If you do not stop this talk from your mouth, fire will come and burn the world. What you are telling is the smoke of the oncoming fire, which has made the life go black and the soul rejectable. When you know that God is the ruler, why do you have faith in nonsense and misbehaviour? Friendship of a fool is like enmity. God is not in need of such services you are talking about. You are speaking of what is needed by your maternal and paternal uncles. Bodily needs and requirements are not of the Lord of Grandeur and Grace. Milk is required by one who is in physical development. Footwear is for one who has the feet, but God does not have such qualities.

“It would also be wrong even if you say all this for such a servant of God about whom He has said: “I am he and he is Me”. About whom He also said: “I was sick and you did not visit Me; I was also sick with him, he alone was not sick; or he is the one who sees through Me and hears through Me, because he hears and sees only as per My wish. Further, talking with a special servant of God in indecent manner, renders the heart dead and the record of your actions become black”.

sections.heading: Inappropriate Names Cause Anger:
paras: If you call a man ‘Fatima’ (literally meaning on who rids one of milk), who was the daughter of the Prophet, a name of pride and honor for women), he will be so angry with you that, he will go after your life; because it is a feminine name, even though both men and women are of the same species. This is how even a man of noble character and good manners would react. The name ‘Fatima’ is appreciable and praiseworthy for women, but it causes a wound like that of a spear for men. Good hands and feet are praiseworthy possession for us, but for the absoluteness of God, it is a bad attribute. Because ‘He neither begets nor was He begotten’: “Lam yalid walam yulad”: (Ikhlas: 112: 3). He is the Creator of the begetter father and begotten son. Getting born (begotten) is the attribute of bodies; so also, of the begetter. Getting born and begotten belongs to this world of materials. They are both created and desirous of creation. The shepherd said: “O Musa! I stitch my mouth. You have caused my heart to burn in shame”. He tore his garment, took a long cold sigh, turned towards the desert and left off.

chapters.title: Prayers to God in Different Ways

paras: A revelation came from God to H.Mūsā: “You have separated My servant from Me. You came into this world to unite and not to separate. As far as possible, do not cause separation, as separation of the husband and wife through divorce, though permissible is considered as the most hateful thing in God’s view, as stated by the Prophet. We have made everyone on a particular character and given him particular jargons coming from his culture and country. Something is a praise in his view and a wrong in yours. It is honey for him and poison for you. Light in his view, is fire for you; rose for him is thorn for you. It is good for him, bad for you. We are far above cleanliness and uncleanliness and smartness and idleness. I have not issued commands to people to get any benefit from their obedience but in order to show benevolence to them. [Once the Prophet asked a maid as to where is God? She replied, ‘In the skies’. This answer by her was considered as a light of knowledge. The same answer by a scholar would amount to infidelity ― Qazi Sajjad Hussain]. Indians can praise in their language and jargons, so also the Sindhis. I do not become clean by the praises. I command them to do good acts so that they may become clean and scatterers of pearls.

sections.heading: Heart, Not Words, Speak Truth:
paras: We do not look at the apparent spoken words; We look at the inner conditions of the heart. We observe the heart if it is humble, even though the words may not reveal humbleness. Because heart is the substance(real), and words are only the accident (products of substance). Accidents of words are just the means to refer but heart being the real substance in the object of Ours. Words from the man’s mouth are just simple and common, out of usage and also refer to what is hidden in the heart; and also, trickery to mean something else than they plainly appear. I go, not after them, but I go after the real purport, concern and feelings of the heart. Therefore, do not go after words but develop real consonance with heart. Burn the fire of love in the heart and burn it to ash in deep thoughts and their explanation to your own self.

sections.heading: Love Needs No Formalities:
paras: “O Mūsā, those who look at formal behaviours are different from those, who have burnt their souls and marched on the path of the soul and God out of their love for Him. Lovers of God burn in fire every moment and have no relief. They are in a ruined state. Their commitments require to be ignored, just as no taxes are imposed on a ruined village. Do not hold them guilty if they say something wrong, just as you do not wash blood of a martyr. For martyrs, blood is better than water, as they are buried with it and blood sticken clothes without bathing them with water, as done in respect of others. Their mistakes are a hundred times better than the right actions of others. There is no practice of facing towards the Ka’ba for the one who is within the Ka’ba itself. One can perform salat facing in any direction. There is no regret for a swimmer to be without footwear when in water. Do not expect guidance from the intoxicated ones. Do not expect darning of clothes for those who have themselves torne them. The religion of love is entirely different from all other religions. God alone is the religion and faith of the lovers. Rubies do not need any official seal or marking on them. They express the quality on their own without any certificate. One in love does not feel sorrow in the ocean of sorrows”.

After this, God put in H.Mūsā’s heart such secrets which cannot be explained. Many points of wisdom and secrets were put into his heart which got mixed up with both actual observations and spoken words. There were some of such high-grade aspects that took away his senses at times; and at times brought him back to senses, as though he was in flight from the very beginning (azal) to the final end (abad); observing things that existed before him and would continue after him. There were matters relating the world of angels and of non-material substances (malakut). It will be foolishness on my part if I try to explain them, as their explanations are beyond the comprehension of wisdom and cannot be understood. If I speak of them, wisdom will be obliterated; and if I write, pens will split apart. And, if I try to explain some of them which can be comprehended, the explanation will go up for such long time as to end on the doomsday, yet will be just very little and incomplete. Therefore, I have shortened my tongue; and if you want to know, you may know about it within yourself.

sections.heading: God’s Displeasure Enthuses H. Mūsā:
paras: When H. Mūsā heard of this displeasure of God, he ran after that shepherd. He followed his footprints and raised the desert dust. The walking of a mad man is different from that of others. One step is as high as that of Rukh, (the legendary bird which picks up elephants and hippopotamuses and flies in the sky), and the other so touching to the ground as the steps of the elephant. At one time it goes high above raising its flag like tide and at another time moving on its belly like the fish. Sometimes he writes his affairs on sand or dust like the astrologer who draws lines and figures on dust or sand. Sometimes he stands erect in astonishment and sometimes he runs fast. Sometimes rolls on the ground like a ball hit by the bat.

At last, H. Mūsā found out the shepherd and said to him: “Be prosperous! Permission has come from God; do not search for any discipline and formalities. You may speak of whatever that comes out to your mouth. Your infidelity is your religion and your religion is the light of your soul. You are now in perfect peace, and because of you, there is another world of peace. This pardon for you has come from God Who does whatever He wishes; ‘God does whatever He wills’; “yaf ‘alul laahu maa yashaa”: (Ibrahim: 14: 27). Do not have any fear. Go and open your mouth in whatever manner you want”.

sections.heading: H.Musa’s Chastisement Elevated the Shepherd:
paras: The shepherd said: “O Mūsā! I have gone away from that stage. Now, I do not have the need to tell in words, I am now involved in the anxieties and concerns of the heart. I have passed beyond the Lote-tree (Sidrat al-Muntaha), to the extent of journey of hundreds of thousands of years in the seventh heaven. I have gone on a hundred thousand years journey on the other side. [The Sidrat al-Muntaha is the highest symbolic point of knowledge and bliss up to which any one, man and angel can reach. None can go beyond it, even Gabriel, the angel of all wisdom cannot go beyond it]. You whipped at the horse (of my thoughts and wisdom) and it changed its direction, took a high jump and passed beyond the heavens. May God convert our material world (Naasuut) into a world of God’s own presence (Laahuut). That is, (may we be raised from material and physical wisdom to the higher knowledge of spiritualism). It was all due to your courage and strength to speak to me of what you spoke. I am highly obliged to them. Now, my condition is beyond any explanation and demonstration. What I am telling now is not my condition and state, I am in a state which can be experienced but not explained.”

sections.heading: Man Cannot Praise God in Full:
paras: What image of yours that you see in the mirror is you alone. It is not the image of the mirrors. One who blows air into the flute does not do so according to his strength, but according to flute’s capacity to bear. God can praise Himself according to His greatness, but we do not have the capacity even to hear that much. What all praises we make are like those of the shepherd. Your praising is quite good from your point of view, but it is defective from God’s point of view. It would be better if instead of words of praise, you have burning emotions of His love and greater passions for His gnosis. When the curtains between you and Him are lifted on the doomsday, you will know that, He is not what you had understood Him to be. Your praises for him are of no worth as they are defective. Yet, He accepts them due to His generosity, just as accepting the salat of a woman in her periods, even though she is exempted from it. Her salat is mingled with her blood; and your thoughts of God are based on similarities and comparisons of the One who is absolutely uncomparable. Blood can be washed with water and the body can be cleansed, but there is such uncleanliness in your inside which cannot be cleansed, otherthan by the water of grace of God. In prostration man say: “Subhana rabbiyal-A‘laa”: “My Great Lord is beyond praise.” That is to say: “O God! My prostration is unworthy of being offered. Offering it to You an unworthy thing is wrong; but You are such as to change the wrong into good: “Yubad dilul laahu saiyi aatihim hasanaat”: ‘Allah will change the evil of such persons into good’ (Furqan: 25: 70). Man says; O God, my prostration, like my existence itself is unworthy. But You may give me good in place of my evil.

sections.heading: God Accepts Bad and Makes It Good:
paras: The world itself is under the impact of God’s tolerant and liberal attitude that He removes the dirt and produces flowers in its place. The manure that we give to the plants is dirty and foul. This is accepted and, in its place, fragrant flowers come about. The unbeliever sees on the doomsday that he was lesser in worth and more empty handed than mud in the matter of granting and generosity. His life did not bring any flowers and fruits. He has done nothing other than polluting the clean things. He says: I have walked on the wrong path, as the Quran says: And the unbeliever shall say: “Woe onto me! I may as well be (mere) dust”. “ya qoolul-kaafiru yaa lai tanee kuntu turaaba”: (Nabaa: 78: 40)

sections.heading: Man’s Evolution from Mud:
paras: How good it would have been if I had not performed the journey and evolved from the level of mud. I would have returned bad things with good just as mud does. The real nature of a person gets exposed when he is on journey. My journey has tested and exposed my real nature and I got no good results from it. Man’s inclination towards the mud is only because he sees nothing good in progress. His case is like that of grass which when lively progresses upward, but when it is exhausted it bends down towards the earth. His desire to go back to earth is due to his greed, as he finds nothing material for him from that world on the doomsday. There is no sincerity and humility in his desire. Green grass rises up and has a desire to rise and rises above as it sees progress, life and beauty in elevation. But as the unbeliever has inclination towards the earth, he is under deficiency, dryness, loss and decadence.

When the inclination of your soul is towards the higher world of spirits, this inclination itself becomes a cause of your progress and takes you above. On the contrary when your head is looking down towards earth, you are sure to be one that sets like the star, moon or sun. Certainly, God does not love things which set: God said: I love not those that set: “laa uhibbul aafileen”: (An‘aam: 6: 76)

H.Mūsā said: “O generous God, the doer of all acts. The One, thinking about whom for a moment is equal to a lifelong thought! I have seen so many crisscrossing things in this world of water and mud that I also felt like raising objections on them just as the angels had raised: as to why a particular thing is made and seeds of mischief are sowed in it. Why there is raising of the fire of cruelties and rioting, which sets afire those simple souls engaged in prayers and worship in their masjids. Blood and pus are spilled and set to flow for the sake of pleasure. With full confidence I believe: there are certainly reasons behind all these, but I desire to see actually those reasons. My confidence tells me to keep quiet, but my sense of seeing insists that I should demand an answer.

“You have exposed your secret to the angels that such objections are purposeful for the reason that only after such piercing questions that the taste of honey-like sweetness can be found. You exposed knowledge to H. Adam in all clarity and eliminated the doubts of the angels about him, by showing to them his capacity to bear the burden of such great knowledge which none else could bear.”

sections.heading: Systematic Hard Work Brings Good Results:
paras: The answer to these points come to H.Musa: “Your final end in death will reveal to you the secret behind death. Fruits speak of the secret of leaves that they protect them from various seasons and bring them up. The secret of blood and semen is the resultant beauty of man. Imperfection is the beginning of every perfect thing. A child, who does not know anything, first wipes off the slate of the earlier writings on it and after that he starts writing. Those in search of truth, first undergo many troubles so as to burn their blood and only after these troubles, hidden secrets are revealed to them. At the time of the wiping off of the earlier writing on the slate itself, it should be realized that whatever is to be written thereafter becomes a lengthy record. The first thing that is done to build a new house is to dig up the foundation. In order to get water in the end, the first act is to dig the earth in depth. Children cry loudly to avoid the syringe for bloodletting, as they are unaware of the benefits behind it; their fathers give money for this service of cupping, as though rewarding a blood sucker.

sections.heading: Struggle for Existence:
paras: Coolies run after to lift heavy loads to snatch the lifting job from other coolies. Think over the struggles of the lifters of heavy loads to snatch from others. Each one wants to take that job. Similar is the struggle of the men of faith to reap benefits from their struggles. Thus, undertaking the burdens is the foundation of getting benefits. Similarly, bitterness is the beginning of the receipt of gains. Paradise is surrounded by unpleasant things and hell by pleasant things. The wealth of your fire is a wet green branch of tree, which is dried to make fire; and to extinguish the fire, you again pour water on it. The tortures of prison are a consequence of the pleasures and enjoyments of the demands of the body. The one who is sitting in the palace as a king is because of his undergoing the troubles of warfare and hard struggles. Whoever is lolling in gold and silver is because of his constant and patient hard work. This is how whatever results are achieved, are due to causes connected with them.

sections.heading: Non-Physical Causes:
paras: As you are entangled in the connections of cause and effect, you have no alternative than to stick on to this. But when someone passes beyond the limits of cause and effect, he sees many things as without causes. Only one who goes beyond the physical matters, can have a place of not bothering about causes. He looks at water and grass having come without causes, just as there are plenty of miracles of the prophets. He considers everything as due to God’s will and power, unbounded by causes. Causes are like the relationship between the body and the sickness. They are like connection between the lamp and the wick. When you are at this level of thinking, you should prepare the wick for the night, when there will be no sunlight. Prepare the roofing for the roof of your house; and be sure that the roof of the sky does not need such roofing. When our beloved puts an end to our sorrows, there is no worry about the loneliness in the night. The day is right before us. Search for the moon only at night, and the beloved through the pangs of love. But you have given up H. Īsā’s wisdom and opted for the donkey’s foolishness and therefore, your place is outside the tent.

sections.heading: Desirous Self Is a Donkey:
paras: H.Īsā’s possession is wisdom and knowledge which are the virtues of the soul and not of the body, and they do not belong to the donkey, and you are of the donkey’s type. Following the desires of the body is the only possession of the donkey, which is also in you, like the desires of yourself. You feel pity on this donkey’s (self’s) braying and respond to it and fulfill the desires, without knowing that this response is a donkish character. You should respond to the call of the wisdom of H. Īsā in you and not to the donkey’s.

Do not make your vicious self as your leader. Ignore it and allow it to cry. Collect the taxes from it like a king and pay the debts of your wisdom. You have followed the donkey for years together. Put an end to it and see that, as against other animals, the master walks behind the donkey like its servant. The Prophet had said: ‘Keep them (women) behind you, because God has kept them behind as followers.’ Consider the one to be behind you as your desiring self, as it requires to be kept behind and wisdom and intellect must be in front.

sections.heading: Lowly Wisdom; a Donkey:
paras: This lowly wisdom has become the donkey. It has no botheration for anything other than fodder. But H. Īsā’s donkey got into the possession of heart and acquired the place of the wise, as it kept the wisdom in front and its donkish desires behind, which had become weaker under the impact of wisdom. It should be known that the donkey becomes weaker when rided upon by a bulky man. But your donkey has become stronger due to the weakness of your wisdom; and your half-dead donkey has become stronger like a python. If you are heart-broken because of the deficiency of wisdom in you, go after H. Īsā’s wisdom, or your master’s wisdom. This will be of great worth to fill up the deficiency.

“O Mūsā! How are you in your connections with the Jews? O Yusuf! How are you in your connections with the jealousies of your brothers? Both of you have suffered at their hands in spite of your efforts to benefit them”. Similarly, a master devotes days and nights to set right his disciples and grants them a fresh life. What a tragedy for those of the imbalanced bile in their bodies who are always sick with headache. Imbalanced bile does not create any scope for improvement. Yet the master ought to do what the sun does; that it sheds its light on every good and bad person.

sections.heading: Address to the Master:
paras: O Master! Even if your disciples are hypocrites, pretenders, thieves and treacherous, you are like honey in the affairs of this and that world and we are like vinegar. The compound of honey and vinegar is the treatment for bile imbalance. We, suffering from dysentery have increased our vinegar and you may be kind to us by increasing honey. Our bitterness has to be cured by your sweetness. We are capable of doing only the wrongs that we have done. We have put dust into our eyes which can only blind us. But O Master! You are like the eye-black which causes brightness of eyes. You are capable of making a worthless thing worthy. These cruel fellows have caused fire to your heart, but your answer to them is to pray to God; “O God! guide my community,” as the noble Prophet used to say.

You are like aloeswood(agar). You can spread pleasing fragrance into the whole world when put into fire. You are not that agar, which would decrease in quantity upon burning. You are not that soul that would become a prisoner of sorrows. The agar may burn out, but its source does not. Wind cannot put out the truth of light. You are the one who cleaned the heavens. You are the one whose cruelty is better than grace. Chastisements of the wise are better than praises of the foolish. The wise brings out knowledge from the inside (heart), whereas an ignorant only speaks out from his mouth. The noble Prophet has said; “Enmity of the wise is better than the love of the ignorant.” Friendship with the wise is very good. Wise enemy is better that a foolish friend.

chapters.title: Beatings of the Wise Are Mercy

paras: A wise man was going on his horse and he saw a snake entering in to the mouth of a man in sleep. He looked at this, and ran to scare away the snake, to save the man from this situation, but he was not in time and the snake went inside. As he had much support from his wisdom, he made hard hittings on the sleeping man. The sleeping man woke up from his deep sleep, and found a Turk cavalier whipping him. He went on severely whipping him and the man started running to save himself. The strong whippings made him fully conscious and anxious as to why he was being whipped. He ran faster and went under an apple tree and there were many rotten apples which had dropped from the tree. The cavalier told him to eat them and compelled him to eat so many apples that they started coming out of his mouth.

The beaten man shouted at the cavalier: “O Master, what is this? Why do you intend to take my life for none of my mistakes? If you want to take my life, take it instantly with a sword and finish me off. It was a very inauspicious time when I came before your sight. He is very fortunate who never saw your face. Without any reason and mistake even, the infidels do not consider this cruelty permissible to continuously beat someone like this: no less, no more. Blood is pouring out of my mouth while I am talking. O God, take revenge of this!”

Every moment he was making such protests, and the cavalier went on whipping him and telling him to run into the forest. With the pain of the whips at the hands of the horseman running fast like the wind, he ran faster and fell down. He was feeling giddy with the stomach full and tired and there were hundreds of wounds on his face and legs. This went on for the whole night and ultimately, he started vomiting bile with rotten apples. All the things he had eaten, good and bad, came out and along with this the snake too. When he saw the snake coming out of his stomach, he fell down before the horseman in thanks. The fear of that black, rough, thick snake put an end to all the pains he was undergoing and he said: “You are like an angel full of mercy or my master and protector. What a prosperous moment was that when I happened to see you: I was dead and you have given me a new life. You are my caretaker like a mother and I was running away from you like a foolish donkey. The donkey runs away from its master because of its foolishness, when actually his master is after it in its own interest. He does not search for it in loss or gain but only to see that it is not torne off by a wolf or some other animal.

“How prosperous is that face which looks at you or which comes into your street all at once. My entire life is engaged in your praise, but earlier I said many senseless and meaningless things about you! O my king, my master and leader, what all was told was not by me but by my ignorance. Please do not hold me responsible for that. Even if I had known a little of what happened, I would not have blabbered all that. I would have praised you very much gentleman, if you had given a little hint of why you did. By your silence, you were causing anxiety to me and silently hitting me on my head. My head went out of my control and my wisdom vanished, in particular, this head of mine, which has a small brain. Pardon me, O beautiful one of face and good manners: and forget all that I said to you in my madness.”

sections.heading: Where Ignorance Is Better:
paras: The horseman said: “Were I were to say even a little of the reason for my acts, your gall bladder would have melted into water. If I were to tell you about the snake, fear would have caused death instantly”. H. Muhammad Mustafā has said: “If I clearly tell you about your enemy that is hidden in you, the gall-bladders of the brave amongst you would tear into pieces. Nobody would walk on the street and think about any job. He would neither have the heart to go humble, nor the body to have the strength to perform salat and fasting. He would become good for nothing as a rat before the cat or would run away from the site of the wolf like a lamb. Nobody would have any program, nor any action. This is how I took care of you without telling you certain things about the tricks and designs of the devils.”

Similarly, I (Rumi) also kept my mouth shut like Abubakr Rabaabi, who did not speak for seven years. I attend to the hardwork of a blacksmith just like H. Dawood did with iron, so that, what is considered as impossible may become possible at my hand, so that feathers may come on the body of the bird that has not been provided with them. Yet I say: when the hand of God came above the hands of the companions of the Prophet, as stated in the Quran: “The hand of God is over their hands”: “yadullaahi fawqa aydeehim”: (Fath: 48: 10). (This refers to the occasion when the Prophet had kept his hand upon the combined hands of his companions seeking affiliation). God made his hand long enough so that it went up to the seventh heaven. His hand showed its capacity to the sky and the result was the splitting of the moon as stated in the Quran: “and the moon is cleft asunder”: “wan shaqqal qamar”: (Qamar: 54: 1). Even this much has been said to meet the requirement of the weak wisdom, as it is not proper to explain the divine nature’s functioning to those with lowly wisdom. You will come to know of these when you get up from your sleep. Let me stop at this, as God knows best.

The horseman continued: “If I were to tell you all that had happened, you would have died instantly. Neither you would have had the strength to eat, nor the scope for vomiting. I was hearing all the unpalatable things you were telling me and carried on my job and silently telling under my lips: ‘God will solve the problem’. Speaking of the reasons is not in my habit. It was not within my powers to leave you to your fate. From my internal pains, I was continuously telling: ‘O God, guide my community as they do not know’. This prayer was made by the Prophet when he was severely troubled by his enemies from Taif.

That person saved by the horseman fell before him saying: “O prosperous one! The wealth of my fortune! You will get a great reward from God. This weak person has no strength to express his thanks. God will be thankful to you in my place, O leader! I do not have the required lips and cheeks and means to express thanks. The enmity of the wise is always like this, their poison is a cause of relief to the soul. Friendship with the fool is sorrowful and misguidance. For this purpose, you may hear this story.
A python was dragging a bear in to its mouth, when a brave man responded to the bear’s cries and rendered help.

sections.heading: Conduct of the Brave:
paras: Brave men in the world are supporters of the oppressed when they hear their cries. From whatever place they hear the calls of the oppressed, they run toward them like the mercy of God. They act like pillars to the falling roofs of houses and as physicians for hidden sicknesses. They are love, justice and benevolence in entirety and work without reward and bribe just like God. If you ask a brave man as to why he goes to the help of others, he will say that it is in response to the pain and helplessness of the victim. Gracefulness is the game of the brave. It is only due to pain that one goes in search of medicines. And whenever consumed, the medicine reaches the spot of pain. Materials of need go to the place where there is need. Water goes to the lower levels. It is only upon asking that an answer comes out. These are unusual matters.

sections.heading: Need: Prior to Achievement:
paras: Therefore, you should not search for water but create thirst within you so that water may gush forth from above and below to quench your thirst as God has said: “And then Lord will slake their thirst with pure drink”: “wa saqaahum rabbuhum sharaaban tahooran”: (Dahr: 76: 21). Therefore, thirst is the prerequisite. And God knows best.

As water gets to lower level, you may become lowly to get it and then you may drink the wine of mercy and get intoxicated. But do not remain content with one source of mercy and go continuingly for more and more, in search of more and more. Bring down the sky under your feet, O brave man, and hear the music of the heavens. Remove the cotton, producing insinuations from your ears, so that the sounds of the heavens may be heard by them in clear manner. Remove the fallen hair of defects from both of your outer and inner eyes so that you may see the invisible gardens and cypress trees. Remove the impacts of common cold from your nose and coolness of mind, so that godly fragrance may enter into your nose. Do not allow the impacts of the fever caused by bile malfunction so that you may enjoy the sweetness of the other world. Get done the treatment for impotence and become a potent man, so that you may be a father of a hundred beautiful children. Remove the shackles of the body form the feet of the soul, so that it may roam about in the gardens of the next life. Remove the chains of miserliness form the hands and necks so that you may find new fortunes from the old heaven. If you cannot go to a worthy master, go toward a center of benevolence like the Ka’aba, and place your deficiencies.

sections.heading: Mercy Searches the Needy:
paras: Helplessness and cryings are a great capital to attract total mercy as great as a wet-nurse for the child. Wet-nurses and mothers are always in search of the child’s cries to attend to him. God has created children, in the form of your needs so that they may cry and the milk of kindness flow out. God has said: ‘say: call upon God, or call upon Rahman: “qulid’ul laaha awid’ur Rahmaana”: (Asra: 17: 110) so that the milk of His grace may flow forth in full. Have patience! Clouds full of milk are in full readiness to fall on us. Have you not heard that your provisions are in the sky as stated in the Quran: ‘and in heaven is your sustenance, as (also) that which you are promised’: “wa fissamaaa’i rizqukum wa maa too‘adoona”: (Zariyat: 51: 22). Such being the case, why do you attach yourself entirely to the affairs of the world. The fear that engagement in godly affairs will cause poverty is a devilish insinuation, as stated by God: ‘The evil one threatens you with poverty’: “Ash Shaitaanu ya’idukumul faqra”: (Al Baqarah: 2: 268). Consider your fear and doubts to be the voice of that treacherous fellow that go deep into ears.

sections.heading: Upper World: Not in Position or Spatial Sense, but Quality Wise:
paras: Every sound that calls you towards the upper world may be taken as one coming from there. And consider the sound that creates the worldly greeds, as from the wolf which tears up humans. The upper world is upper, not in the spatial sense but in the sense of wisdom and soul. A cause is above the effect. Stone and iron are above the spark, as they are the cause of spark. They are not above in the spatial sense. One person is considered to be above another, even if they both are sitting together in the same place. The above level is in respect of the status even if he is away from the authority. Stone and iron are superior by way of their priority in action in togetherness to spark, but both are equal to each other. Yet, sparks are superior to them from the point of view of the object, because the purpose of their togetherness is the spark. And, in another aspect stones are physical bodies but sparks are life and soul of both.

In respect of time, sparks are later and behind iron and stone, yet in their quality they are above iron and stone. Branch of a tree is prior to the fruit in time, but, in respect of worth, fruit that comes later, is superior. And as the object of the tree is fruit, the fruit comes in front of the tree.

sections.heading: No Victory Without Strategy:
paras: Now, we turn towards the bear and the python, as the discussions on the things hidden in the heart (latent) and of the bodies (patent) are very long and elaborate. When the bear started crying and shrieking in the grip of the python, the brave man rid it of the python’s grip. His methods and courage helped him in his efforts and he killed the python. He caught hold of the python in such a way that the bear was released, and physically saved. Python had a great strength but had no strategy and strategy provides victory. But you should not be proud of your strategy, as there is another strategy more worthy than yours. There are many strategists who hide themselves in their traps to catch their victims. But you may be careful about God, who is the best of strategists: “wallahu hairul maakireen”: (Al-Imran: 3: 54). When you look at your own strategy, return to it and find out from where it has come and look at its starting point.

sections.heading: Light of Wisdom from the Upper World:
paras: Whatever that has come into this lowly world has come from the upper world. Therefore, look at the source of coming at the upper level and not at what has come about in the lower world. Looking at the upper world gives light to your sight, though at initial levels it remains as darkness. Develop the habit of looking at light and be not like the bat, which does not look at light. Looking at the ultimate end of acts and things is an evidence of your light, your farsight and insight. And following carnal desires is a curtain for them. Your master has seen hundreds of such ultimate ends. He is not like the one who has just seen one. The one who sees only one is so flabbergasted at the sight that he becomes proud of it and keeps himself away from the master out of arrogance and pride. This is the case of Saamiri, who saw a little light within himself after learning it form H. Mūsā, but became arrogant and disobedient to him. He had learnt the art from H. Musa and shut his eyes from him. As such, H. Mūsā showed another art which took away his life. [Saamiri was an Isrealite, who took a little mud from the hooves of the horse of an angel, which would bring out green grass under its steps. He made a model of calf out of gold and silver and put the mud in it, as a result of which this calf would mimic like a live heifer. Projecting this as miracle he made people worship it, when H. Musa had gone away to the mount, and started challenging him. As a consequence of this, H. Musa cursed him that his body would become unbearably hot upon going closer to anyone. He told the people not to touch him. (He remaining untouchable could also be due to his arrogance and holding others at arm’s length ― Abdullah Yusuf Ali: The Holy Quran: page 810)

sections.heading: Do Not Betray Masters:
paras: Much of the wisdom comes into the brain in order to gain leadership, but in fact, causes the loss of the head itself. If you do not want to lose your head, you should become lowly and go under the guidance and protection of a high-level master (Qutub). Do not consider yourself to be above the master, howsoever higher you may go, and even become a king. You may become as valuable and sweet as honey, but do not ignore the sweetness given by the master. Your thoughts are just imagined pictures, but his thoughts are life and soul. Your gold is impure and he is a gold mine. Of course, you have your own existence, yet search for yourself in his existence. Become like a dove which says, ‘koov, koov’ in search of its beloved, which in man’s language (Persian) means: “where is he? Where is he?”

sections.heading: Seek Help When in Need:
paras: If you do not render service to your fellow human beings, your position is like that of the bear in the python’s mouth. If the sweetness of the thanks of the fellow humans appears bitter to you, it means that you are as incapable as the bear in the python’s mouth. If you have an efficient master, you can get rid of such compulsions and taken away from dangers by the master. You should pray humbly to God when you need support, to provide a supporter in the form of a master, as you are blind and need someone to guide you. But you are much lesser than the bear, as you do not have even the capacity to cry to seek the help of others. Because the bear cried for help, it got help of that brave man and saved itself.
You should know that your master will pray to God to soften your stony heart, soft like wax, and teach it to cry, and make your cries prosperous and cause of mercy.
A blind beggar was telling: “May God help me, I am twice blind, O people of the world, have two times pity on me as I have two kinds of blindness, and I am between them.”
People asked him in surprise: “Do not talk in puzzles. Tell us clearly, as to what you mean by two times blindness; because, one blindness of yours, we see, and we do not see the other blindness”.

The blind man said: “I have a very rough tone which is highly repulsive, and this is my second blindness. My rough voice becomes a capital of my sorrows. Because of my repulsive voice people’s sympathy for me gets reduced. Wherever my bad voice goes, it creates anger, resentment and hatred for me. Therefore, have two times pity on me for my two blindnesses, and make this non-possessive fellow a possessive one.”

With such heart-felt pleading of this fellow, the repulsiveness of his voice was reduced and the people found sympathy for him. The revelation of his secret made his defective voice appear good to the people. It was the voice of his heart that made the voice of his mouth better. If his heart’s voice also happened to be bad, the person would be thrice blind. This will be long standing blindness.

sections.heading: Vicious Heart; Hidden Blindness:
paras: With the first two apparent blindnesses, if there is no blindness of the third type, that is, he has a good heart, generous people who give without any expectation may be inclined to keep their hand of affection upon his head. Since the man’s voice lost its viciousness, it became such a cause of sympathy that even hard-hearted became soft like wax. As the lamentation of the infidel is coarse, like braying of a donkey which is very loud at the start and mild at the end, it fails to attract sympathizers. The statement from the Quran: go away therein, and do not speak to me: “akh sa’uu fiihaa wa laa tukallimuun”: (Al-Mu’minun: 23: 108) has come for such voice, because it is like a dog inebriated with the blood of the people. This will be told to them by God when they cry out to get out of hell.

As the cries of the bear became a cause of mercy, your cries should not be such as to cause repulsion. This treatment will be shown to you for your showing wolfishness to innocent men like H. Yusuf for drinking their blood. That is to say, you have trampled upon the rights that you had upon yourself and upon other creatures of God. Therefore, repent on your vicious acts and vomit what all you have swallowed. And, if your wound is very old, go for its cauterising by burning. O old fox, give up your foxiness and seek help from God as: He is the best to protect and the best to help: “ni‘mal mawlaa wa ni‘man nasiir”: (Anfal: 8: 40).

When the bear was released from the grip of python, and it looked at the brave grace of the man, it became his close friend like the dog of the companions of kahaf. The gentleman out of tiredness, laid on the ground and the bear, with all concern, became his guard. Another person passed that way and enquired about his health and his connections with the bear. The former narrated the matter relating to the python. Hearing this that person said: “O foolish man! Do not develop the company of a bear. A fool’s friendship is worse than enmity. The bear is fit to be chased by every means you know.” The former said: “You say this out of jealousy. Why should you look at the bear, look at its concern for me?”

sections.heading: Misfortune Blocks Wisdom:
paras: The latter said: “Foolish people’s love results only in misery. My jealousy is better than its love. Take care! Come with me and chase away the bear. Do not prefer the bear to me, develop connection with one of the same species.”
The former said: “Go away you jealous fellow! Attend to your job.”

The latter said: “This alone was my job, which I have done. But what I did is not your fortune O good man, I cannot be lesser than the bear. Give it up so that I may be your friend. My heart shivers at the thought of your fate. Do not go with such bear into the forest. My heart does not shiver without reasons. What I am fearing of is due to God’s light in me. This is neither nonsense nor self-praise. I am a faithful person and I see things with the Light of God as the Prophet has said that the faithful see through the Light of God. Take care! And run away from this furnace full of fire.”

That person said all this, but it did not enter into the ears. Suspicion is a great block for man. The later adviser held his hand but the former pulled back his hand. Then the latter said: “I shall go away when the friend is determined not to straighten himself.”
The former replied: “Do go away! Do not be anxious about me. You are only a blabberer. Do not talk of gnosticism.”
The latter persisted: “I am not your enemy. I shall be much pleased if you follow me.”
The former said: “I am sleepy. Leave me off and, go!” The latter persisted: “Take the advice of a friend so that you may sleep under the protection of a wise man, and be nearby to him.”

sections.heading: Suspicions upon Well-Wishers:
paras: Upon this persistence, the former got into suspicions, got wild and turned his face away from him, thinking that he is after his life. Or he has some greed; or else, he is a beggar or thief. Or he has made a bet with his friends that he would separate me from my friend by causing fears in me. Or that he would frighten me. Or he is jealous of love from my friend, as otherwise, there is no need for him to take so much interest in my affairs.”

Because of his suspicion and ill-will, not a single good thought came to his mind. His entire good thinking was towards the bear. May be, he belonged to the same species as of the bear in character. He was suspicious, foolish and incapable. Because of his ill-luck he was of wrong temperament, arrogant, misguided, proud, mentally blind, mean, rejectable, and unfortunate. He preferred a bear to a well-natured man. He was black faced with bad thinking and bad results. Because of his doggish nature, he made accusations against a good man and considered the bear to be lovable and just.

sections.heading: Miracles Rejected:
paras: H.Mūsā said to a calf-worshiper: “O with unconscious thinking, misguided with misfortune and unguided! You had a hundred doubts about my prophethood. With such arguments and fineness of thoughts, while I was with you, you saw hundreds of thousands of miracles in me, yet hundreds of thoughts, doubts and suspicions arose in you. You were helpless before your thoughts and insinuations. You made so many taunts upon my prophethood.

“I raised dust from the sea floor and saved you all from the mischief of Pharaoh and his followers. For forty days there came vessels and plates of food from heaven. With my prayers, streams of water gushed forth from the rocks. A stick in my hand became a male python. Water turned into blood for my indecent enemy. A stick became a snake and my palm became as bright as the sun. With the reflection of my face the sun became a shooting star. O ill-witted fellow, these miracles and hundreds like them, did not wipe off your doubts.

sections.heading: Magic Accepted:
paras: “With the power of magic, the calf (made by Saamiri) made a sound, and you fell down in prostration saying, ‘you are my God’. All your suspicions were swept away by the flood. Your senseless smartness went to sleep. Why did you not have suspicion, in this matter? You, one with an ugly face! Why did you place your head before this? Why did you not think that this may be a trick played by Saamiri, and a mischief to trap the fools? O mean fellow, why did you not think as to what Saamiri was, so as to make a god in the world. When your heart was with him in this trickery, you got rid of all doubts and suspicions. How can a cow’s calf be fit to be god, when you did not agree with my prophethood? With your donkishness, you prostrated to the calf and your wisdom became a victim of Saamiri’s magic. You turned your eyes away from the light of the One of Majesty. This is a great ignorance and basic misguidance upon your wisdom and choice. You are a mine of ignorance requiring to be finished off.”

sections.heading: Foolish Taste of the Foolish:
paras: The golden calf said: “These are flowers of the taste of the fools. You have seen more mind-baffling events than me. But every mean fellow will not accept the truth. What appeals to the worthless fellows is worthlessness. What the useless fellows admire is uselessness. Because, every species attracts its own species. The cow does not go nearer to the male lion. The wolf cannot fall in love with H. Yusuf. It does not do anything other than swallowing him treacherously. When it gets rid of its wolfishness, it becomes friendly, just as the dog became man-like in the company of the Companions of Kahaf”.

sections.heading: Vicious Do Not See Nobility:
paras: When the noble and truthful H.Abū Bakr looked at the truthfulness of H.Muhammed, he spoke out: “He is truthful.” When he smelt the fragrance of H.Muhammed, he said: “This is not a face that lies.” but since Abū Jahl did not have anything in common with H.Muhammed, he looked at the miracle of the splitting of moon but he did not believe in him. The pains of a suffering person cannot remain unexposed how much ever he may try to hide. Yet an ignorant fellow could not see it even when we brought his pains to his notice. The mirror of the heart must be clear, in order that you may identify the ugly from the beautiful.

That wise person left the foolish man silently saying: “La howla” (there is no power except with God). When doubts become stronger with advice and persistence, it is better that speech and advice be put to an end. That is why there is the command in the Qurān: ‘Decline to interfere’: “aw a‘rid anhum”: (Maida: 5: 420). This becomes attributable to him. When your medicine increases the pain, stop administering it and turn towards the other patient as the instructions came to the Prophet in Surah ‘Abasa 5: 80 (he frowned) the substance of which is: “When a blind man came to the Prophet seeking the Truth at a time when the Prophet was engaged in persuading the pagan Quraish leaders, the Prophet disliked his interruption. The revelation came that he ought not to feel embarrassed at his poverty and deny instruction. ‘You are greedy for the instructions to the elevated people, so that the common people may learn their religion from the leaders. O Muhammad, you have seen that a group of leaders are ready to learn from you and you became happy thinking that they will become good supporters of the faith, as they were the lords from Arabia and Abyssinia, and that your message will reach beyond the cities of Tabuk and Basra, as the saying goes: ‘people follow the faith of the kings.’ For this reason, you turned away your face with displeasure from the blind man (Abdullah bin Ummi Maktum) seeking instructions. You thought that such occasion of meeting with the leaders comes very rarely; and there is plenty of time to meet your companions. You thought that the blind man came to you at the time, when it was very short and rare, and you turned away from giving advice for guidance and, not as resentment or quarrelsomeness.

sections.heading: Blind Seekers and Elevated Refuters:
paras: “O Muhammad, in the sight of God, this one blind man is better than hundreds of Caesars of Rome and their ministers. Remember that the common people are like mines (of gold) and each one of them, as a mine of greatness, is better than hundreds and thousands of such men-in-power. The hidden mine of rubies is better than a hundred thousand mines of copper. O Muhammad, wealth and gains are of no use in this matter. What is required is a breast full of love, its pangs and smoke. A blind man with a bright heart has come to you with full enthusiasm. Give instructions to him. He has a right to receive instructions. Two-three ill witted fellows refusing to learn from you cannot make you bitter as you are sugar mine. Two-three foolish fellows may make false accusations against you but God will stand as a witness against them.
[Up to this is an explanation of the subject matter of Surah ‘Abasa. The following lines refer to the substance of the Prophet’s sayings.]

sections.heading: Enemy Accepts Greatness by Hate:
paras: The Prophet said: “I am unconcerned with the acceptance or otherwise of the world. Why should one feel aggrieved in whose favour God stands as a witness. Bats are well known for the dislike of sun. As against this, if a bat receives its food from the sun, it means that it is not sun. A hundred of such bats give evidence to me of that fact that I am a bright sun of God. If a dung-eating worm turns towards the flower, it means that it is not a rose. If a counterfeit coin prepares itself to be tested by the touchstone, it means that the touchstone is defective. Know this, a thief goes at night and not at the day for stealing. He will not come after me as I am not a night but a bright day. I shine upon the world.

“I am a divider; I separate the flour like a sieve from the husk. Husk cannot pass through me. I separate the flour form husk to show as to what is really worthy. I separate men from their looks. I am like a balance of God and I distinguish between the heavy weight and light weight. Only a calf can consider an ox as God. One purchases a donkey to keep upon its back only what is worthy of being kept on it. I am not a cow that the calf would come to me and I am not a wild thorny plant that a camel would like to eat me. An incompetent person thinks he has done some harm to me but what he has done is only that he has removed the dust form my mirror”.

The great physician Galen asked his assistants to fetch a particular medicine for him. One of them said: “This medicine is used as a cure for madness. May God keep you away from madness. Do not seek this.”

Galen replied: “A madman’s eyes have fallen upon me. He looked at me for a while, winked at me, and tore my sleeve. Had there not been some similarity with him, why would that accursed fellow have cast his attention on me? He would not have come near me, if he did not find something common with himself in me. He would not have thought of dealing anything with me, if I were not like him. If two persons come together, it is certainly due to something common in between them. Every bird flies with one of its own flock. Living with one without commonness is like in a grave and sepulcher.

sections.heading: Commonness Brings Togetherness:
paras: A wise man said: “I saw a crow and a crane picking up together. I was taken by surprise and tried to know as to what was common between them. With all curiosity, when I went nearer to them, I found both of them to be lame.” The commonness between them was their lameness. Otherwise, there is no reason for birds or anybody of different species remaining together. And in particular, the falcon flying high in the sky cannot have any connection with the owl attached to earth.

One is the sun of ‘Illiyyiin’, that is: with a record of noble acts, at an elevated level, while the other is a bat whose record of ignoble acts, is at a low level (Sijjiin). One is light devoid of all defects, while the other is a blind beggar at every door. One is a moon connected with the Pleiades (a conspicuous star cluster in the constellation, Taurus), while the other is a worm circling around dung. One has the face of H. Yusuf and breath of H. Isa, while the other one is a wolf, donkey or bear. One is in flight upon Laamakaan (space beyond the space), while the other one is along the dustbin like dog. One is a highly elevated king, while the other one is mourning in furnace. One is so generous that people feel low before him, while the other one is full of shame due to destitution. One is a leader of the time; and the other is overlapped with dust.

sections.heading: Hate of Opponents:
paras: Garden is the proper place for bulbuls, and a dirty place is for the dung-worm. The flower with its body language is saying to the dung-worm that it is smelling foul: “You may run away from the garden, as your hate for the garden speaks of your imperfectness. My self-respect throws its spears on your head telling you to be far away from it. O mean fellow, if you remain closer to me, it will be presumed that you are of my family. I shall be at a loss in your company, as people will think that you belong to me. When God has created me in cleanliness, it is not proper for me to allow dirt to fall on me. The breast of the Prophet was operated upon to remove a bad vein and the same cannot come again.

sections.heading: Enemy’s Hate, Evidence of Greatness:
paras: It was one of the marks on H.Adam that he was to be prostrated by angels for his high grade. And another mark was that Satan should not prostrate to him as he was too far away from him. If the devil too had prostrated to H. Adam, he would not be H. Adam but someone else. Prostration by every angel was his standard and the refusal to do so by the enemy established his greatness. Acceptance of his greatness by the angels is evidence of his greatness. So also, the refusal of that dog, Ibliis. There is no end to this discussion. Let us go back to see what the bear did with that brave man.

That man went into sleep, and the bear flew away the flies hovering upon him, but the flies returned obstinately. He flew them off several times from the man’s face, but soon they came back again. The bear got angry with the flies and brought a hard, big stone from the hillock. It looked and found the flies had collected upon his face. It lifted that stone and hit upon the flies, in order that they might all go away. The stone made the sleeping man’s face as poppyseeds. And this became a famous example of foolishness all over the world that, “the friendship of a fool is like the friendship of the bear”.

sections.heading: Fool Is Unreliable:
paras: A fool’s love is enmity and his enmity is love. His promises are unreliable, destructive and weak; his words are hollow and his honesty suspectful. Even if he swears upon God, he should not be believed. Irresponsible fellow violates his promises. As his promise without swearing is false, you should not fall into his trap because of his swearing. His vicious self is dominant upon him, and his wisdom is its prisoner. Consider him to be one who has swallowed hundreds of thousands of holy books to commit breach of promises. As he is in the habit of breaking promises, he will do so even after taking oath, because with such breach of promises his self is already immune. He will not yield even to a strong promise. Because, if a prisoner puts handcuffs upon a master, the master will certainly break them and come out free. He will hit him with those handcuffs upon his face. You may take care of your promises and follow the God’s command: ‘Fulfill all obligations’: “awfoo bil’uqood” (Al-Maidah: 5: 1), and ‘keep your oaths’: “wahfazoo aimaanakum”: (Al-Maidah: 5: 89). Know that a faithful person knows as to with whom he is making an oath and makes his body as a rope with which he ties the promise.
One of the senior companions of the Prophet fell sick, and become thin like thread. H. Muhammad went to him to enquire about his health, as he was noble and was affectionate in his conduct.

sections.heading: Visit to a Sick Man Is Rewarding:
paras: Visiting a sick man is entirely for your own benefit as you only get its gains. The first benefit is that the sick man may be of very elevated spiritual state (Qutub) and grand like a king. As you do not have two eyes of the heart, you cannot consider aloeswood (agar) as more honourable than fire. The entire world is full of such elevated persons and even extreme corners of the world are not without them just as there are hidden treasures in ruins. Therefore, develop an intention to meet an unknown godly man, even without any object, when you get information about him. When you do not have the eyes that cannot see hidden great ones, consider everything of the world as a treasure. If he is not such an elevated person like the Qutub, he can be at least a co-traveler. He may not be a king but certainly he can be a horseman. Therefore, consider and develop concern for men, whoever they may be, footmen or horsemen.

sections.heading: Company of Others Is Beneficial:
paras: Showing grace even to an enemy is good, as there is a possibility of his becoming a friend. Even if he does not become a friend, his enmity is certainly reduced, as gratefulness is a soothing balm for enmity. Yet, there are many other benefits, but I want to avoid stretching the matter. The sum and substance are that, you should be a friend and follower of the collective life and create a companion for yourself from outside, just as the idol-maker, creates a companion for himself out of stone. The largeness of the travelers of the caravan breaks the backs and spears of the dacoits.

This resentful message came to H.Mūsā from God: “O the one who has seen the sun rising from the lapel: I made you an east to raise the sun from my light. I am God! But when I fell sick, you did not come to see me.”

H. Mūsā said: “O God, you are free from every attribute of loss. You are free from any loss or deficiency. How can you have the attribute of sickness. I cannot understand the secret of your sickness. Do clarify this to me.”

sections.heading: Man’s Sickness Is God’s Sickness:
paras: Then, God further said: “I was sick. Why did you not enquire about Me with your kindness?”
H. Mūsā said: “O God, how can there be any sickness on your part. I cannot understand this. Clarify this mystery.”

Then God said: “This is very clear. A close servant of mine was sick. I was he. Know this well! His sickness in My sickness. His weakness is My weakness. Tell anybody desirous to remain in My company to be in the company of My friends (Aulia). Their company prevents the effects of devil’s insinuations. If you remain away from them, you will be ruined as you are only a part and not the whole. One who is separated from the whole of the good ones will be easily caught by the devil, finding one to be helpless. He will chew his head. Keeping you away from the company of companions even for a moment may be considered as his treachery. Know this well.”

When a gardener looked into his garden, he saw three persons appearing to him as thieves. One was a Mawlavi (jurist), another a Syed (a descendant of H. Alī), and the third a sūfī. Each one of them was talkative, shameless and blabbering. He said to himself: “I have a hundred arguments against them but with togetherness in a company they are blessed. I cannot win against all the three, if I have to physically deal with them. Therefore, I must first separate them from each other. By throwing away one from the other two, I can find each of them alone, and thus, I can break their heads”. Thus resolving, he put the sūfī on one way so as to destroy him in loneliness.
