He told the sūfī to go to his house and bring a blanket for his companions. When the sūfī left, he told the other two: “You are a jurist and the other is of noble descent. We eat our food as per your decisions. We depend upon your legal decisions on all matters.”

About the Syed, he said: “He is our king and prince. He is a Syed and from the family of the H.Mustafā. Who is that mean sūfī, a devourer of food, so as to be a companion of kings like you? You may cord him like cotton when he returns, and you may remain in my garden for a week. What is the worth of the garden? My life itself is your property. You are like my right eye”. He created suspicions in their minds and cheated them. How regretful! Suspecting friends is not proper.

When the sūfī was let to go and he was alone, the gardener took a thick club in his hand and went behind him. He told him: “O doggish sūfī, you are that sufi who dashed forcibly into our garden. Which great sūfī, H.Junaid or H.Bāyazīd has taught you to do like this? From which other sūfī have you learnt to do like this?” The poor sūfī was lonely and the gardener beat him, rendering him half dead and finally smashed his head. While dying the sūfī said: “My time anyway has passed off. But my friends, take care of yourselves. Be warned! You considered me as other than yours. You did not think: whatever I may be, but I cannot be a greater stranger than this devil. Whatever I have tasted will be tasted by you. Such a type of beating is a punishment of every mean fellow. What has come upon me will come upon you also. You will also have to drink such a syrup. This world is a hillock and whatever you say will boomerang upon you like an echo.”

After dealing with the sūfī, he resorted to another trick for the other two. He told the Syed, “Go to my house as I have prepared chapati (thin flat bread) for you. Tell the servant at the door to bring for you chapatis and roasted chicken”

sections.heading: Facts and Doubts About Descendants:
paras: After he left, he told the jurist (Mawlavi): “You are the one with sharp eyes. That you are a jurist is clear and certain. But that fellow claims for himself the family of the Prophet without any evidence. Who knows about his mother and as to what all she did. The claim of descent is made by women. Can anyone be satisfied with that claim. With imperfect wisdom, can one believe her words. There are many hollow foolish fellows in the world who have claimed their connections with the Prophet and H. Alī.”

Such suspicions are cast upon godly people by only such fellows who are themselves products of fornications and fornicators. One whose head gets into vertigo thinks that the house is rolling around. Whatever was told by that blabbering gardener about others was his own situation and he was far away from the descendants of the Prophet. Had he not been from the semen of the reverters from faith, he would not have said such things about the family of the Prophet. He recited some magic spells; the jurist heard and foolishly became his obedient victim.

Then the gardener went towards the Syed and said: “You are an ass. Who called you in this garden? Have you received thievery from the inheritance of the Prophet? The cub of the lion resembles the lion. Tell me what resemblance you have with the Prophet?”

In his misguidance, that mean gardener did to the Syed, what the Kharijites had done with the family of the Prophet. See how much permanent and transferring enmity devils and ghosts have with the descendants of the Prophet like Yazid and Shumar. The Syed got destroyed with the beatings of the gardener, cried and told the jurist: “Now that you are reduced in strength and lonely, be like a drum and beat well on your belly. Even if I am not a Syed and suitable friend, I am no less valuable than that cruel fellow. You have handed me over to that self-serving fellow. You have committed a foolish act and you will get a bad reward.”

Then the gardener turned toward the jurist and said: “What kind of jurist you are? You are a disgrace to every ill-witted fellow. O hand-broken fellow! Do you give a verdict that one should simply get inside a house without asking for permission. Have you read any base for this in Imam Ghazali’s Waseeth and Muheeth, the famous books on Hanfi Jurisprudence? So, saying, he freely used his hands to beat him and satisfied the meanness of his heart. The jurist said: “You have every right to beat me as I am entirely in your control. I am certainly entitled for this punishment and a hundred more of this kind. This is the punishment for him who gets away from his companions. I have heard all the insults you cast on me and I myself beat upon my head for its having lost his honour.”

In short, the gardener beat him well and thrashed him out of his garden and shut its door. Whoever gives up the company of friends faces difficulties of these kinds. Thus, enquiring about one’s sickness is for this reason only to explain that it results in hundreds of aspects of love, as visits to the sick bring about social cohesion.
The unique uncamparable Prophet went to make enquiries about his companion and found him in his last moments.

When you are away from the friends of God, it is as good as remaining away from God. When separation from friends is sorrowful, it is all the more in separations from the kings of spiritualism. Go towards the shadow of these kings, so that you may become better than the sun in brightness. Remain under the protection of one such beloved of God, as there are possibilities of a man-of-heart granting you freedom from worldly constrictions. Be so with this intention, whether you are in your own place or on a journey. Go from one street to another and from one home to another in search of them, and never get tired of searching. As far as possible, do not turn away from godly people and try your utmost to be with them and know that, God knows best.

H.Baayazid, master of the community was going towards Makka to perform Hajj and Umrah. In whichever city he entered on the way, he searched for great men, making enquiries about such persons throughout the city, who has settled himself upon the pillars of Tariqat (Special methods adopted by the sūfis for the purification of the soul and to get spiritual attainments. Different schools of sūfis have slightly different methods of their own due to the differences of geographical places, times and the capacities of the disciples and the people at large around them ― Translator)

God put into Baayazīd’s heart: “The basic objective of your journey should be to meet a man of God. Have an intention to get such a treasure; and the other profits or losses that you meet on the way are only consequential.

sections.heading: Intention Predominates Action and Better:
paras: A farmer sows the seeds of wheat for the sake of wheat, but as a consequence, he also gets fodder. If you sow the seeds of maize, you get maize and not wheat. Therefore, your efforts should be only to search for the great men. At the time of the Hajj, you make an intention for Ka‘aba, but as a consequence, you see the city of Makka too. The object of Ascension of the Prophet was only to see God, but as a consequence, angels and ‘arsh were also seen. The Noble Prophet, has said: “Intention is the base of actions”. Good intentions bring about many blooming flowers. Intention of a faithful person is better than his actions. This is what the king of kingdoms has said: “A faithful person’s intention is better than his action, while the action of the hypocrite is better than his intention.”

A fresh disciple of a shaikh constructed a new house and the sheikh tested the disciple’s abilities. He asked him as to why he has kept the windows? The disciple said: “It is to allow light to enter”. The sheikh said: “This is a part object. You should have it to allow the call of prayer to enter into the house. Light as per its nature, on its own, enters into the house. Therefore, your intention should be for something greater”.

sections.heading: Closed Eyes Show Invisible Things:
paras: H. Baayazīd, during his journey, searched very much for a guide like Khizr of the time. He saw an old man bent like the crescent; and he found in his talks the grandeur of the man-of-truth. He was blind of eyes, with a heart bright like the sun, and engrossed in thoughts like an elephant which sees its native country, Hindustan, in its dreams. The dear ones often remain in thoughts and appear in dreams. By keeping their eyes shut, the holy people see a hundred pleasurable sceneries of the other world. And upon opening the eyes, they see nothing. They see many wonders in dreams as the heart becomes a window in sleep. The one who sees good dreams even when awake is a godly person, so high in stature that you should cast your eyes on his feet.

When H. Baayazīd found him among the top most level saints, called Qutubs, he humbled himself and readied for service. He sat before him and made enquiries and found him to be a destitute but with a family. The saint asked him: “Where are you proceeding to? What is your final destination?” H. Baayazīd said: “Out of my great love for it, I am proceeding to Ka‘aba.” He asked him: “How much money you have for expenses of the journey?” He replied: “Two hundred silver coins, which I have secured tightly in the corner of my mantle.”

sections.heading: Service to Man; Service to God:
paras: Then, he said: “You may circumambulate around me for seven times and consider it to be better than your hajj. Be generous and keep those coins before me and think that you have performed your hajj and met the object. You performed your circumambulation and cleansed the remaining part of your life and ran along Safaa. I swear upon God, Who has seen your soul. He has granted excellence to me upon His house (ka‘aba). Though Ka‘aba is the house for His worship, my creation (as man) also is a great house of His secrets. Ever since, He made this house of a man (heart) as His house, He has not gone into that house (Ka‘aba). And in this house (heart) of mine, none other than the Living and Perceiving (Hayy) and the self-Existing (Qayyum) has entered. If you look at me, it means you are looking at God, as with union and identification with God, men become one with Him. Your looking at me (as man) is like looking at God and your going around me (as man) is like going around the Ka‘aba. Service to me is like obedience and praising to God. Be warned! Do not think that God is separate from me. Open your eyes wide and look at me so that you may see the Light of God in man. O Baayazīd! You have already found out the Ka‘aba. You have already obtained a hundred greatnesses, honours and grandeurs. God has called the Ka‘aba as ‘My house’(baitii) only once, and addressed me as “My Servant” (yaa-‘ibaadii) seventy times.”

H. Baayazīd put all these points into his memory and dressed his ears like with earrings of gold. H. Baayazīd was a high-level knower of God, but after hearing all this, he got elevated to still higher level like a perfect disciple.

sections.heading: Special Benefits of Sickness:
paras: As the Prophet looked at the sick companion, he showed great attention toward him. When he looked at the Prophet, he became fresh and smart as though he was created by God just then, He said: “This is the great reward for me for my sickness that, early in the morning, the king has come to me; and as such, I regained my health and comfort because of the impacts of his gracious visit. Prosperous is this sickness, its pain and fever. Prosperous is the pain and deprivation of the nightly sleep. Great is the love and grant of God upon me in my old age, with such sickness and pain. He gave me back-pain so that I may get up from sleep at night and perform tahajjud prayer. So that, I may not sleep for the whole night like a buffalo. God has granted such pains to me out of His grace. Further, this break down has risen up that mercy of the king for me to so such an extent that hell cannot frighten me. Sickness became a treasury of benevolences. When the skin of the fruit was peeled, there came out fresh pulp.”

My brother, having patience in a dark, cold place and in circumstances of pain, tiresomeness and sorrows is a fountain of life-giving-water and a cup of intoxicating wine as all higher achievements are hidden in pains. Spring seasons are hidden in autumns as though autumn itself is spring. Do not run away from autumn. Become a friend of sorrows and manage your affairs even in circumstances of disgust. Search for a long life in your death.

sections.heading: Consultations Are Helpful:
paras: Whatever is told by your desiring self is vicious. It should not be heard, but its opposite should be done. Go against it, as all prophets have said the same thing and this advice has come from generation to generation. It is necessary to have consultations in attending to jobs, so that any pain of failures may be reduced. The prophets have resorted to many methods to meet their ends and it is upon them that one grindstone has rotated upon another. The vicious self (fleshy soul) of everyone wants to destroy him and create confusions and misguidance all over the world.

Their followers demanded from them as to with whom, they should consult to do their jobs? They said: “It should be with a man of perfect wisdom.” They asked: “What to do if a child or a woman with no sufficient wisdom and clear opinion comes forward”? They said: “Consult them, but do the opposite of what they say and follow your path.”

Consider your fleshy soul as a woman (with no sufficient wisdom) or worse than her, as she is only a part of yours; and your self is mischief in entirety. You may consult your vicious self and do the opposite of what it says. Even if it gives an advice to perform salat and fasting, think that it is doing so to cheat you through these means. [Many a time salat and fasting are resorted to by mischievous fellows, only as a ruse to pose themselves as pious, ultimately to cheat people. The mischievous self gives this advice to them. The case of the Jewish vazir who resorted to piety to destroy the Christians is already cited in detail. Cheats always don the appearances of noble people and professionals. No cheat says: “I am a cheat; get cheated by me.” Resorting to pious acts is the commonest form of cheating, of which innocent masses are the most gullible victims ― Translator].

sections.heading: Consultation with Self:
paras: You can consult your fleshy self in your routine jobs, but doing against its advice is perfectness. But it would be very difficult to go against it and fight. Therefore, it is necessary that you should go to a learned friend and seek his help. Wisdom gets strength with the wisdom of another, just as sugarcane develops well in a farm exclusively for sugarcane. I have seen many treacheries of the commanding self. Its highest achievement is that it eliminates your sense of good and bad from you. It gives new and newer promises to you which have been broken by it a thousand times. Even if you live for a thousand years, it will give you new designs every day. It will show false promises as true. With the promise of increasing your sexual potential, it destroys it altogether.

sections.heading: God’s Grace Alters Situations:
paras: O Zia ul Haq Husamuddin, come nearer to me, as without you, grass does not grow in infertile land. A curtain is hanged along the sky to condemn a sorrowful heart which is a victim of vicious self, indicating that the treacheries of the self are also caused by God and the treatment to undo them can be only through God. Wisdom of the people in the matters of fate is confused and crisscrossed. That black serpent which was lying on the path like a worm became a large python. O Musa, at your hand, snakes and pythons became drowsy and dry sticks, because God gave you a command to hold on. He said: ‘Seize it and fear not’: “Qaala khuzhaa wa laa takhaf”: (Taha: 20: 21), so that the python may become a stick in your hand. When H. Musa removed his hand after putting it under his armpit, it shined bright like the sun. As such, O Husamuddin, you may also brighten the dark night and bring out a new morning with your bright self.

sections.heading: How God’s Grace Works:
paras: The vicious self has set a hell of fire. Blow air with your mouth on it to extinguish it, as the blow of your mouth is stronger than the waves of ocean. The vicious self is an ocean of treacheries, but appears like froth. It is a hell of mischief but appears as 0f little warmth. It appears small to you, so that you may consider it lowly, and may not step back and need the courage to fight with it. In similar manner, a large army of the infidels appeared small to the Prophet’s eyes, as it happened at the time of the battle of Badr. This was to make him attack without fear, and he did it. Had he seen them in large numbers, he would have hesitated. The showing of lesser numbers was a grant of God, O Muhammad, otherwise, you would have become desperate. They were shown in lesser numbers to you and to your companions, because this was a battle for the apparent as well as the unseen. This gave great hidden support to the Prophet from God so that he did not turn his face from the difficult situation. Showing of the enemies in lesser numbers itself was a victory and joy as of a festival day. That was a day of great prosperity, as he was under the support and guidance of God. One who has no support of God will see a rabbit as a lion.

sections.heading: Underestimation of Opponents:
paras: They are unfortunate who see a hundred as only one from a distance and hit upon the enemy under this wrong impression. The great mighty sword, Zulfiqar of H. Ali appears to them just as a spear. Under this foolish impression, they become bold and resort to fight; and God catches them through this ruse, so that they may walk with their own feet into the furnace in a foolish manner. The furnace appears to them as a piece of burning grass, which can be put out and destroyed with one blow from the mouth, and they do so with it. Know well, the egotist self-destroys men strong like hills, and the world laughs and cries due to its impacts. It appears like a narrow stream just deep enough upto the ankle but actually it is so deep that hundreds of large-sized men like Aoj bin Unuq, (for whom the depths of oceans reached up to the knees), drowned into it. Waves of blood appear to it as dunes of musk. Pharaoh blindly saw the sea as a dry bed and rashly entered into it with all his might. There upon, he went into the seabed. His eyes failed to see it.

sections.heading: God Does Not Bless the Weak-Minded:
paras: One who has seen God, gets his eyesight brightened. He can be seen only by those wise ones who have deep insight. God cannot share His secrets with the weak-minded. The weak-minded consider poison as sugar and walk on a wrong path upon the calling of ghosts.

O sky, you move faster in the last days of trial period. At least, give some peace to us. Your sharp dagger is after our lives and your poisoned syringes are on a killing spree. O sky, learn to show mercy from the All Merciful, and do not bite on the hearts of the ants like a serpent. For the sake of the One Who has set in motion the wheel of your dome, rotate in a different manner to show mercy, well before you uproot us from our base. The truth is that, you have first taken care of us from the beginning in such a manner that our seed grew into a plant from water and clay. For the sake of the One, Who has created you in all cleanliness and hanged so many torches in you. He has kept you so full of your contents that the denier of God called you alone as the Eternal and Immutable.

sections.heading: Wisdom Is Subtle and Above All:
paras: We are thankful to God that we have understood your beginning. The prophets have revealed your secrets to us. Only man knows that space and the world are created ones but not the spider, which plays happily within its web. Mosquito does not know as to from when it is in this garden as it takes birth in spring and dies within it. A slowly moving woodworm that takes birth within wood, cannot know of the time, when the wood came into existence. If the worm comes to know of this reality, it becomes wisdom in the shape of worm. Wisdom projects itself in many shapes and colors, but it is subtle like the fairy, rather miles and miles above the fairy in subtlety. Where is the fairy to compare with, wisdom is far above the angels. But you do not try to understand all this. You have the wings of the housefly and therefore you fly downward and not upward.

sections.heading: Taqlid (Uncritical Faith) Degrades You:
paras: Though your wisdom can lead you upward, but the bird of the uncritical faith (Taqlid) takes you downward. Uncritical faith is a heavy burden upon the life. This is not inherent and spontaneous. It is borrowed thing from others. But we sit comfortably thinking that it is our own property. It is better to get rid of this wisdom, it is better to go mad than to have it. Whatever that is projected as useful by this stupidity must be avoided. Whatever is considered as life-giving-water by this stupidity must be thrown away and what is shown as poison must be drunk.

sections.heading: Chase Away Praises and Praisers:
paras: Whoever with immature wisdom praises you on your face may be chased away; and his praises, as investment and profits may be passed on to those who are destitute of wisdom. Leave and go away from that place, which is considered as peaceful by immature wisdom and reside in a place of fear and turmoil. Say goodbye to the honours of such place and opt to become dishonored. I have tested far-seeing-wisdom by now. Hereafterwords, I shall make myself mad.

One night a nobleman told a humorist: “You have married a prostitute in haste. You should have told me about your desire to marry, so that I could get you married to a seclusive, chaste woman.” He said: “I have married nine seclusive women of noble birth, but they all became unchaste and I suffered a lot in sorrows. Therefore, knowing fully well, I married this prostitute to see what she would become.”
I have also tested wisdom very much. From now onwards, I shall search for the fields of madness.

A person said that he wanted to meet a wiseman with whom he wanted to consult on some matter. Another person told him: “There is only one wiseman (H. Bahalool) in our city, who deliberately projects himself as a mad man. Mounted on a bamboo stick, calling it as a horse, he runs around as though riding a horse just as children do. Day and night he plays around with children. He is a great hidden treasure. He is the soul of the world. He is very wise and sharp like a spark. He rides upon the stars in the heavens. He is highly respected by the angels. But he is hidden from others through his pretended madness”.

sections.heading: Peculiarities of Saintly and Wise Men:
paras: But be careful, not to consider every madman to be wise in reality by keeping his (Bahlool’s) case in view, and do not keep your forehead before the calf. Saintly people do not speak to you in straightforward manner. They keep hundreds of thousands of secrets within themselves which relate to the unseen world. This is because people do not have the capacity to understand them. They cannot differentiate between aloeswood (agar) and dung. When you cannot understand them, even when they are clearly in the open, how can you understand when they have tied the curtain of madness before them. If the eyes of your confidence are open, you can see the commander of the frontline army under every stone. For you there is a spokesman behind every blanket. The saint expresses his ability to whomsoever he wishes, if he finds him to be capable. Nobody can understand him through his wisdom, and particularly the one who has projected himself as mad. If a thief steals the materials of a blind person, he cannot catch the thief even if he is right before him. The blind man cannot identify the thief, even if the thief, out of his enmity pounces upon him. When a dog bites a blind man in shabby clothes, the blind man cannot identify the dog.

A street dog was pouncing upon a blind beggar like a ferocious lion. Dogs and also ignorant fellows pounce upon the faqirs of even that level the dust of whose feet moon applies on its eyes like eye black.

sections.heading: Fear Creates Flattery of the Mean:
paras: The blind beggar, out of the fear of the dog was humbled and started honouring the dog saying: “O master of the game animals, O hunting lion! You are victorious. Please relieve me.”

Under the compulsion of time, a wise man honours the donkey’s tail and addresses it in soft words. So also, this blind beggar told the dog: “O lion, what are you going to get by catching a weak game like me. Your friends in the forest hunt upon fat donkeys, but you catch a blind fellow who is roaming about in the streets. Your friends are in search of fat donkeys for their hunt and you are searching for a blind fellow out of your treachery.”

sections.heading: Mean Becomes Great After Training:
paras: Yet, there are dogs which are trained to hunt animals, which go to hunt donkeys in the forest. But this untrained dog was pouncing upon the blind. A trained dog got rid of its misguidance after training and is searching for halal animals. Upon training, the dog became smart and disciplined. And when it remained in the company of pious people, it got the honour of a dog of the Companions of the Cave. The dog became aware as to what should be its hunt. It recognized its master after getting the light of knowledge from the master’s companionship.

sections.heading: What and Where Is Knowledge:
paras: Think over as to what and where that knowledge is. The blind do not identify things. Yet, there are many with eyes, who do not see. This is not due to blindness, but because of the fact that they are in the intoxication of ignorance. Of all the blind, earth is the most blind, but with God’s grace it became capable of finding the enemy. It saw the light of H. Mūsā and presented its grants when he needed. It identified Qārūn and pulled him within itself. It caused earthquakes to kill all false claimants.

sections.heading: Non-Living Totally Obedient to God:
paras: Dust, air, water and burning fire are not aware of us, but are aware of God. As against them, we are ignorant of God and aware of other things. We are unaware of God inspite of being warned of Him by so many prophets. Inevitably, the entire universe ― heavens, earth, mountains refused to undertake the Trust of God, being afraid thereof: ‘but man undertook it’: “wa ashfaqna minhaa”: (Ahzaab: 33: 72). In order to undertake this Trust earth was in need of some of the qualities of living beings, which it lacked. Therefore, it refused along with other creatures ― heavens and mountains, compounds of mud, water, air and earth, that is, materials. They said: “We do not want life. We are disgusted of it as it makes us alive with creatures but dead with God”. When man gets separated from other creatures, he becomes a total destitute like an orphaned child. To maintain the love of God along with other creatures, it requires a very strong heart.

sections.heading: Blind Cannot Identify Own Materials:
paras: When the thief steals the materials of the blind, he cries without interruption, until the thief himself says that, he has stolen, and that he is an expert thief. The blind man cannot identify the thief, on his own, as he neither has the seeing capacity of the eyes nor the light to help them. When the thief admits of the theft, it requires that he is held tightly so that he may spell out the particulars of the materials. Thus, holding on to the thief, needs a great struggle (Jihad-e-Akbar) to compel him to say about the stolen materials. This has to be the way in respect of the man’s vicious self. This requires the squeezing of the vicious self.

sections.heading: Vicious Self: Most Expert Thief:
paras: Vicious self is an expert thief. First of all, it has stolen your mascara from your eyes making you semi-blind and then stolen your wisdom. Until you regain your perfect eyesight and wisdom you cannot see things well. You can certainly regain by remaining in the company of the great men of heart. Thus, the wealth of wisdom that was lost can be regained. One, who is blind at heart, cannot see the markings of the devil, who has committed theft of the sensibilities of the eyes, ears and soul. You may search for all those lost things from the men of heart and spirit and not form those without spiritual sensibilities. Creatures are without sensibilities when they come against the thief of the self.

Let us return to that man who was in search of the knowledge of secrets, so that we may also have some consultation with the revealer of secrets. The seeker of information approached Shaykh Bahlool and told him: “O father, who is behaving like a child, tell me about a secret.” He replied: “Go away from this chain as the door cannot open. Go away, as today is not a day to reveal secrets. Had there been a way to the house of the non-material world (Lahoot) through the material world (Nasoot), I also would have been seated on a decorated stage like the so-called masters (mashayakhs) in the teaching shops.

A police officer, at midnight, reached a place where he saw an inebriated man lying at the base of the wall. He said: "Hey, you are intoxicated with wine, tell me, what have you drunk?”. The man replied: “I have drunk, what is there in the wine-pot.” He said: “Speak out clearly! What is there in the wine-pot?" He replied: "That which I drank”. The officer said: “This is a dilly-dallying reply. Tell me clearly what really you drank? He replied: "The same that was in the wine-pot.”

This question and answer process went on; and the police officer was caught in slush like an ass. Then he told to the drunk: “Be warned, take sighs of pain!” The intoxicated man, instead, made laughing sounds: "ha., ha., ha., ha." The police officer said: “I told you to make sighs of sorrow, but you are making sounds of joy.” The man replied: “I am happy but you are bent in your back in sorrows”. 'Sigh’s’ come about from men in sorrows, pain, and oppression. The sounds of 'ha., ha., ha' from the mouth of the drunkard come out of pleasure.

The police officer said: “I don’t know all that. Get up! Do not pose yourself as a learned man. Get up and put an end to this blabbering.” The drunk said: "You may go away! Where is your place and where is mine?” The officer said: “You are under intoxication! Get up and walk toward the prison.” The drunk fellow said: “O Officer, leave all this, and walk away from here! What material of a naked man can be pawned? If I had the strength to walk, I would have walked to my house; and this quarrel would not have arisen".

The following words are of Shaykh Bahlool, whom a seeker of advice contacted: "If I were wise and under control, I would have opened up a shop, just as the showy sheikhs and sūfis do, and sat on an ostentatious honorable place. If I were to have suggestions to make and the methods of profit making from them, I also would have had good status and recognition like the grand sheikhs. I also would have had a begging bag full of begged materials, daily grants and offerings. Go away from me, as by mistake, you have come here. Go and search for a long beard and a khanqah of sūfis.”

The seeker of wisdom from H.Bahlool said: “Stop you horse for a moment, O rider on the bamboo stick! Turn your horse toward me for a moment!” H.Bahlool turned toward him and said: "Say fast, what you want to say, because my horse is very strong and uncontrollable. Be fast, so that it may not give you a kick. Tell me clearly! What do you want?”

The seeker found no scope to speak of what he wanted to know, as H. Bahlool was in a hurry. He ignored his question and engaged him in lighter vein, and said: "I intend to marry a woman from this street. Please tell me who is suitable for one like me?”

sections.heading: Three Kinds of Women:
paras: H. Bahlool said: "There are three kinds of women in the world: two of those are a cause of trouble, and one is an ever-accompanying wealth. If you marry this woman, she will be entirely yours. The second one is yours to half an extent and the third one will have no concern for you. She will never be yours. You have heard what I said. Now be off! I shall run away from here, so that my horse may not give you a double kick. If it does so, you will not get up from here till the doomsday.”

So, saying, the Sheikh drove his horse amongst the children. The seeker again called him: "Please come back and tell me in detail. You have spoken of three types of women. Choose one among them for me.”

The sheikh drove his horse back and said: “A virgin! She will be entirely yours and you will be relieved of all sorrows from her. The one who would be half with you is a widow, as she would have half inclination towards her past husband. And the third one, who is not at all with you, is a widow with her children. Her whole heart would be inclined towards the children and the father of the children. Now, do run away so that my horse may not give a double kick and the hooves of my haughty horse may not injure you.”

So, saying, the sheikh made loud cries as mad men do and called back the children towards him. The seeker called him yet again and said: “Please come back, O king! There is one more question to be asked.” Then the sheikh turned and rode towards him and said: “Tell me fast. That child has taken my ball and ran away from the field.”

The seeker said: “O king! With so much of wisdom and experience, what is this artificiality? What is it that you are doing like this? I cannot understand. You are so ahead of the fullest wisdom in explaining matters. You are a sun of knowledge. Why have you hidden yourself in madness?”

sections.heading: Wise Men Do Not Reveal Wisdom:
paras: The Sheikh said: “This is what the common masses think about me and as such they want to make me a qazi of the city. I avoid them, but they do not agree. They say: There is no other person of your calibre and knowledge. It is not proper and legal for anyone to give judgments of lower standard when you are here. There is no provision in law to make our leader and guide, of a person who is lesser in worth than you. Being compelled under this circumstance, I have made myself mad and incompetent and kept myself as a stranger to them.”

“Though to look at, I have become mad, but in truth I am just the same as I have always been. My wisdom is a treasure, but I am a ruin. Treasures are hidden in ruins. If I expose this treasure of mine, I will really become mad. Because of this I have to hide myself in madness. One who does not become mad in this manner, is infact, mad. He is like one who does not hide himself in his house upon seeing a police officer. My wisdom is a lasting substance in its own existence and not temporary and borrowed from others like accident. Perfect wisdom does not expose itself and remains hidden. I am a mine of sugar and a farm of sugarcane. Sugar comes out from me and I eat my own sugar.”

sections.heading: Knowledge for Making Money Is No Knowledge:
paras: Uncritical knowledge learnt from others and taught to others gets disgusted when the audiences do not show interest in hearing, as this knowledge is for making a livelihood and not for getting the inner sight of God. The seeker of such knowledge is also a seeker of these worldly materials. The object of seeking knowledge by the small and big ones is this world is to gain wealth, and not to get rid of its compulsions. They are like rats which create holes here and there in every direction for their refuge and not like the birds which are free of such holes. They make holes everywhere but never bother about the sighting of God. As they move about in the deserts and not in search of light, they always struggle in darkness. If God gives them the feathers of wisdom, they ignore the acts of the rats and fly like birds. If they do not search for feathers, they will remain under the layers of mud and never think of the path to Samaak, the farthest star in the sky.

sections.heading: Speakable and Thought-Provoking Knowledge:
paras: Spoken knowledge has no soul and is in love with and search of buyers. Such knowledge may be very great for discussions, but it will not get buyers. It becomes useless and gets lost. But my knowledge is not of spoken words, but one that drags me from the lowly world to the higher world; and God is its buyer, as Allah has said: ‘God has bought from the believers their lives and their wealth’: "innal laaha ashtara minal mu'mineena anfusahum wa amwaalahum": (Tauba: 9: 111). Damages payable upon my killing are the sighting of the Lord of majesty and honor, which only I eat and that earning is a perfectly permissible payment (I sacrifice my life for Him and get this as its price). Ignore those worldly destitutes as your purchasers. After all, what can a handful of dust purchase. Do not eat mud, do not buy mud and do not search for mud, as one who eats mud is always pale-faced and sick.

sections.heading: God 's Extra Benevolence to Crush Vicious Self:
paras: Purchase the hearts of the people to remain always youthful and to keep your face red like babuna flower (redbud tree). Be always in search of hearts so as to be fresh and happy like flowers and wine. That is not a heart which searches for mud. Heart which belongs to that upper realm alone can understand the meaning of what I said. O God! Just giving this heart of your realm is not enough. Your extra benevolence is required for it to reach its realities. Show kindness to us by purchasing us from ourselves. Lift the curtains between us, so as to make us see You, and do not hide Yourself from us. You have also given us this obnoxious self (nafs), whose dagger has penetrated deep upto our bones. Purchase us back from its control. None other than You, the crownless and throneless King, can save us from the shackles of this vicious self (nafs). The desires of the vicious self have put such a heavy lock on us, which cannot be opened other than Your grace. We turn our faces towards You alone, because You are nearer to us than ourselves. Inspite of such nearness we are far away from You. This is a deep darkness. Send Your light to destroy this darkness. We are praying to You. But this prayer of ours is not ours, but this is also granted by You, because we are like a furnace in which there is no scope for flowers to come about. The flowers of prayer have come about in our burning furnace because of Your grants. This is a living sample of Your loving kindness.

sections.heading: Grant of Eyes, Tongue, Ears:
paras: You have granted wisdom and showed the means of doing their jobs to our blood and intestines. None else can do this, other than Your grace. In two pieces of the fatty eyes of ours, You have provided such light, the waves of which go far and attack the heavens. There are pieces of flesh in our mouths, as tongues, which flow streams upon streams of intelligence towards those holes which are called 'ears', which carry the fruits of intelligence towards the garden of life inside.

sections.heading: God’s Laws: Gardens Beneath Which Rivers Flow:
paras: God’s laws are the highways leading to the gardens of life, and the gardens of this world are only branches of that garden. These only are the base and origin of joys of life, which give us extreme bliss and satisfaction. You may refer to: “beneath which rivers flow” as stated in the Quran: ‘Gardens beneath which rivers flow’: "jaanaatin tajree min tahtihal anhaar”: (Baqarah: 2: 25) and many more times throughout the Qurān.

There is no limit to the grants of God. Now tell us about the narrative of the Prophet’s visit to the sick companion. As for thanking God! How can you express thanks to Him, as the expression of thanks to Him by you, is again a fresh grant from Him. The truth is: your inability to express thanks itself is an expression of all thanks. Know this; think over it and let us stop at this!

Upon visiting the sick man, the Prophet said to him: “Perhaps you made a supplication and, in your ignorance, drank poisonous soup. Think over, and say what you supplicated for, that you are in this trouble." He said: "I do not remember. If you please cast your attention upon me, it will come back to my memory". Through the light-spreading attention of the Prophet, he recalled to his memory what he had prayed to God.

Upon the attention of the lightful parentage of the Prophet, the forgotten prayer came back to his mind, through that hole that is there from heart to heart. That light came which differentiates between the right and wrong. He said: “I now remember O Prophet! The prayer which was made by this father of nonsense. When I was sunk in sins, I was waving my hands and feet. A sinful person knocks at the door of forgievance. A sinking fellow tries to catch a straw. A message of warning and fear had come from you, that the sinners will face a severe punishment. I got worried and there was no means of escape. I was held in a strong prison and there was no key to unlock it. There was neither a scope for patience, nor a way to run away to some other place. There was neither hope of repentance, nor opportunity for arguments. There was none to befriend me other than God. My job was in great difficulty. I was suffering with sorrows like Haruut and Maruut, hanging upside down in the well. I was craving before my Creator.

sections.heading: Haruut and Maruut:
paras: [Haruut and Maruut, according to Biblical narratives were two angels who came down on earth as men proficient in magic. With magical powers they used to bring about quarrels between husbands and wives. They committed fornication with a beautiful woman, consequent upon which they were hanged upside down in a well where they will remain till the doomsday. And that woman was converted into planet Venus and pushed deep into the heaven. This story became popular among the common Muslims. But Quran does not speak of all that - As taken from Abdulla Yusuf Ali’s exegesis of Quran. The punishment of the Haruut and Maruut is taken as an illustration by Rumi – Translator].

sections.heading: Haruut and Maruut Preferred Punishment in This World:
paras: Haruut and Maruut were aware of the severity of the punishment of hell and therefore, decided to get punished for their sins in this world itself, as the severest of the punishment here is milder than that of hell; and also, there is an end to worldly punishment, but the punishment of hell is endless. They preferred to undergo the punishment here itself, as they are very well aware, wise and expert magicians. What they did was right as the inconvenience caused by smoke is far lesser than that by fire. There is no end and limit to the pains of the next world; and as against this, punishment of this world is far milder.

sections.heading: Wrong to Seek Punishment:
paras: That man is blessed and prosperous, who struggles here by inflicting hardships of life upon his body and puts the burden of worship on it to seek solace of the heart. The sick companion said: “I also prayed to God saying: O God, the punishment due to me there, may be imposed upon me fast here itself, so that I may remain relieved of it in the next world. With such a request I knocked at the door of God. As a result, this sickness developed in me and my life has lost all its comforts. I am, by now, tired of the remembrances of God and repeated pleadings. I am not unaware of the good and bad aspects of things. Had I not seen your prosperous and soul inspiring face, I would have been completely lost to myself. You have shown me a royal sympathy.”

The Prophet said: “Be careful, never to make such supplication again and get yourself uprooted from the base. O humble ant! What strength do you have to bear the burden of such a high mountain being put upon you”?

sections.heading: Worldly Punishment Is Also Severe:
paras: The companion said: “O king! I repent for my mistake. I shall never bring about any job in a hurry. This world is like the desert of Tia. And you are like H. Mūsā; [Tia is the desert in which H. Mūsā along with Bani Israel roamed about for forty years. Because of H. Mūsā’s prayers, they were getting heavenly food Mann and Salva; and streams of water sprouted from rocks. They used to roam about from one spot in the morning and after roaming for the whole day reach the same spot in the evening. After forty years of repentance, they were released from this desert upon H. Mūsā’s pleadings ― Qazi Sajjad Hussain.]
We roam about for years together in a life of sins. We repent, get released and again commit sins, and are thus held up in the first stage itself.

H.Mūsā’s community (Bani Israel) used to roam about for the whole day and come back to the starting point in the evening. They used to say: “Had H. Mūsā’s heart been pleased with us, the way to get out of Tia, would have become known. Had he been completely disgusted with us, the arrival of Mann and Salwa from the sky would have stopped. Water would not have sprouted from the rocks. These things have protected our lives. Had it been otherwise, fire would have fallen on us instead of food, and destroyed us in this place itself. As H. Mūsā is at two hearts for us, sometimes he is an enemy and sometimes, a friend. His anger sets fire to our materials and his concern for us makes the arrows of troubles return to their place. When does his anger for us turn into concern? O God, this is not far away from Your benevolence.”

The sick companion continued: “Praising anyone on his face is bad manners, and I am deliberately taking the name of H. Mūsā for your attributes. And even H. Mūsā would not like taking his name before you.”

Then he started talking about God: “We have broken the commitment of our obedience to You a hundred times, but your commitment remained undisturbed like a mountain. Our commitment is like a scrap of grass and gets overtaken by every kind of wind, but Your commitment is larger than a mountain, rather hundreds of mountains. And yours is stronger upon our wavering commitment. With this strength You may have mercy on us, O King! I have seen myself and my disgrace and therefore, O King, do not put us to trial to confirm; as, if You put us on trial, many of our hidden disgraces will get exposed. You have no limits in Your grandeur and beauty and we are beyond limits in our wrongs and misguidance. Impose the unlimitedness of your grace upon the unlimited meanness of the handful of our dust. Look at our destitution: only a thread of our clothing has remained upon us. We were a large city and now what is left is just a wall. O King and Protector! Protect whatever is left out by now, so that the devil may not be pleased to the full extent. Forgive us, not for our sake but for the sake of Your forgivance that You have shown to earlier people, as per Your usual practice.

sections.heading: Treacheries Do Not Reward:
paras: “You have imposed the quality of mercy into the lumps of flesh and fat of men, with Your power. Exhibit that power and show mercy to us. O Accepter of prayers! If this prayer of mine increases Your anger for its improper approach, teach us another way of seeking Your indulgence. Teach us just as You taught to H. Adam the methods of seeking pardon and to seek protection from Iblis after he had fallen from Your grace due to disobedience. What is Satan after all, that he should be above H. Adam and win the game on the board. His treachery resorted to meet his jealousy, but in fact, went in favor of H. Adam. His treachery became a cause of his disgrace. He played one trick and forgot that God can play two hundred tricks. In his blindness, he cut off the pole of his tent. He set fire to the farmland of others during the darkness of night, but wind blew the fire to his own farmland. God’s curse was a blindfold on his eyes and he could not see his own end. His treacheries caused so much loss to him that, he started saying that H. Ādam played tricks and trapped him.”

sections.heading: Meaning of Curse (La‘nat):
paras: Curse is what makes a man pervert in sight; and jealous, arrogant and meanly in manners, and remains in that state until he finds that the effects of all these have recoiled upon himself. He sees all the pieces of the chessboard of life in wrong positions resulting in defeat everywhere and loss and disgrace. If he had considered himself as humble and weak, he would have considered his wound as fatal and dangerous upon which he would have felt its pain, which would have taken him to seek relief. Looking at the pain as dangerous and fatal, takes the pain away from its source. Were not the mothers to feel labour pain, there would be no way for the baby to be born.

sections.heading: Pharaoh’s Claim of Lordship:
paras: Trusts of the powers of goodness are like the babies in the wombs of the heart and this advice is like the midwife. When there is no labour pain, there is no midwife and without labour pain there is no way for the baby to come out. One who has not felt pains in life, is a dacoit who has no emotions of kindness. Lack of pain ultimately leads one to be so arrogant as to claim godhood, as Pharaoh claimed saying: ‘I am your lord, the most high!’: “ana rabbu kumul a’laa”: (Nazi‘aat: 79: 24). This saying was inappropriate and ultimately it was a curse. Speaking of your attainment of closeness with God in an appropriate manner at the appropriate time is a cause of mercy, as was in the case of H. Mansur Hallaj who said: “I am the truth”: Ana al haqq. [H. Mansur was sunk deep into the belief of Gods' existence in everything or everything’s existence in God, or existence itself as God and over dominated by it (wahadatul wujud) that, he felt himself completely annihilated in God's essence of 'Al Haq'. That is: nothing exits except God or God is everything. While Pharaoh's claim was total arrogance and claim of parity with God, Mansur’s was total submission to the extent of total annihilation ― Translators’ explanation].

sections.heading: Inappropriate Claim to Be Crushed:
paras: Claiming of the existence of God in everything to appropriate it to one’s own self specifically, at the exclusion of others by saying or feeling as such, is inappropriate. This requires to be crushed just as slaughtering of a cock that crows at inappropriate time is necessary so as to protect the people from misguidance in respect of time.

[This understanding or feeling of the existence of God in everything including me, has been misunderstood by many sufis of later days, who emphasized and claimed as ‘in me’ as though not in other men and all other things. This was their most inappropriate claim. This caused great disrepute to sufis and sufism itself. This was akin to Pharaoh’s: ‘I am your great lord.’ This resulted in another arrogant claim: "I have realized it. Therefore, I claim it. Others have not realized it and they do not claim. Why should I bother about others? Realizing and claiming is their job. It is none of my business to think about others. I am so much engrossed in myself, that I have no time and scope to think of others.” This was a more inappropriate claim.

This inappropriate understanding of “wahadatul wujud” sank such sufis in a dismal abyss and others had to counter and alter it by another doctrine: “wahadatul shuhud” (Observance or appearance of God in everything.) This cooled the impacts of this “wahadatul wujud” and sufis got divided into these doctrines. But the common people, recognized God in their simple manner as shown by Rumi in the incident relating to H. Musa’s chastisement of a shepherd for speaking of God as if He is a baby. H. Musa’s chastisement was disapproved by God. Common people follow their simple ways.

From the days of these controversial doctrines, ununderstandable by common masses, unapproved by non-sufis, the decline of sufistic thoughts started in the Islamic world, creating intellectual and spiritual chaos, which continues to this day. This decline compared with a slow, gradual decline of Muslim political power, resulted in a sense of pessimism everywhere. To this, were added great confusions from the western world, which had just then come into its modern age, whose progress coincided with Islamic and Muslim decline from the 18th century onwards. Consequent to these developments, some rejected sufism and its apparent symbols and centers, and others like Allama Iqbal (1877-1938) went deeper into this ocean and tried to explain Sufism’s lost wealth and its spirit and its potential to help humanity as a whole ― Translator’s Note].

sections.heading: Crushing of Vicious Self:
paras: What is slaughtering? It is crushing of the vicious self by way of denying its demands and working against it through will power and strict austerities. Stings of the scorpion are cut off in order to protect its life. So also, remove the fangs of the serpent, so that it is protected from the hitting stones of people. A masterguide’s shadow only can crush the vicious self and therefore, hold on to him strongly, upon which God’s alliance will come to your support; and actually, His penetration into you. Have faith in the statement: “You did not throw but God threw the dust”, as whatever you do is from the soul of God to your soul. He only is the supporter and carrier of your burden; and be hopeful of his support at every moment.

sections.heading: Delayed Catching and Granting by God:
paras: Do not be sorry at yourself for not having been with Him for so long, as He is the one, who catches the wrongdoers after giving them a long rope, and when He catches, He catches them strong. So also, if His mercy comes after a long time, it will come at high levels. His attention will not ignore you even for a moment. If you want to know about His concern and love, read once again and know and think over on Surah: (Dhuha: 93) wherein He says to the Prophet: "By the glorious morning light and the stillness of the night, at no moment did He forsake him, nor was He displeased! What comes later is better than the present. And soon, you will be well-pleased”.

If you say that wrong thoughts and misfortune are also from Him, you are right; but they are not causes of the stoppage of His grants. Even giving troubles to you is also a perfection of His state. I shall explain this with an illustration:

chapters.title: Faith in God for Good and Bad

paras: A painter made two different paintings, each with good and bad appearance. In one, he made a beautiful, houri-like picture; and in the other one of ugly devils and ghosts. Both these paintings are evidences of his great skill, which speak of his wisdom and expertise and not of his own good or bad qualities. He makes extremely beautiful pictures to represent beauty. The senses of the people derive pleasure out of them. He presents ugliness through ugly pictures in such a way that all ugliness is consolidated in them. Through them his expertise and perfectness in painting are established and his critics feel disgraced.

sections.heading: Good and Bad Are God’s Creations:
paras: Through this example, you may note that, if God were not to make ugly things also, there would be lack of perfectness in His creative quality. That is why, He creates both the faithful and infidels. Thus, faith and infidelity are proofs of His creative capacities and of His godhood and these fall in prostration before Him. But know the difference that the faithful worships Him with pleasure as he seeks God’s consonance and deserves to be closeby to him. The infidel also prostrates, but under compulsion, his object is not the Creator but something else.

sections.heading: Bad Also Worship Him in Bad Ways:
paras: A rebel builds a fort for his rebellious purpose, but projects as though he is doing for the king. He becomes a rebel but ultimately submits to the king when the fort he built falls to the king. One sincere subject builds the fort for the king not to project his own glory and grandeur. He builds with honest intentions. The ugly fellow says: “O Creator of the ugly, You are powerful in creating the ugly and also the beautiful”. And the beautiful says: “O King of beauty and grace, You have created me without any defects. Thanks to you, praises to You, O Provider of benevolences. You are well aware and observing of my conditions”.
The sum and substance of this is: He did whatever He desired, both good and bad, and flowers and thorns. He is the King above all kings, the Maker of all things and Doer of whatever He wishes.

The Prophet told the sick man: “You should tell God to make your difficulties easy for you. Grant the good things of this world and also those of the other world. Make the straight path pleasurable like a garden as our final destination is Your noble self. The faithful will ask the angels on the doomsday, as to, whether the path towards hell was not the same for both the faithful and infidels. Both the faithful and infidels passed on the same path. We did not see fire and smoke on the way. This is the path of happiness and paradise. Where is the other path for the lowly, degraded fellows?”

sections.heading: Path for Heaven and Hell Is the Same:
paras: The angels will say: “The green garden that you saw on the way at that place, was the place, where hell was located and also other places of harsh punishments. It became a green garden full of flowers and fruits for you. This is for the reason that you had caused hardship upon your hellish self, infidelity and mischievous nature to such an extent that this portion of hell became clean and clear of all hellish qualities. Thus, its fire was cooled by you for the sake of God. The fire of passions that was blazing became a greenery of piety and light of guidance. The fire of your anger also turned into toleration and self-control. The darkness of your ignorance was converted into knowledge. The fire of your greed became a desire of sacrifice for the good of others. Thorns of jealousy became flowers.

sections.heading: Good Acts Destroy Hellish Portion of the Common Path:
paras: “You have already destroyed all your fires for the sake of God, and converted your hellish self into a garden and sowed in it the seeds of sincerity, which developed into trees by the side of the streams upon which the bulbuls sing the songs of the praises of God. You accepted the call of those calling you towards God, and collected water for the hellfire of the self. Even your hell became a green garden with all pleasing contents for you. What else is the reward of good acts other than benevolence, gratitude and appropriate recompense?

“Remember! Had you not said: ‘We are sacrifices? We have annihilated ourselves before His attributes and qualities. Whether destitutes and mad, we are intoxicated with the wine of the gnosis of God. We keep our heads bowed down before His commands, and pledge our sweet life to Him. So long as the thoughts of our Friend are there in our hearts, obedience and sacrifice are our jobs.”

sections.heading: Go to the Brightness of Noble Souls:
paras: Wherever such lovers of God light their lamp, hearts of hundreds of thousands of lovers lit up. Such lovers who are already in the court of God, and those who have cast their attention towards it, face towards that lamp, like moths. O my heart! Go towards those who have bright hearts who are like the coat of mail for your chest. They will provide a place for you in their hearts, so as to fill you with God’s knowledge up to the brim like the cup with wine. Make a residence for you in their hearts and through that become like the radiant moon of the sky. They will open the record of heart like planet Mercury (which is called as the writer of the heavens), so that secrets are revealed to you. They are your people, and be with them. You are a part of the moon and become the full moon. There is no need for the part to remain away from its whole. It should go to the whole not to its opposite. Then you make yourself as the species of their genus and observe the secrets in their methods.

sections.heading: Praises of the Lowly and Slaps of the Great:
paras: In spite of being wise, you fall into the trap of others like women who get duped by false praises and pretensions. Do not go after false praises, pretensions and sweet pleasing words of treachery which you safely keep in your pocket like women. Slaps on your face and harsh abusive words from great men are more appropriate than the praises of the misguided. Receive the slaps from great men and not the honey from the mean fellows, so that you may become a man with the impacts of great men. It is from them that wealth and honor are obtainable. Their souls provide life to the body; and life becomes lively with their soul.

sections.heading: Runners Away from Great Men Are Destitutes:
paras: If you see destitutes and deprived, you may think that they have run away from the masters. They ran away from the masters because they wanted the masters to tow their line and do what they wanted. This was their misfortune and blindness. Were they to do what the masters wanted them to do, they would have reformed themselves and others. Consider that fellow, who runs away from the masters, as one who has run away from wealth. You have learnt a profession to make an earning for the body; now you may put efforts to learn something for the soul and faith. You were impotent in the world and kept yourself in hiding. Think as to what your fate will be when you go out of this world. Learn a profession through which you can get relief and earning in the next world. That is a city which is full of bazaars and profits; and do not be under the impression that all this is in this world alone.

sections.heading: Love: Nonperishable Earning of Other Life:
paras: God has said that earnings of this world are like the earnings from the games of children (who play with glass marbles and shattered clay-pieces) in comparison with the earnings of that world. It is like a child’s caressing of another child in imitation to the elders making love. Children open shops in their games. It is for no other purpose than to pass time. At nightfall, other children, one by one go to their homes with hunger leaving you alone. This world is a playground and death is a nightfall. From this, you go to the home of your grave, tired and empty-handed, with all regrets and griefs.

Earning of the faith is love, which is an inner absorption; and ability to make it is from the light of God. The mean self of yours, desires for perishable earnings. Do not go after it for longer time and stop at that level. Be also sure that even if sensory self makes a demand for good earnings, it would be a treachery with ulterior motives behind your back.

It is reported from the life of H.Mu‘awiah, that the maternal uncle of Muslims, was sleeping in his palace one night. (Maternal uncle: as he was the brother of H. Umme Habeeba, the Prophet’s wife. Since the Prophet’s wives are the mothers of the Muslims, their brothers are their maternal uncles and as H. Mu‘awiah is her brother, so he is the maternal uncle of Muslims). The door of the palace was bolted from inside as he did not want to see anybody, being tired for having talked to many people for the whole day in connection with the affairs of the state. All of a sudden, someone woke him up from sleep, and upon the opening of his eyes, that man hid himself. He said to himself: “There is no way for anyone to enter. Who could be that disobedient fellow, who dared to enter?” He moved around and searched to find the invisible person. Behind the door, he saw a person with his back toward him, hiding his face behind the curtain. He warned him and said: “Who are you? What is your name?” He replied: “My name is Iblis, the well-known accursed one.”

He asked him: “Why did you try to wake me up? Tell me the truth, and do not be evasive and confusing.” He said: “The closing time for the prayer was approaching and one had to run toward the masjid. The Prophet has said to hurry up for obedience to command before the passing off of time. He has stinged the pearls of meanings through this statement.”

H.Mu‘awiah said: “No No. This cannot be your object that you should guide me for good. It is not possible that the thief should enter into my house and tell me that he is doing the watchman’s job. How can I believe his words? A thief cannot know of doing a job for reward and gain. In particular, a thief like you, as you are a highway robber. Why did you show your kindness to me?”

sections.heading: Iblis Remembers God’s Graces upon Him:
paras: He said: “I was earlier an angel and performed my obediences with all my heart and soul. I was the teacher for the other angels. I was the secret bearer of the searchers of God and a companion of the beings of the ‘Arsh. The love for earlier profession cannot vanish from the heart; so also, the love of the first occasion. Whether you see the cities of Rome or of China on your journey, the love of your country does not vanish from the heart. We are also among those who have drunk the wine of God’s love and been the lovers of His great court. The very beginning of our life from birth itself was for His love and the seed of His love is sowed into our heart. We have seen good times of the days and drunk the water of mercy during the spring season. Was it not the hand of His benevolence that brought us up? Was it not He that brought us into existence from ‘adam (non-existence)? We have seen very many grants from Him and walked along in the garden of His consonance and acceptance. He used to keep the hand of His affection upon our head and look at us with concern. When I was drinking milk in my childhood, He used to rock my cradle. Whose milk have I drunk other than His? What else has reared me other than His care? The habit that has entered into someone along with the milk of childhood cannot be kept away. The river of His grants has gone angry with me, but the doors of His grace cannot remain closed. The coin of His benevolence and grant is so pure and thick that His wrath upon it is thin like a layer of dust. As a consequence of His benevolence, He has created this world and granted particles of light to the sun. If His separation from me is a result of His anger, it is only to make me aware of the value of togetherness. When His separation rubs the ears of soul, the soul comes to know of the worth of togetherness.

sections.heading: Permanent Benevolence, Temporary Anger:
paras: The noble Prophet has said: “God said, that My intention in the matter of creation is to show My benevolence and goodness. I have created them so that my creatures may seek benefits from Me, so that they may put their hands into My honey. It is not to get any gain from them. Where is the garment on a naked man, which I can remove?” Iblis continued: “He has chased me away from Him for a few days. Yet my eyes are set upon His face since then, as I have all hopes to regain my lost position. When God, out of His resentment causes something which makes a man feel aggrieved, He looks at the causes. But I do not look at the cause but at God alone, who is the Causer. I know that this Causer is the cause of causes for my troubles. Kindness is the inherent quality of God and resentment is subsequent and temporary. I look at His kindness and ignore His resentment.

sections.heading: Jealousy: Product of Excessive Love:
paras: “I know that I did not prostrate to Adam and this was done out to my jealousy; and jealousy came about out of my love for God and not out of deliberation and evil intention. Jealousy of this kind with increased love for the beloved came about due to the nearness of another to the beloved. Jealousy is an inevitable consequence of friendship and love. When they are taken over by others, it is just as saying, ‘May God’s mercy be on you!’ after sneezing. When only one game was left upon the chess board of my fate as decided by God and nothing else remained, I had no option left other than to play that last game. I played that game and got myself caught in misery. I enjoy even this misery as I am defeated by Him and not by others. Getting defeated by the greater is better than winning over the weaker. How can any chessman escape when it is caught between all the squares? So also, man caught in the six dimensions of space, where he is a part of it, has no means to go out of them. This is the game played by God. One caught in the fire of six dimensions cannot get out of them other than through one’s Creator. Whether infidelity or faith; they are made by His court and are His slaves."

H. Amir Mu‘awiah said: “All that is correct, but there is no participation of yours in this. You have misguided lakhs like me. You have broken the house for treasure. You are fire and you cannot do anything other than burning. Who is there whose clothes you have not torne. As setting fire is your nature, you cannot do anything other than this. The curse of God upon you has made you a burner and master of thieves. When you were such as to enter into arguments with God, of what worth am I for your treachery. Your talking about the gnosis and greatness of God is like the whistling of the bird-catchers who mimic the sounds of birds to bring down the birds on the ground to their nets from the air under their impression that one of their flock is calling for help! And they get trapped. This whistling sound has fooled many a persons.

sections.heading: Long Cherished History of Destruction:
paras: “The people of the days of H. Noah were destroyed and their hearts burned and broke into pieces. You brought destruction upon the people of ‘Aad by getting them involved in punishments and pains. The people of H. Lot became victims of falling rocks and stones and compelled to dive into rotting stagnant water. The brain of Nimrod shattered into pieces because of you. You have raised thousands of mischiefs. The wise philosophic mind of Pharaoh became foolish and failed to understand you. Abu Lahab became worthless because of you; and the masterly wiseman, Abul Hikam, became a father of ignorance, Abu Jahl, because of you. You have defeated lakhs of expert players on the chessboard of your tricks. With the entrapping of your bishop on the chessboard, many hearts burned and got blackened. You are an ocean of treachery and all people are a drop of it. You are like a mountain and all people are like particles before it. O quarrelsome fellow, who can escape from your treachery of drowning in ocean, except the one wished otherwise by God? Many bright stars have become black, because of you and many troops of the armies got scattered by you. Many innocent faithfuls lost their faith and are running about upturned in the depths of hell. Many a wise, pious men like Bal‘aam Bevoor and recluses like Barsisa became your victims, got frustrated and turned into infidels by you”.

Iblis said: “Unknot all these knots. Know this, I am only a tester for the true and false. God has made me a tester between the lion and dog. He has made me the separator of the genuine from non-genuine. I have never blackened the non-genuine. (It is black on its own). I am only a tester of gold and I decide its worth only. I guide the virtuous and also lead the vicious. I am a leader and peace provider for the good, but I have friendship with the bad as well. I am a garden, and as such, I take care of the green branch of the tree and also of the cut off dry branches.

sections.heading: Virtues and Vices, Not Made by Iblis:
paras: “When I put grass before an animal, it is to test it to see as to of what kind it is. If a bitch delivers a baby of deer, a doubt arises whether the youngling is a dog or deer. I put grass and bones before it, to see to which side it goes. If it goes towards the bone, it is a dog; and if towards grass, it is certain to be deer. God’s mercy and wrath go together and it is through them that the world of good and bad has come about. You may place grass and bone before the man’s self and provide the food for his body and food for the soul. If he takes the food for his body, he is vicious; and if he takes the food for the soul, he is good. If he serves his body, he is an ass; and if he enters into the sea of the soul, he gets pearls. Though good and bad are different from each other, yet both are engaged in the same work. Prophets present obedience before the people and the enemies of faith present sensuous desires. How can I convert virtue into vice? I am not God. God alone can do it. I invite the people to the vice which also is a creation of God. I am not the creator of vices. I cannot convert good into vice. I am not God. Only God can do it. I am just a mirror to show good and bad. If a black fellow gets angry with his blackness and blows air from his mouth in anger upon the mirror as to why it is reflecting its black face, what is the mirror’s fault. The mirror will say: “It is not a mistake on my part. Find fault with the one who has polished me to be a reflector. He has made me a tale bearer and truthful so as to say who is beautiful and who is ugly. I am only a witness; and there is no prison for a witness. I am not a prisoner. God is a witness to this effect.

sections.heading: Difference Between Acquired Character and Instinct:
paras: “Wherever I see a fruit-bearing tree, I take care of it. I am like a wet nurse for the tree and I take care of it like her. And wherever, I see a bitter and dry tree, I cut it off to protect the surroundings of ill effects. A dry tree tells the gardener: “Why do you cut off my head for no wrong by me”. The gardener tells it: “Keep quiet, O uncultured fellow! Is not your becoming dry a sin?” The dry tree says: “But I am straight. I am not crooked. You are unnecessarily cutting off my roots for no fault of mine”. The gardener tells: “You are unfortunate. It was better for you to be crooked than to be dry. A crooked tree is capable of absorbing the water of life but a dry one is not. Had you been green you would have remained sunk in the water of life. Your root and foundation were wrong and therefore, you had nothing to do with a good tree. If a bitter branch is grafted with a good branch, it becomes good with the impacts of the good branch. A good thing put its impact on bad things. A man of bad conduct can be rectified but not one of a bad instinct.

If I have woken you up from sleep for the sake of faith, it is for the reason that, that conduct is my base and instinct. You can accept my reasoning in this matter that I am good with the good and bad with the bad.”

H. Mu‘awiah angrily retorted: “O Dacoit! Do not argue falsely. You do not have a way for you in me. Do not search for it. You are a dacoit and I am a merchant on journey. You cannot come in disguise to me. Do not try to move around my merchandise with evil intentions posing yourself as a buyer. You are not a buyer of anybody’s materials. Dacoits do not buy; they loot. If they project themselves as buyers, it is only trickery and treachery.”

H.Mu‘awiah said to God: “It cannot be understood as to what trick he is playing. O God! Hear our complaints against the enemy. If I again argue with this dacoit, he will take away my dervish’s rough woolen garment. O God! His words are like smoke. Help me, as otherwise my blanket will go black. I cannot win over Iblis in arguments, as he is dangerous to every noble and meanly person. H. Adam who is the leader of all knowers of sciences was slow in speed against this dog with lightning speed. He got him thrown down from paradise to earth. He fell down and got trapped by his fish hook. He cried: ‘Our Lord! We have wronged our own souls’: "Rabbanaa zhalamnaa anfusanaa”: (A'raf: 7: 23). There is no limit to his treacheries and magic spells. In every word of his, there are mischiefs and lakhs of magic spells are hidden in them. In one blow from his mouth, he ties up the bravery of brave men and arises, vile passions in both men and women.

“O devil, destroyer of the people, full of mischief, tell me the truth. Why did you wake me up from sleep? Your excuses cannot have any effect upon me. Be warned! Tell me clearly the purpose of your waking me up!”

Iblis said: “A suspicious person will not accept the truth even if he is provided with hundred evidences. A person with suspicions within his inside will have his suspicions further increased with more arguments. When arguments enter into him, they make him sick. The sword of a mujahid fighting for a great cause becomes the weapon of the thief. In such a case the answer for his suspicions is silence and avoidance of arguments, as he is held up in the prison of doubts. O simpleton! What complaints you have against me before God. Do not complain to God. Complain to your own mean vicious self. If you eat too much of sweet, sores will develop on your skin; you will get fever and become sick.

sections.heading: Man Curses Satan, but Obeys His Self:
paras: “Without any mistake from him, you curse upon Iblis. Why do you not think of the mischief emanating from your own self. All these things are not from Iblis, but from your own self, as you are going toward a lamb like the wolf. By looking at the lamb surrounded by green grass, you never think that the greenery you see might be a trap. You do not think as such, because your wisdom has gone away from you. Craze for the lamb has blinded your wisdom. Greed of things makes you blind and deaf. What happens to you is by your own vicious self”.

Iblis continued: “Don’t look at me with cross-eyes. I’m disgusted of vices, greed and meanness. I agree that I had committed a wrong for which I feel ashamed even now. I am still awaiting to see that my autumn is converted into spring. Greed and ill will are the products of the things made out of the four fundamental elements − earth, water, air and fire. You (men) are all surrounded by them. But I am not made of these four elements and not surrounded by them. I also hope to be relieved of pain and injury and be pardoned of the wrongs done by me; and wait on to see when my dark night would change into bright day. I am disgraced by all men and women and all put the blame of their mistakes upon me. A fat wolf is straightening itself due to hunger, but onlookers disgrace it saying that it has eaten too much fatty food and therefore trying hard to digest. As it is not in a position to walk due to hunger, people say, it is sick of indigestion due to over eating.”

H.Mu‘awiah said: “You cannot get riddance from me other than by telling the truth. Justice is calling upon you to tell the truth. Tell the truth so that you may go out of my grip. Treachery cannot set at rest the storm of my fight”. Iblis said: “How can you differentiate between truth and falsehood when you are full of doubts and suspicions?” H. Mu’awiah said: “The noble Prophet has told us of the signs of truth and falsehood and fixed a yardstick. He has said: ‘Falsehood causes doubts in the minds and truth spreads a pleasure of joy and contentment.’

sections.heading: Impacts of Truth and Falsehood:
paras: Falsehood does not provide satisfaction to the heart. Water and oil mixed together do not give bright light to the lamp. Truth provides peace to the heart. Truths are the grains spread over the net of heart except of a heart that is sick. When the taste of one’s mouth is spoiled, one does not feel the taste of this and that.
