When the heart is protected and safe from sickness and consequent pains, it becomes aware of the taste of the truth and falsehood.

“As H. Adam’s greed had moved towards wheat grains, it took away the safety and security of the heart. Therefore, he heard of your falsehood and treachery and got trapped and drank mortal poison. He could not differentiate between wheat grains and scorpions, as greed had made him semiconscious and spoiled his discriminating faculty. People are unconscious in desires and greed and therefore, accept your treacheries as real. One, who got rid of the quality of greed, enabled one’s ear to be familiar with the secrets. You may hear now, as people have narrated this story so as to be able to open this knot.”

A person upon being appointed as a Qazi (judge) started weeping. His assistant asked the reason for crying and said that, it was not a time of crying but of rejoicing and prosperity. The Qazi said: “How can an ignorant person pass a judgment between two litigants, who are well aware of facts. The two fellows know very well about their respective facts; and how can the judge, unaware of these facts, solve their case? He is ignorant and unaware of their affairs. How can he interfere into the affairs of their lives and property?”

sections.heading: Selflessness Shows the Truth:
paras: His assistant said: “The two litigants are well aware of each other’s rights, but they are overtaken by selfishness. But you are not ignorant, and you are the lamp of the community. As you do not have any personal interest in their claims, your eyes are bright enough to see the truth. Impartiality gives greatness to wisdom. Both these well- aware-litigants are blinded by their self-interest and their knowledge is buried under self-interest. Selflessness converts ignorance into knowledge; and selfishness converts knowledge into cruelty and crookedness. So long as you do not take bribe, you are bright-sighted and know the truth, and upon taking bribe, you become blind and a slave of your vicious self.”

H. Mu‘awiah said to Iblis: “I have separated greed from me. I have not eaten many morsels of sensuous desires, and eaten within required permissible limits. My heart, full of God’s knowledge, has become so bright that I can separate truth from falsehood.”

H. Mu‘awiah continued: “O accused dog, give the answer to my question. Tell me the truth and do not search for lies. Tell me, why you woke me up. You are personified treachery and the enemy of people’s awakening. Like poppy seeds and their extract, you bring about sleep; and like wine, you spoil wisdom and intelligence. I have tied you on the wooden board and hit nails upon you hands and feet. You cannot escape from me. Tell me the truth and do not give excuses. I expect from every man only that which is as per his nature and habit. I do not search for sweetness in sour vinegar. I do not take a eunuch as my soldier. I do not search for godhood or godly signs in the idols like the infidels. I do not search for the fragrance of musk in dung. I do not search for a dry brick in water. I do not want a thief as my watchman. I do not expect Satan to do good to me as he is an alien. He cannot wake me up from sleep for my good.”

Iblis tried further to avoid a direct answer but the leader of the faithful did not accept but rejected and insisted. At last, Iblis humbled himself before the Amir and said: “I woke you up so that you may join the congregational prayer following the practice of the messenger of God, the increaser of all prosperity. Were you to lose the congregational prayer, this world would have become dark and unattractive for you. Out of loss and pain you would shed tears from your eyes like water dropping from the goatskin. Everyone has a taste for worship. He remains restless upon its non-performance in time. Your loss in this manner would provide two hundred times of reward. Where is the reward for prayer and where is the reward for this sense of sorrow and humility upon its loss?”

A person was about to enter the masjid and found that people were coming out. He asked one of them as to what happened to the congregation that people are going out. He said: “The noble Prophet concluded the salat and finished the supplication. Where are you going now, O imperfect one, when the Prophet has already turned toward the last salutation (salaam)”

That man took a long sigh, which revealed the feelings of his pain, and it gave a fragrance of the blood of his heart. That man told him: “Give this sigh to me and I give my salat to you.” The first man agreed and said: “I give my sigh to you and accept your salat for me.” He took that long sigh full of hundreds of devotions and humilities. He returned with humilities and submissions. He went as a falcon and now returned as a royal falcon.

In his dream, he heard the voice of an invisible angel (haatif), telling him: “You have purchased the life-giving-water and medicine. Because of this appreciation by that man and in his honor, the salat of all others was accepted.”

chapters.title: Sighs of Deprivation Greater Than Thanks

paras: Then, ‘Azaazil, (the original name of Iblis before his fall) said: “O wise leader, I should speak to you of my treachery clearly. If your salat in time were to be lost, you would have had great pain, cries and sighs of heart. That regretting, lamentation and groaning would have rewarded two hundred times of normal reward to you. I woke you up fearing that the heat of your sighs may not set on fire the curtain between you and God. You should not get such a sigh which would provide that path to you towards God, which can be seen only in the light of such groanings and sighs. I am jealous, and out of my jealousy I did not like that. I am an enemy of good and my job is treachery and showing of ill will. Now that you have seen my treachery, yet you may not remain contented and at rest with it, so that you may lead the entire world.”

Then, H. Mu‘awiah said: “Now, you have told the truth. You could do only this much and you are capable of that alone. You are a spider and you can catch only a fly. But you doggish fellow! Know this! I am not a fly. I am a white falcon, which can be caught only by a king. Spider cannot go around me. O you meanly thief, you can only do this much. You can take the fly from honey towards buttermilk. Go on and catch the flies as long as you can and call the flies towards butter milk. And if you call them towards honey, that would also be a false pretext and trick towards buttermilk. You woke me up from what was a sleep, in order to deprive me of a greater reward which I would have got by crying and sighing, if I had not woken up. You showed a whirlpool to me as a boat. You called me towards good in order to keep me away from better.”

chapters.title: Exchange of Jute Fabric for Woolen Fabric

paras: Satan’s waking up of H.Mu‘awiah is like this illustration:

A man found a thief in his house and he started running after him. Up to two-three fields he ran after him and the thief due to his continuous running to escape got sunk in his sweat. The house owner went very near to the thief and was about to catch him, when another thief called at him to come to him to see the markings of the thief to lead him to the thief. He told him to come fast so as to see every detail of the thief. Upon hearing this, the house-owner felt himself in suspense and said to himself, to consider the thief as virtually dead and feared that another thief might be on the other side, and at any moment, he might pounce upon on him, if he did not go away fast. That thief may extend his hand upon his wife and children. It is more proper to go towards the nearer thief. This Muslim is calling out of his concern for me and I shall be put to shame if I do not go towards him fast. Upon the hope of that well-wisher, he left free the thief and returned to his place. He asked the caller: “What is the matter? What for you are shouting and calling like this?” He said: “Look at the foot prints of that fellow living upon the immoral earnings of his wife. He is a mean shameless procurer of customers to his wife. Look at these foot prints and go after him under their guidance.”

sections.heading: Markings Not Needed, When Object Is at Hand:
paras: The house-owner said: “What nonsense are you talking about, you fool! I had virtually caught hold of that thief. Because of your calling, I left him free. It is my fault that I considered an ass like you as man. What a great nonsense and foolery. When the real person is caught, what and where is the need of his markings.”
That fellow said: “I am showing the true symptoms. These are the markings. I am well aware of them.”

The house-owner said: “You are a pick pocket, or you are mad. Rather, you are also a thief, well aware of that thief. I would have caught hold of my enemy’s hair and dragged him, and you got him released to show his markings. You are talking of the causes and paths, when I have already gone ahead of them. When you have already reached your object, where is the need for markings that lead to the object and to argue over them. He looks at the actions of God, who is not aware of His attributes and qualities, because study of His actions leads to His qualities, potentialities and attributes. And the one is held up in attributes only is a prisoner of attributes, who has not seen His essence.”

sections.heading: Those in Essence of God, Do Not Need Attributes:
paras: Therefore, those who have reached Him and are close to Him are sunk in His essence. They do not look at His attributes. When you have already dived deep to the depth of the stream, you do not concern yourself with the colour of the stream’s water. If you bring out information about the colour of water, it is like exchanging jute fabric for a woolen fabric. Obediences of the common people are the sins of the great men. Closeness with God of the common people is like a curtain for the elevated ones. “Hasanaatul abraari sa’iyaatul muqarribin”.

If a minister is posted as a police officer by the king, it means that the king is displeased with him. Certainly, the minister might have done some wrong and the change can never be without reason. For one who was already in police force from the beginning, this position is a matter of his fortune and honour. On the contrary for the one who was a king’s minister, this position is degradation and a penalty for some wrong. If you are called at the king’s place from the door and again sent back, it means that there is something wrong with you. You take a plea of fate or predestination in this regard with your ignorance that, it was already predestined. You do not think as to upon what reason, you were at a respectable status till yesterday. You have spoiled your own share by your mistakes. An efficient person increases his share with his own efforts. There is another example of the wrong behavior. You may hear about this from the statements in the Quran.

In a particular manner of hide-and-seek game, the hypocrites played tricks with the Prophet saying: “O Muhammed, for the honour of the religion we would construct a masjid.” But, in fact, they were turning back from the religion. In this manner they spoke of untenable arguments, and they constructed another masjid apart from the Prophet’s masjid. They made a floor, roof and dome of the masjid and through this they wanted to divide the community. They came over to the Prophet and sat before him on their knees as the camel sits, and said: “O Prophet of God! Be kind to us by visiting this masjid so that it may become prosperous and that your name may remain on top till the doomsday. This masjid is for the rainy and slushy season and for the occasion of needs and difficulties so that travelers may stay here and rest. So also, that on its model more such places may come about. So that, the principles of the religion may increase and fill the surroundings. When friends assemble, their discussions will turn bitterness into sweetness. Please sit there for some time, purify us and teach us about the worth and value of faith. You may grace the masjid and those connected with it. We are like a dark night and you may be with us for some time like the bright moon, so that, with your beauty, the night may get converted into a bright day. You are the one, whose beauty brightens the soul just as the sun brightens the world.”

sections.heading: Few Cowards Cause Defeat to the Army:
paras: Alas! Had these words been from the heart, they would have met the objects of these people. The word that comes to the mouth without the impressions of heart and soul, is like greenery on the garbage pit. You have to just look at it and pass off, as it is not worthy of sitting and smelling. Be careful! Do not go towards the sweet words of the dishonest. Remember well that they are like a crumbling bridge. If someone, without knowing about it, keeps his foot, it breaks itself and breaks that man’s leg also. Whenever an army meets defeat, it is due to two-three cowards and eunuchs. Such men carry the weapons and come forward boldly and the other soldiers believe them and take them as true friends. But when the coward sees some injuries, he turns his face and runs away causing a breakage of your back.
This narrative is getting lengthened and its object is getting forgotten.

The hypocrites recited many magic spells upon the Prophet, running the horses of treacheries and designs towards him. They flattered and entreated him with their magical words and extended their hospitality. The Prophet of mercy and kindness heard their statements, only with smiles and saying ‘yes, yes’. He thanked them and pleased their messengers as having received the message. Their treachery was clear before him, as clear as a hair appears in milk. The Prophet behaved as though he had not seen that hair and his dignity spoke well of the milk.

There were lakhs of hairs of treacheries and designs, but he kept his eyes shut at all of them. Rightly has that ocean of grace said: “I am more kind to you than your own selves. I sit beside fire, which is burning hot and full of blazing flames. You are flying towards it like moths and both my hands are chasing you away from it.”

sections.heading: Prophet Warned:
paras: The Prophet was about to ready himself to go to the masjid, a voice from God came: “Do not hear anything from the ghouls (a group of ghosts who hide themselves with leaves of various colours in forests and misguide people). These mischievous fellows have resorted to tricks and designs. What all they say is the opposite of what they intend. Their intention is nothing but blackening of faces. Christians and Jews never wish well of your religion. They have built a masjid on a bridge to hell. They have played a game of treachery with God. Their intention is to bring rift among your companions. A senseless fellow can never know of the graces of God. They intend to call that Jew from Syria, whose sermons are very well known to the Jews. [The Jew referred to here is Abu ‘Aamir, a resident of Madina, who earlier used to talk about the forecast in the Bible of the arrival of Prophet Muhammad. He was taken as a Christian priest after he converted to Christianity. After the Prophet’s migration from Makka to Madina, he was reluctant, and after the Muslim victory in the battle of Badr, he left Madina for Syria, where he settled and started conspiring with others against the Muslims ― Qazi Sajjad Hussain, Urdu translator of Mathnavi]

The Prophet said: “Yes! But we are going on a journey to Tabuk for jihad. After my return from there, I shall come over to that masjid.” In this manner he evaded the matter and played the game of chess with the treacherous people.

When he returned from the battle, the hypocrites reminded him of his promise. Then, God told him: “O Prophet! Tell them clearly. Seek no excuse. Does not matter if they resort to fight. Be prepared and fight it out.” The Prophet told them: “O treacherous fellows! Be quiet, so that I may not reveal your secret intentions. I am not coming over to you. Forget me once and for all.”

sections.heading: Swearing: a Shield of the Lies:
paras: When the Prophet revealed to them of some of their intentions, their design got upset. The messengers went away from him. Sometime later, they again came back with the Quran held under their armpits saying: “May God help us! May God help us”. They all came and swore upon God to impress upon him of their sincerity, projecting swearing as a defensive shield. Swearing was a part of their bad habit. Such people without sincerity break their oaths every time. Truthful people do not need the support of oaths, as both of their eyes are bright exposers of truth. Breach of promise and covenants is actually foolishness. Acting according to promises is what the pious people do.

The Prophet asked: “Should I believe your oaths or the words of God?” The people once again swore with the Quran in their hands, adding, they were fasting as well. We swear upon this true and clear book of God, the construction of the masjid is for the sake of God. There is no trick and design behind it. Our intention in this is nothing but upholding of truth, and remembrance of God and saying: “O our Lord.”

The prophet said: “God’s voice is clearly coming to my ears and repeating like an echo. God has put a seal upon your ears, so that you may not learn from God’s voice. The voice clearly comes to me. It completely cleans me like filtered water free of residue. This is as clear as H. Musa Kaleemullah had heard from the tree, which he clearly heard: ‘O fortunate one! Verily, I am God’: “Innani anallaah”: (Taahaa: 20: 14). Lights were shed along with this calling.

Upon feeling humble before the light of inspiration, the hypocrites used to feel humbled, yet they used fresh swearing. When God has called an oath as a shield, how can a fighter give up the shield as the Quran says: ‘They have made their oaths as a screen (for their misdeeds)’: “Ittakhazoo aymaanahum junnatan”: (Mujaadilah: 58: 16)

One of the companions of the Prophet got an insinuation in his mind in the matter of the Prophet’s not believing the oath. These elderly respected people are being put to shame by the Prophet. Why his generosity, honour and grace are not shown to them. Prophets have been putting curtains upon lakhs of defects. Yet again, the companion questioned his own heart and repented, so that he might not be put to shame before God. But this crooked impression did not go out of his mind in full. Love for the vicious people did not go out of his heart completely. The ill-effects of love for the hypocrites did have their accursed impacts which made faithful Muslims also bad and disobedient like them.

sections.heading: Faithful and Hypocrites Differentiated:
paras: Later, that companion cried calling upon God: “O knower of the secrets, do not keep me insisting upon this kind of infidelity. My heart is not within my control just as eyes also are not, as otherwise I would have set fire to my heart in my anger.” With these conflicts into his heart, he got into sleep and in it, he happened to see that mosque in dream. He found it to be full of dung and filth. Its stones were in a dirty place due to their uncleanliness and black smoke was emanating from them. It went into his mouth and injured his throat. He instantly fell in prostration telling: “O God! These are the signs of denials. It is better to be angry on such matters than to have self-control, which is separating me from faith.”

If you go on scratching the faith of the namesake worldly Muslims, they would appear like the foul-smelling concentric layers of onions. Every layer will be with more foulness than the other. The layer of the true people will be more meaningful than that of others.

That group of people had strengthened with hundred types of treacheries, because of hypocrisy, falsehood and imperfect faith. It had covered up itself with hundred types of garments upon its back in order to destroy the masjid of the people of Quba. [This was a masjid built by the Prophet in the village of Quba, nearby to Madina, where he had settled for some time]. The hypocrites were making efforts to destroy this. Like the people of the elephant, the people of Abyssinia, who had constructed a ka‘aba in their country as a rival to the Ka‘aba at Makka, which was set on fire by God. What happened to them may be read in the Quran in Surah, Al-fiil (S: 105). They had come over to Makka to destroy the Ka‘aba, to avenge the destruction of their ka‘aba. The possessions of the blackened faces of the opponents of faith are nothing but treacheries, designs and fights.

sections.heading: Prophet’s Companions Had No Doubts:
paras: There were some other companions also who had similar suspicions. They also saw the masjid in similar dreams. This went on to such an extent that everyone was fully convinced of the correctness of the Prophet’s stand. If I go on explaining the affairs of all these people, those in doubts will be fully convinced. But I am afraid of revealing their secrets. The companions were men of very subtle feelings and observations. It was alright for them to have some doubts. They had accepted the law in a simple manner as simple people. Their faith was that which they got simply by taking it as was given by the Prophet. They were passers of faith and not its inheritors. They took it without putting its provisions to test and trial. As the wisdom of the Quran is the lost treasure of the faithful, they very clearly identified their lost treasure without seeking evidences as every man easily identifies his materials, which are regained by him after having been lost.

You have lost your camel and are searching for it. When it is found out by you, you will certainly identify it as yours. What was it that you have lost? It was a she-camel which went away from your hand and was lost and unseen. The caravan was readying itself to load materials when your camel was out of sight. You were in search of it with dry lips here and there as the caravan had gone much farther and the night was approaching. Your materials were lying on the road. Full of fears, you were searching for the camel, pleading to the people: “O Muslims! Has anyone of you seen my camel, which left me after taking its morning meal. Whoever gives me its location, will be rewarded so many dirhams by me”. Then, you go on asking everyone about the camel’s location, upon which every mean fellow laughs at you. One tells: “I have seen a camel which was going that way. A red camel was going toward the forest.” Another says: “It has only one ear, the other one is cut off.” Another was saying: “It was wearing a decorated saddle.” Another was telling: “It is one-eyed,” and another said: “It had no hair on its body due to scabies.” In order to get the reward, every mean fellow spoke of a hundred marks of the camel.

All this is said to insist that everyone is uninformed and misguided. This is a usual common matter. It is not a secret. Everyone knows this fact. If you are destined to know the truth of matters, you will take it as delicious food. Everyone speaks of some attributes of God as though he alone knows them and these are not known to others. Because God is hidden from all.

The philosopher explains about God in a different manner. The dialectician criticizes his arguments. The sufis find fault with both. The others are confused variously. Everyone presents his conclusions in such a way that everyone should accept him as correct.

[The philosopher says that essence of God is absolute and all attributes to Him are only imaginations and unsubstantial. Scholastic theologians say that He has some attributes but they differ with each other in some attributes of physical nature, like hands, face etc. The well-versed sufis accept all attributes, but do not try to explain their specificities. And the rest are those who claim to know about God, but do not really know, but only claim ― As explained by Urdu translator, Qazi Sajjad Hussain.]

sections.heading: Truth Not Knowable Without Falsity:
paras: But you should know that all these people are neither true in full nor totally wrong. Some are right and some are wrong. Because truth cannot be explained without reference to falsity. Every untruth has some element of truth within it. Common people expend counterfeits in the hope of connecting them into genuine ones. A counterfeit certainly has some element or other of genuineness. Had there been no genuine coins in use in the world, why the counterfeits would come. So long as there is no truth, there cannot be untruth. Untruth has to be identified by comparing with truth. Falsity spreads through truth. People buy the crooked things in the hope of them as straight. People eat poison when it is mixed up with sugar. Where there is no tasty wheat, what are we to do with those who sell millet as wheat.

sections.heading: Lailatul Qadr Hidden in Other Nights:
paras: Therefore, do not call these beliefs as false. Falsities are the traps of the heart because of their being mixed up with the fragrance of truths. Therefore, do not say that all these are mere imaginations and misguidance. There cannot be imagination in the world without there being realities. Truth is hidden in untruth just as the Night of Power (Lailatul Qadr) is hidden in other nights, and that is hidden, so that you may search for it in other nights. Know this that all nights are not the Nights of Power, nor that all nights are devoid of it. Among those who wear the garments of wool, there are some real faqirs, though the rest are only self-projectors as real. Therefore, carry a test on them and find out the real and hold on to him. It is the duty of the wise, faithful person to differentiate and identify the real king of faqr from beggars.

sections.heading: Defects Needed to Certify Merit:
paras: Had there been no defective things in the world, all fools would have become merchants as identifying the commodities would be very easy. When there are no defective commodities, there cannot be a difference between the competents and incompetents. If everything is defective, then - there is no need for wisdom to play its role. If every wood is the same, there is no value for agarwood. One who says that all are true, is foolish; and one who says that all are false is untrue and unfortunate.

Those who carry on the trade of the instructions of the prophets are real profiteers; and merchants of material things are blind and deaf. A worldly man who considers the worldly things only should rub his eyes, clear them and see that these things are snakes. Have proper sense and penetrate deep into them to see whether they are really profit-giving. Consider the losses that Pharoah and Th(s)amud have undergone.

chapters.title: Trials by God to Cause Perfection

paras: Look at the sky for two times as God has said: ‘Again turn your vision a second time’: “Th(s)ummarji’il basra karratain”: (Mulk: 67: 4). Do not remain satisfied with one vision on this roof full of lights (sky). Look again and again to see whether there is any flaw in it, “Hal tara min futūr”: (Mulk: 67: 3). As He has asked you to look at this subtle and nice roof, look at it again and again like a searcher of defects. Such being the case with plane sky, think as to how many times you will have to look at the dark, hard, rough and rugged earth to know, appreciate and depreciate it. These are the things that are out of your body. Consider the difficulties involved, use of wisdom and elaborate efforts required to remove the crudeness of character and conduct within your body to make them clean.

sections.heading: Earth Undergoes Many Trials:
paras: Earth is involved in so many trials like those of the cold of winter and heat of summer, pleasing spring and harsh autumn. Winds, clouds and lightnings are the trials upon it so that the differences of accidents upon its substance may become clear, so as to remove its clayish colour and bring forth from its hidden pockets rubies and stones and also what all that its sullen clay has stolen from the treasuries of God and the oceans of His grace. The police officer of fate tells it to tell the truth of its treacheries and thefts in detail, so that under the impacts of its persuasive and threatening police-tactics resulting in the fire of hope and despair, all materials hidden by it may come out. Spring season comes as the persuation of that police officer and autumn as his threats and warnings. Winter season comes as a virtual wooden board of punishment upon which the criminal is lain with the hands and feet tied to nails causing severe pain so that the hidden thief may be exposed.

sections.heading: Austerities for Trial of Body:
paras: In a similar manner, one who performs austerities and hardship on the body receives a situation of expansion of his soul at one time, when he feels great elation of soul and at another time, constriction of the soul and consequent spiritual pain, deficiency and hopelessness. These situations are like the situations of spring and autumn on the body which are similar those on earth. This is because our body is made of earth and water. And these are deprivers of the essence of the soul and its light just as thieves do with the owner of goods.

sections.heading: Trials by God for Our Good
paras: God puts heat, cold, pain and sorrow upon our bodies. And also imposes hunger, fear and reduction of material possessions and sicknesses so that the worth of our soul may be exposed. He has issued warnings of the torture of hell and given promises of heavenly pleasure to make us self-conscious in a proper manner as He has kept good and bad intertwined together. He has mixed up truth and falsities; and so also the genuine and counterfeit together, and put them all together in a leather bag (of the body). He has also given to us the tester of these things as wisdom, which can identify the subtle and fine differences between them. We find other testers amongst ourselves with better and more mature wisdom in the form of guides. With these testers, man can find out the subtle differences between the intertwined and opposing qualities and sit upon them to tackle them properly like a prime minister. God had told H. Mūsā’s mother to give milk to the baby and put him in the river and have no fear for him.

sections.heading: ALAST: and Its Impacts and Example:
paras: In order to identify a proper guide, an inherent straight forward wisdom is required. [One who is aware of the covenant made by men with God in the very beginning itself when God asked all humans, well before they were born, whether or not He was their Lord. And all of them had replied ‘YES! We do accept You as our Lord to be obeyed’. This is called the covenant of ‘Alast’. One who has confidence and faith in this spiritual matter will always remember to do good things and avoid bad ones. ―Translator]

Such a person can have the inherent wisdom within him to identify a proper, competent guide, as there are pseudo guides also in the world. O mother of Musa, just make your baby taste your milk and put him in the river and do not worry about him. [That apart, one more special treatment is required for one such person to create the proper taste to know the truth; as had happened in the case of H. Musa. His mother fed him with her milk only once just after birth and put him in a box and in the river, leaving him to the care of God. As prophet Musa had tasted the milk of Alast (the first ever occasion) and remembered it inherently, he refused to drink the milk which had a different taste than that of his mother. Through a series of events, his mother was brought nearer to him to feed her milk. The covenant of Alast involved Mūsā’s birth, taste of mother’s milk, his being thrown into river, being picked up from it, being brought to Pharoah’s wife, providing the milk of his own mother, and bringing up in the royal palace and so on, and thereafter till the end of his life, are the special provisions made for him as he had to perform single-handedly one of the toughest acts in history. ― Translator].

sections.heading: Women: Causes of Great Men:
paras: One who has drunk the milk of Alast on the day of Alast will identify all things in their proper perspectives just as H.Mūsā did.

You can now very well understand that the purpose of all this is not to tell a story, but to make you informed of subtle matters in a lucid manner. O mother of Mūsā, give milk to your baby to make him identify the differences of milk from different women. So also, all mothers. Train up your babies from the earliest stage of life so as to be able to find out the difference between true and false guides, both of whom are the same in appearance but different in inner qualities. So that, he may enjoy the taste of your own milk (and upbringing) and refuse to take the milk of other wet-nurses.

chapters.title: Search and Recollection of the Truth

paras: O the one relying upon me! What will you do when you lose your camel? Everyone is pointing to some kind of identification of your camel. But you do not know where your camel is. And you also know that its identification marks they are telling about are wrong. [This is what happens in the case of a person in search of truth. One having an inherent wisdom and fragrance of the covenant of Alast does not get misguided. The owner was not misguided by the fellows who spoke of the identification marks of the camel. He went on searching]

sections.heading: False Pretenders of Learning:
paras: One who has not lost his camel also starts searching like the loser, only for fun or imitation saying: ‘I have also lost my camel and I shall reward anyone who finds it out’. This, he does only to imitate you and be one with you in searching. He is in the greed of an unseen camel. [There are persons who really do not need a guide to know the truth. They simply join a guide only to impress upon others that they are also curious to know the truth]. Such a person cannot find the difference between the right and wrong, but takes your words only as his guide to make himself at par with you. If you say that some identity is wrong, he accepts the same and becomes your follower. As against him, when someone tells you about the truth, you verify with your inherent sincere reasoning and accept it and believe in it. Such information becomes a medicine for your anxiety and exposes your rich and generous sense.

sections.heading: What Happens Under a True Guide:
paras: The color of the face brightens, and your muscles become stronger and your body and soul become hundred times more effective. Your feet start running and your eyes become brighter. Your body gets converted into animal soul with all physical potentialities, and later your animal soul gets converted into human soul, and your spiritual powers become more. [Animal soul controls the body of all living beings including man. But the human soul is provided to man only. Other animals do not have it. Matters relating to mind, thoughts, feelings, conscience, consciousness etc., which as special to humans are possessed, controlled and directed by the human soul].

When such true informations are provided to you by your guide, you tell him: “You are a true holder of trust. What all you say are true informations. They contain bright and reliable signs. They are from authentic records, worthy and means of deliverance. Now that you have spoken of the truth, hold on to my hand and proceed forward. You are a proper guide. I shall follow you. You have found out my lost camel. Take me to it and show it to me.”

sections.heading: Real Loser and Pretender Become One:
paras: As regards the one who is not a master of camel and has not lost it, search for the camel is just an imitation. The correct information about the unseen camel has not increased his confidence, excepting similar expression of confidence in imitation of the owner and loser of the camel. From the anxieties and struggles of the owner-loser of the camel, he feels only this much that the anxieties and struggles are not for fun but are real. This man had no share and interest of any kind in that camel, but in fact, he has also lost the camel of which he is not aware. His face was hidden behind the curtain of the anxiety of the camel-loser. He is a loser of the camel whereas this fellow has not lost but only forgotten his camel. He runs along with the loser and becomes his sympathizer in his own anxiety of his forgotten camel. (In like manner, an imitator of truth while going with a truthful person gets his imitation a little color of truth and he also goes along with him. A dull student becomes intelligent by imitating an intelligent and hardworking classmate). When the loser’s camel was found out in the desert, the other fellow also found out his forgotten camel. When he looked at the loser’s camel, he lost interest in the loser’s camel. From a blind follower, he became one who found out the truth as a researcher, upon seeing his forgotten camel also grazing in the desert. Instantly he also became a seeker of his lost camel. As long as he had not seen his forgotten camel, he was not anxious about it. After seeing his own camel, he left the company of the camel-loser and proceeded alone to catch his camel. And that became the object of his life. This is how an imitator of the searcher of God, in due course, himself becomes a searcher and follower of God and proceeds alone.

sections.heading: Vices Also Lead to Truth:
paras: The true loser told him: “You have left me. So far you have been with me”. He replied: “Till now I was an imitator, engaged in flattering and following you. Now, I am your sympathizer. I am separating myself from you as I want to search alone. All through, I was hiding the details of my camel, but now I have found out my object and I am fully satisfied. So long as I had not found it out, I did not desire for it. Now, my lowly copper is defeated and overtaken by more worthy gold. It is God’s grace upon me that my vices are converted into virtues. Many thanks! Fun has gone away and seriousness has replaced it. It were my vices that became the means of my going up to the truth. Therefore, do not find fault with vices. Your real desire compelled you to go in search, and you found out the truth. But in my case, it is my struggle and desire that explained the truth to me. [I had not lost anything, but I was only ignorant of it. While being with you I recalled to my mind as to what I was ignorant of and I am fully aware of it now].

“Your truthfulness engaged you in a search, but my searching took me to the truth. I sowed the seed of my fortune in the land which was useless and funny in my view. But now I found out that it was not wasteful but a real useful effort. For every seed that I sowed, a hundred plants sprouted from it. The thief stealthily entered the house and upon getting inside, he found that it was his own house.”

sections.heading: Words Cannot Explain: Heart Should Learn on Its Own:
paras: O the desperate one! Get up and be active in order to gain enthusiasm. Undergo hardship to gain comfort. We have talked of two camels: one, the lost one; and the other, forgotten one. They are not two but only one. Words are very narrow and limited, but meanings are wide and many. Words are always insufficient in the matter of explanations of the contents. That is why the noble Prophet said: ‘The tongue or language (or word) is a helper to explain things.” Another great man has said: ‘One who has understood his Lord becomes dumb. He cannot speak or explain.’ In the matter of understanding, words are like astrolabe, the instrument used to measure the distances of the stars. This instrument gives a rough estimate of the affairs of the heavens and stars, but cannot give all features in exactness. It does not know the affairs of the heavens and the sun. And, in particular, the astrolabe is deficient in explaining about this visible apparent heaven, which is just a scrap in spite of its vastness before that invisible heaven, of which this large sun is a tiny particle. Any number of words and explanations cannot encompass the reality of that invisible heaven.

When it was clear that it was not a masjid but a house of treachery and net of the Jews, the Prophet directed that it should be uprooted and converted into a heap of dust. The builder of the mosque, Abu ‘Aamir, the priest, was a trickster from the beginning. He was not a builder but a destroyer, but the etymological meaning of his name is ‘one who assembles people’. What he had done was not a generous act but an act of spreading of a net. The piece of flesh that you attach to the fish-hook is not to feed but a bait to catch the fish. Such a feeding is neither grant nor generosity. The masjid at Quba built by the Prophet was also made of stoney material, which also had no sense of feeling, but was not like the Masjid-e-Dhiraar. Lifeless materials cannot do such jobs of cruelty but the Great Commander, God, got sprinkled oil upon it. The truths of things are different. So also the truths of men, which are their fundamentals, are different. There is a vast difference between the one who gives and the one who receives. Even their lives and deaths are different. Even their graves are not to be taken as the same. When their cases have been different in this world itself, what can I say about the differences between them in the next world. Therefore, everyone should test his acts upon the results that come out of his acts. Be careful not to make a Masjid-e-Dhiraar. You have ridiculed upon the builders of that masjid, but if you think deeply into your acts, there are possibilities of these also being like that.

[The word ‘Hindus’ here means ‘Indian Muslims’ as the narrative explains. The word ‘Hindu’ is Persian: meaning black, thief, dacoit, black mole of the face and also India. It has been used in these different senses at the different places in the Math(s)navi. Here it is used to mean Indians. The context of they being in salat (the Islamic prayer) shows that Indian Muslims are meant by it ― Translator].

Four Hindus entered into a masjid to perform the prayer with bowings and prostrations. Everyone made the intention for it and started the prayer with Takbir and engaged himself in all humility and reverence Then the Mu’azzin entered into the masjid and one of them said: “O Mu’azzin, have you announced the azaan? What is the time now?”. The other Hindu said with devotion: “Oh you have spoken. This should not be done in salat. The continuity of the salat has broken”. The third said to the second: “My dear uncle! Why do you put a remark upon him? Put it upon yourself”. The fourth said: “May God be praised; I did not fall into the well like these three!”
The salat of all the four was lost for talking of matters not connected with salat. The finders of faults themselves went out of the way.

sections.heading: Search and Accept Your Own Defects:
paras: That man requires to be praised and appreciated who looks at his own faults himself and also accepts his own faults if pointed out by others. Because, half of himself is from this world full of defects and the other half is related to the unseen, hidden world. Therefore, one should look at one’s own faults. When you are having a hundred wounds upon your head, it is required that the soothing ointment is applied on them. Considering a wound as wound itself is its medicine as it is only upon this consideration that the treatment starts. This involves the consideration of yourself being as humble and weak seeking the mercy of others. When you accept your humbleness, you say, “take pity on me”. Even if you do not have defects, you should not remain at peace, as there is a possibility of the defects being known later. Have you not heard of God’s statement: ‘Fear you not’: “ala takhaafu”: (Fussilaat: 41: 30) for the faithful people. That is to say, those who are faithful ought not to consider themselves to be at peace and remain contented.

Satan led a long life with a good reputation as the teacher of the angels. Later, he got disgraced and came to be called Iblis. He was well known for his high status and, so regretfully for him, there was its opposite later.

sections.heading: Eliminate Fear, Become Strong and Then Talk of Peace:
paras: There is no scope for peace, contentment, honour and reputation in the world until you get out of fear. First eliminate fear and become strong and then talk of peace. O teenager! You can talk ill of the bearded chin only so long as you do not get the beard. Lack of a beard is a defect of manliness. Growth of the beard is inevitable. Do not make fun of the elderly with beard. Growth of beard is a merit and not a defect. Consider the defects in the other man, for a lesson for you to avoid them. Be thankful, that he has become a cause to learn a lesson from him and not you for him. He fell in a well and warned you of its danger. You have not fallen, as otherwise, you would have been a cause of caution for him. If he has taken a drink of poison, you may avoid it and drink a sweet syrup instead.

That blood-spilling Turkic Tribe of Ghuzaan made a surprise attack upon a village to loot the inhabitants. They caught hold of two great men of the village and attempted to kill one of them. They tied his hands to slaughter him. That man said: “O kings and great men! Why do you throw me in the well of death? Why are you thirsty for my blood? What reason is there in killing me, when I am poor and destitute?”

sections.heading: Take Lessons from Other’s Troubles:
paras: The Ghuzaan said: “To create fear in the other man, so that he may give us the clue of hidden money”. The victim said: “He is poorer than me”. The Ghuzaan said: “He has made himself poor. In fact, he is quite rich”. The victim said: “This is only your speculation and, in this speculation, both of us stand on the same footing. O king, you may kill him first, so that I may fall into fear and give you the clue about money”.

The misfortune of others becomes a cause of fear and warning for us. Look at this great grace of God upon us that we (Muslims) have come in the last days of the world. And, those of later days are much ahead of those of the earlier days. The prophet has said: “As a community we have come later in time to all other communities, but on the doomsday, we shall be in the forefront. (Nahnu Aakhirun al Saabiquun). So much so: the destruction of the communities of H.Noah and H. Huud created scope for the formation of the clouds of mercy upon us. They were destroyed so that we may fear and learn lessons. Had God done otherwise, you would have been destroyed.

Much has been said about the people by God with regards to their sins, their stoney hearts and black interiors. About their disregard for the commands of God, their carelessness about the doomsday; their love and craze for this mean world and obedience to the demands of their self like women in this matter. (Women are more self-centered than men). Their running away from advisers and refusal to meet the noble people. Their remaining without concern for the matters of heart, of the people of heart and their inner greatness; and their playing tricks like foxes with the kings of this and that world. Their consideration of the contented people as beggars and hidden enemies, because of their jealousy for them. Thus, the attitude of these people and their results are before you.

sections.heading: Pervert Conclusions:
paras: And you are no better than them. If you give something to someone and he accepts it, you call him a beggar; if not, you call him treacherous, trickster and liar. If he mingles with you, you think that he does so out of greed to take something from you; and if not, you say that he is inclined towards arrogance and pride. If he shows self-control upon provocation, you call him a coward and if he exhibits his self-respect, you consider him to be haughty.

sections.heading: Engaged in Self-Seeking Affairs:
paras: Or, like a hypocrite, you show excuses to do good things or say that you are involved in the maintenance of expenses of your wife and children saying: “ I do not have time even to scratch my head, nor do I have the occasion to get involved in religious matters.” And, you ask others to remember you in their prayers so that your end may also be like that of the saints. Even this is not said with sincerity, with feelings of pain and burning of heart but simply, like the blabberings of an awakened man in sleep who immediately thereafter goes back into sleep. You go on grumbling that you do not have any relief from the worries of the family; and with great efforts and hard work you make Halal earnings. But you have no concern for Halal and Haram (that is permissible and impermissible). You are, in fact, one among such misguided rebellious fellows whose killing becomes so permissible as no other killing is. You have relieved yourself of your duties to God. You have relieved yourself of the affairs of religion but not of Satan.

sections.heading: Unlimited Greed for Worldly Gains:
paras: You have no patience and contentment without this mean world. You have only gone after all the materials spread over the world. In this matter you very much appreciate what God has said: ‘And the earth We laid out, how gracious was the spreader’: “Wal ardha farashnaha fa ni‘mal maahiduun”: (Zariyat: 51: 48). You try to appropriate every spread-out thing for yourself. You cannot have patience in the matter of grabbing these things. You have no patience upon comforts and luxuries. How can you have patience upon the search of God? When you have no patience to separate the clean from the unclean, how can you have patience with the One who has created you. When you have no patience to know of polluted water, how can you be patient with the fountain of God. When you have no patience with family members, how can you have it with the Ever Living and Graceful God.

sections.heading: Yet, They Hope for Forgiveness:
paras: You say that God will forgive you. Consider this assessment as a ghostly voice from the forest. Do you know of prophet, H.Ibrahīm, that as soon as he came out of the cave where he was being brought up, started the search for God and went on considering the star, the moon and the sun, one after another as his Lord. Upon their setting, he denied them of their lordship saying: “I shall not look at both the worlds until I come to know about their owner”. He also said that he would not even eat his food until he found out the attributes of God. How can anybody’s eating and living be justified without his knowing about the One who has created and provided these things.

sections.heading: Enjoying Provisions Without Knowing the Provider:
paras: It is only the cows and donkeys which can eat without knowing their Lord. This applies to those humans also who live and enjoy life and the provisions made for it. Rather, they are worse than cattle as stated in the Qur’an: ‘They are like cattle, nay misguided’: “Ūlaaika kal an‘aami bal hum Adhallu”: (Al A’raf: 7: 179). This is not just due to ignorance but due to their treacherous and incurable-foul-smelling-disease. Their treacheries got degraded and disgraced. They lost their precious time. They made useless and foolish efforts and ultimately got nothing out of life either for this world or that.

Some of them do say that they are concerned about all this. But in this saying also there is a falsehood and treachery of their vicious self. They say that God is Forgiving and Merciful and they will be forgiven by Him. This is nothing but a pleading of the mean, shameless self. In the matter of God’s obedience, they say like this. When they do not have some needed things, they feel grieved and sorry and suffer anxiety. Why do they not stop feeling in this manner when they say that God is Forgiving and Merciful and leave everything to Him.

sections.heading: Weakness of Old Age:
paras: An elderly man said to a physician that he was in great anxiety about his brain. The physician said: “The weakness of the brain is due to old age”. The old man said: “There is a dark spot in my eyes.” The Physician said: “Sir, this is due to old age.” He said: “I have pain in my back.” The physician said: “O Weak elderly man! This is due to old age.” He said: “Whatever I eat remains undigested.” He replied: “This is due to the weakness of the stomach due to old age.” He said: “I also feel difficulty in breathing. Air gets choked.” He replied: “Yes! Breathing also becomes difficult in old age. And many other ailments also come about.”
He said: “My potency has come to a complete stop in entirety!”
He replied: “This is due to old age!”
He said: “My legs feel tired. I feel difficulty in walking”.
He replied: “This is due to old age, which has forced you to seclusion.”
“My back has bent down like a bow,”
“This pain and defect are due to old age.”
“O Physician! My eyes have gone blurred.”
“This is also due to old age.”

Then the old man got angry and said: “You are ill-witted. You are stuck on this point of old age. Is this the only thing that you learnt from medical science? You are a rotten-minded fellow! Your wisdom has not taught you this much that God has created remedy for every ailment. Because of your lack of full knowledge, you are a foolish ass! Because of your weak legs, you have kept yourself attached to the earth”.

Then the physician said: “You are a man in the sixties. This anger and wrath of yours is also due to old age. When all your limbs and parts of the body have become weak, your power of self-control and patience has also become weak. You cannot even bear to hear two words; and drink one mouthful of water, and vomit it.

sections.heading: Exceptions: Saints and Prophets:
paras: This is the situation of every old man except the one who is intoxicated with the truth of God. Within him is a clean healthy life. From outside, he is old to look at but within himself he is young like a child. He is one like the prophets and saints, who are hidden from all good and bad people. But the mean fellows are jealous of them. When these mean fellows know them with certainty as to who they are, why should they have ill will and unhealthy speculations about them. Were these jealous fellows to know of the punishment they would undergo on the doomsday, they would have considered them as unsheathed swords and avoided facing them. The saintly are self-composed, joyous and happy before you, but their inside is full of such powers which can cause doomsday-like-troubles for you which they do not expose. All their possessions are like heaven and hell. They are more elevated than whatever you think about them, as they have adopted for themselves the character and conduct of God. What is a godly character and conduct? It is some quality that does not get annihilated. These cannot be conceived by man, just as God cannot be conceived in mind. Those who misbehave with them will not do so, if they know about their state and level.

sections.heading: Masjids of Bricks, Masjids of Hearts:
paras: Foolish people honour and respect the masjid and they are bent upon harming the men of heart. With the abilities of donkeys, you must know that the masjid is built of material things, but the hearts of these great men are the real masjids requiring all respects and honours. The masjid that is there in the hearts of these great men is the place of worship for all as God is very much in them. Masjid made of bricks belongs to this world and their hearts belong to that world. Troubling the saints brings destruction to the trouble-giving-communities. God has not disgraced those people who have honoured their great men.

The enemies of the prophets went forward to fight with them. They looked only at their bodies and considered them simply as men. They did not look at their souls inside. You too have the same misconduct, and avoid them, and your fate also will be like their’s. In spite of your misconduct, if you have not been punished like the earlier people so far, you should not think such will be the case later too. A pail let down in the well will not always come back empty. It will come full of water. When all these defective signs are in you, there is no scope for you to remain unaffected always.

sections.heading: Boy’s Explanation of the Grave:
paras: A boy was following his father’s funeral, crying very much, beating his forehead in grief. He was saying: “O my father, after all, where are you being taken; taken to bury you in mud, in a narrow, small house, which has no carpet. Not even a mat. It has no lamp for the night, nor a window for light during the day. It does not even have the smell of food or a mark of it. Neither it has a good door, nor roof and balcony. It has no window with glass shutters for light to enter. It has no well-water for the guests, no neighbours nearby to be of help in need. What will happen to your body which was kissed by the people and now in this dark black house. It is a narrow house, so pressing that you can neither have your face intact, nor its color”

sections.heading: Buffoon’s House Resembled Grave:
paras: In this manner, the boy was talking about his father and shedding tears of blood in sorrow. As against this, a buffoon told his father: “O honourable elder! I swear upon God! This man is being taken to our house!” The buffoon’s father told him: “Do not be foolish!” But the buffoon retorted to his father: “Look at the signs of the house that this boy is talking about. What all he said, without any doubt refers to our house. It also has no mat, no lamp and no food. Neither its door is in order, nor its roof and balcony”

sections.heading: Hearts of the Destroyed People Resemble Graves:
paras: In this manner, all the destroyed communities have a hundred signs. But stubborn people do not look at them. Their hearts are narrow without any light of the rays of God’s sun. Their hearts are narrow and short like the hearts of the Jews, totally devoid of the taste of looking at the Ever-Loving-kind Emperor. Their hearts neither have the light of the sun, nor do they have open space, nor open doors. Grave is better than such a heart. Therefore, get out of the grave of your heart.

sections.heading: God Alone Can Save in the Absence of Means:
paras: You are H. Yūsuf of your time and the sun of the sky. Get out of the well which has imprisoned you as H. Yūsuf was, and show your beautiful face. You are H. Yūnus who was getting cooked in the belly of the fish. He had no other alternative than to praise God and seek His mercy for escape. Had he not been a repeat reciter of God’s praises (Tasbih) he would have continued to be in the prison of the fish’s belly till the doomsday. He got freedom from this prison with the support of constant praises of God seeking his support. What is this repeat recitation? It is a sign of the day of Alast, the time when mankind made covenant of total obedience to God. This is a spiritual recitation of remembrance of God to identify and speak of all His attributes and actions to come together to one’s rescue when all other means of escape are lost. If you have forgotten this recitation, you may hear the recitations made by the fishes as follows: -

sections.heading: Meaning of Fish, Yūnus and Recitations Explained:
paras: Whoever has seen God, has become a godly man. Whoever has seen this ocean of godhood, sinks into it and moves everywhere in the ocean like fish. He has no restraint and obstacles. The fish is free in the ocean, and the material world is also as large as the ocean, but man’s body is like the fish. And the soul is like H. Yūnus held up in the fish together with the body in the ocean of the material world. In other words, this world may be taken as an ocean, man’s body as fish and H. Yūnus as soul held up in the body. The body, as fish is carrying the soul as of H. Yūnus everywhere. Here, H. Yūnus, as soul, as imprisoned in the body of the fish, is deprived of the morning light which normally increases as the day moves forward. In such a situation you as soul, have no means of escape at all, except to go on reciting the names of God as H.Yūnus did.

Then your soul will be freed from the prison of your body, just as H. Yūnus was freed from the body of the fish. If you do not do this, your soul will be crushed and digested by the body just as the food of the fish gets digested.

chapters.title: Elucidation and Lessons from the Incidents of H.Yusuf and H.Yūnus

paras: [H.Yūsuf was felled by his brothers in a well that was on the caravan route where there was hope of a caravan passing, putting its bucket for water, upon which H. Yūsuf could catch the bucket and be brought out by the bucket puller, and get freed. In fact, this happened. Further, H.Yūsuf had a shining day light upon him in the well, and he was too young to know of the difficulties in which he was caught. Therefore, he did not make any praises of God and pray to Him for relief, but maintained a silent hope of relief with total surrender to God.

As against him, H.Yūnus was swallowed by the fish and imprisoned in its dark narrow, stomach which would have digested and finished him in the normal course. There was absolutely no scope for any relief either inside the fish and from any outside agency. This was a case of total and absolute helplessness. The only hope was of relief with God’s own intervention. Therefore, he had to rely only upon repeated praises of God which he did and got relief which could be none other than this fish vomiting him out. In fact, the very act of swallowing him by the fish was an earlier relief as otherwise, he would have drowned and got finished in water.

The lesson is that resorting to only praises of God and prayers to God ought to be in the case of absolute hopelessness. On the contrary, where there is the slightest opportunity of escape from the difficulties, efforts have to be made supported by praises and prayers and faith in God, which the Mathnavi cites on many occasions ― Translator].

sections.heading: World: Not Devoid of Great Men:
paras: There are such fishes of the body which are controlled by their souls who are in large numbers in this ocean of material world like the fishes in the ocean. They are saintly people, but you do not see them as you are mentally blind. They are moving around and touching you. Open your eyes so as to see them in clarity. They move around and touch you as they are desirous of gracing and benefiting you. You have not clearly seen those fishes but your ears have certainly heard their repeated praises. These fishes have no body and they are only souls. Their bodies are annihilated in their souls. They do not have any sense of self-glorification, ill-will or jealousy. The soul of your repeated praises ought to be patience as it is a proper praise, (as was in the case of H. Yūsuf).

sections.heading: Patience: Bridge to Paradise:
paras: No praise has such a grade as patience, as patience is the key for expansion, development and largeness. Patience is like the bridge of righteousness beyond which is paradise. It is like an ugly slave and its possessor is like a beautiful master. You cannot go forward alone in life. You have to go along with your ugly slave of patience. So long as you do not take the slave with you, you cannot meet your object as the slave is a must to accompany you. You are too soft-hearted to know the taste of patience, in particular, to meet the beautiful beloved of Chagil (region in Turkistan where the people are very beautiful). Men have a taste for warfare, glory and grandeur while the eunuch has for the male sex organ. His religion, meditation and thoughts are for nothing but the sex organ, which take him to lowly levels. Even if by chance, he happens to go up to the level of the sky, do not hold him in respect as he has learnt the lessons of the lowly levels. He runs his horse towards lowly levels, even though he is raising his ball to go up. Where is the need to fear the flags of beggars, as they are the slaves of a piece of bread? Know these facts well; and if you cannot, hear this incident in connection with this.

A well-built person found a lonely boy and the boy feared him, and turned pale. The well-built man told him: “Be not afraid of me, my beautiful boy as you are above me. Though I have frightening looks, consider me as a eunuch. Sit upon my back and drive me as you drive a camel”. Men’s appearance and hidden qualities are different. From outside, they are men, but hidden within, they are accursed satans. O you fat fellow! You are like a drum which is being beaten by the air with the leaves and tender branches of the tree. By getting misled by its sound, which was full of air like the goatskin, the fox lost its prey, in spite of its cunningness and cleverness. When she found a big drum without anything inside, she said: “A pig is better than this empty goatskin”. Foxes get frightened with the sound of drums but the wise men beat it so loud that it is better not to tell. Many pseudo saints are like drums.

A frightful man wearing many weapons, riding on his horse, was going in a forest. An archer looked at him and got frightened and pulled his arrow on the bow to shoot at him. The horse-rider shouted at him: “I am a weak person though strong in appearance. Be careful, not to look at my strong body as I'm weaker than an old woman in fight”.
The archer said: “Go away! You did well that you told me about this, as out of your fear, I would have shot the arrow at you”.

There are many such people lacking bravery, yet carrying swords in their hands who get killed by their own weapons in battles. If you carry weapons like Rustams, when you do not have strength and courage, be sure that you will lose your life. Therefore, young man, give up the sword and make your life itself as a shield and protect yourself. The treacheries and designs of worldly men have no effect on the lonely brave men of faith. Treacheries and designs are your weapons, which are your own makings, which weaken your life and soul. These treacheries are of no use for you. Give them up and search for graceful God. Other benefits will come before you on their own. These things are of no use for you. Give them up and cleanse yourself of the bad effects and get rid of the misfortune. The angels said: “We have no knowledge except what You have taught us!” (Surah Baqarah: 2: 32). That is the right way. Treacheries, excuses and false pleadings are of no use in this path. One who considers oneself as wise, is in reality foolish. In this connection, you may hear this story in the matter of ignorance and purposeless application of immature wisdom.

A Bedouin was carrying a bag of wheat on his camel on one side, and on the other side he hanged a bag full of sand. He sat upon both of them. A person asked him about his country and put many other questions stringing pearls of wisdom; and then asked him about the contents of the bags, advising him to tell truly. The Bedouin said: “One contains wheat and the other sand, which is not food for mankind.” He asked him as to why he filled one bag with sand. He said: “So that it may not be a single bag, so as to balance the weight on both sides.” The wise man said: “You may shift half of the wheat in the other bag after emptying it of sand, and maintain the balance on both sides, so that the bags may be of lesser weight, and the burden upon the camel is reduced.”

The Bedouin said: “O wise, capable and noble man! How great of you! You have such subtle understanding and good advice. But you are without proper clothing and tired and walking on foot.” He felt pity for him and decided to make him sit on his camel. Then he told him: “O sweet tongued, tell me in detail about yourself. You have such great ability. Tell me the truth! Are you a king or a vazir?”
The wiseman said: “I am none of them. I am an ordinary common man. Look at my dress and my condition.” The Bedouin said: “How many camels and cows do you have?”
He said: “I have neither camels nor cows. Do not enquire too much.”
The Bedouin asked: “What are the commodities in you shop?”

He replied: “Where do I have a shop, and so also my house? I do not have any food to eat, clothing to wear and other jobs to do. I do not have any means of livelihood, no kitchen and no materials to cook.”

The Bedouin said: “I am asking about your cash and money. You are walking alone; and you have very good advising capacity. You have the alchemy to convert copper into gold. And, you have the pearls of wisdom and intelligence in layers upon layers. You might have kept treasures at home. There is none wiser than you in the world.”

The wiseman said: “I swear upon God. I do not have all this, O leader of the Arabs! My entire wealth consists of a means of spending the night, with naked feet and body. I roam about; and I go to anybody who gives me bread. Excepting thoughts and headache, I do not get anything else form my wisdom, excellence and art.”

sections.heading: Wisdom Without Application Is Useless:
paras: Then the Bedouin told him: “Go away from me so that your misfortune may not fall on my head. Take your accursed wisdom away from me. Even your words are unfortunate for the people. Either you may go that way and I go this, and if you have to go forward, I shall go backwards. My one bag of wheat and another of sand, are much better than your mean worthless suggestions. My bags of wheat and sand are certainly better than your wisdom. My foolishness is a very prosperous foolishness that my heart is safe and secure from difficulties with materials that I have. If you want that these difficulties of yours are reduced, better try to reduce your wisdom.”

sections.heading: Experts and Specialists:
paras: Wisdom that comes out of our choice and personal inclinations is devoid of the grace of the light of God. Wisdom of the worldly matters increases doubts and speculations, and that of the faith takes one to the heavens. Cunning foxes of the later days have taken themselves ahead of the earlier wise men. Cunning and expert foxes of one art and subject have imposed themselves upon those men, who know the truths of matters. Tricksters have spent their lifetimes to learn more tricks and tricky devices. They have destroyed their sense of service to others, generosity of character and gracefulness. These qualities are the providers of profits and gains and are their alchemies. But they have destroyed them by their narrow selfishness.

sections.heading: Real and Pseudo Intelligence:
paras: Intelligence is that which widens the ways. And ways are those that take the passers to the kings of virtues. The king is one who is a king on his own, independent of treasuries and armies. They are the leaders of nobilities, and masters of noble acts. They go after and possess the everlasting kingdom of morals like the kingship and honour of the faith of Muhammad, the Prophet. There is no decline to the laws of Muhammad till the doomsday. Impacts of evil eyes are far away from this kingdom.

It is reported from the life of H. Ibrahim Ad-ham that, once he was sitting on a road adjacent to the bank of a river. The king of this world who had turned into the king of that world by discarding his kingdom, was stitching his old-patched-garment. One of his old regional leaders came over there. He was one among his slaves. He recognized the old master and fell down in prostration before him. He found the physical conditions and conduct of the king as having been completely changed and was astonished at this condition and his patched-garment; and on the fact that he has discarded a wonderful large kingdom and resorted to this poverty which was on very subtle lines of lack of material grandeur but full of spiritual, esoteric matters of mysticism and gnosticism. He thought it strange that after leaving such grand kingdom, he is using a needle to stitch torne garment. He has discarded the kingdom of seven continents and put on a beggar’s garment.

sections.heading: Knowledge of Inner Feelings:
paras: The shaikh came to know of his inner thoughts. Shaikhs are like lions whose forests are the hearts of people. Lions, which move about in these forests of hearts full of hopes and fears. Hidden secrets are not hidden from them. O poor fellows, though rich of wordly attainments, take care of your hearts and tutor them in the gatherings of the men of hearts. Apparent devotion of the body is required before the worldly lords, because they can see only the apparent acts, and are ignorant of their inner feelings about them. God keeps their feelings hidden from them. As against this, discipline and good behaviour of the heart is required before the men of hearts as their hearts look at the hearts of those before them.

sections.heading: Kings of This and That World:
paras: But people behave in an opposite manner. They go before these great men of blind hearts with respect to get great status and sit in a lower place before them. But they ignore to behave well before these men of bright hearts who can see their inner self. Similar to them, you also do this because you are made as fuel for fire. As you do not possess the light of intelligence and guidance, you polish your face to attract the attention of the worldly people who are blind at heart. But before those bright-hearted great men, this polishing is not necessary. You may ignore your outward appearance. Yet, you go to them with artificial uncleanliness to impress upon them that you are not bothered about apparent cleanliness. Do not be proud of this artificial behaviour.

sections.heading: Kingdom of That World:
paras: Upon coming to know of the inner feelings of this visitor, the shaikh threw away his stitching needle in water and loudly called upon the needle to come back. Instantly, thousands of fishes of God, came up. Each one of them had a needle of gold in its mouth as though telling the shaikh to take the needles of gold. They raised their heads from the ocean of truth and offered them to him. The shaikh said: “O my God! I have asked for my needle. Show the proper sign of acceptance of prayer, My Lord, with Your kindness.” Suddenly another fish came holding his needle in its mouth. He looked at it and said: “O leader, tell me which kingdom is better? Kingdom of the heart or the kingdom of this worthless world. What you see is a sign of the apparent world. It is of no worth. Search for the hidden matters and do not keep your eyes on the visible things.

sections.heading: Greatness of That World:
paras: This world is like a city to which branches of the tree with flowers are brought form the garden. They bring only the branches and not the garden. This city is too small to accommodate that large garden. In particular, a garden which, inspite of its vastness is so small that its sky is only, a leaf of the garden of heaven. Rather, it is the pulp and this world is like its rind. If you dare not take your steps towards that garden, at least search for its spread-out-fragrance and cure yourself of the cold which has spoiled your sense of smelling. So that, this fragrance may become a cause of attraction for your soul. So that, it may become a light for your eyes. So that, it may drag you toward that garden, and show you the path of guidance. So that, it may brighten your blind eyes and connect your heart to Mount Sina, where H. Mūsā saw the light of God and heard His voice. H. Yusuf, son of prophet Yāqūb, sent his shirt through his brothers telling them to put it on the face of his father, so that he might smell its fragrance. About this fragrance, Prophet Muhammad said in his sermons: “The coolness of my eyes is in my salat.”

sections.heading: Interconnections Respectively of the External and Internal Senses:
paras: All the five respective external senses: seeing, hearing, touching, tasting and smelling are inter connected. They have all risen form a highly placed root. The food of one sense becomes a cause of power of all the others by providing sips of its water for them all. Similarly, there are five other inner entities: heart, soul, self (nafs comprising of commands, repentance and satisfaction), the fourth, hidden knowledge of the essences of all things, and the fifth, capacity to keep secrets as secrets. When one of these inner entities receives any information, the other four also share it. For example: when the eyes see something, the heart receives its impacts, and this creates the feeling of attraction for the seen object, which results in the purity and sincerity of love, which is kept as a secret to keep up the dignity of the beloved object as what is beautiful and lovable for one need not be so for others. Others may not consider it beautiful, in which case its dignity and honour as held by the lover may be reduced in the view of others. Therefore, sincerity (of keeping) and truthfulness become the cause of waking up of all other inner senses, which also become friendly to all the five senses ― the taste to enjoy the pleasure attached to the beloved object.

chapters.title: Wisdom, Thought, Wahii and Other Overflowings

sections.heading: Interconnection of Internal Senses:
paras: Apart from what is stated in the preceding lines relating to the external senses, there are similar situations to the internal senses of heart, soul etc. When one sense opens the ties of movements, the other senses also change. When one of these five inner senses feels such senses which cannot be sensed by external senses, the subtle heavenly spiritual realities appear on the other senses. This is like the jumping of the sheep in the steam, one after another, by all other sheep, following one that jumps first. Thus, it becomes necessary for a seeker to consider all these five subtle senses as sheep and take them to the meadow of the unseeable spiritual world for pasture, provided by God, as stated in the Quran: ‘And Who brings out the (green and luscious) pasture’: “Wallazii akhrajal mar‘aa”: (A‘laa: 87: 4). So that, they may graze upon the ears of prosperous grain and sweet smelling plants, so that they may find the paths towards the gardens of realities and truths of matters.

sections.heading: Each Sense Is a Messenger to All:
paras: Each one of your senses is a messenger to other senses to instantly take them toward paradise. Your senses reveal the secrets known to them to the other senses, without a tongue, freely, by remaining independent of all means of communications, and without posing intelligential or spiritual examples. Informations given through words are liable to be interpreted differently, but in this case, as there are no words, there are no scopes for interpretation. Whatever is cognised is by direct and clear observation. That is the capital for all further observations. That clear reality has no scope at all for any interpretation.

sections.heading: Control of Own Senses and of Others:
paras: When all senses come under the control of your senses, even heavens will not remain out of your control. This control relates to the senses of other people also. Sky is like the rind and the light of the soul is the pulp. When there is a dispute as to whom the rind belongs, the fair judgement is that, it belongs to the one who owns the pulp. Similarly, when there is a dispute on a bundle of grass, the judgement is that, it belongs to the one to whom the grains belong. On this analogy, sky which is like the rind belongs to the soul which is the pulp. The only difference is ― sky is open, clear and visible, but the soul is not.
