The rings that move around you when you step into water in the form of water waves are like the iron shields made for you by H. Dawood in whose hand iron melted like wax.

sections.heading: Look at Causer, Not the Causes:
paras: Sulaimān is right before every one of us. But our ignorance and arrogance blindfold our eyes and cast magic spells. We do not care to see him because of our confinement in sleep and absurdities. Sounds of thunder create headache in an ignorant thirsty fellow, who does not know that they open the gates of the clouds of prosperity and provide water to meet his thirst. He is in search of flowing water. He thinks of the stream alone as the source of water. He does not have the knowledge that the source of water are the clouds is the sky. He drives the horse of his wisdom towards the cause and remains unaware of the Creator of the causes. One who looks at the Causer of causes in clarity, will never look at the various causes in the world. He finds a clear morning of deliverance, success and victory from the Causer of causes. He receives from the Causer so much of information within a few moments, which others get in a hundred years of struggle.

There was a godly man deeply sunk in worship sitting upon the hot sand of a desert like the people of Abbadan, (which is a very hot place). Many hajis from different places came over to that place and their eyes fell on this thin, weak person. His place of sitting was dry hot sand but he was fresh and wet. The hot wind of the desert was as though a cold wind for him. The hajis were astonished at his loneliness and his remaining safe in that troublesome surroundings. He was standing up for salat on the sand, which was so hot that it could boil water.

In such a difficult situation, you would feel him to be in a garden of greenery and flowers. Or, he was in flight upon burraq sitting upon which the noble Prophet had gone towards the heavens; or, proudly riding upon duldul, the mule that the king of Alexandria had sent as present to the Prophet. Or, he has kept his feet upon soft silk and wearing silk garments. Or, the hot air was better than the cool morning breeze of the gardens. He was standing with a fresh face for salat full of humility, submission and devotion. He was in secret conversation with his Beloved and completely sunk in his long, deep surroundings.

The group of hajis stood up in all respect waiting for him to finish his prayer. When that dervish came out of his depths of commitments, one haji with a bright conscience in the group, saw that water was dripping from his face and hands and his clothes were wet with water as though he has just then performed ablution. So, he asked him: “From where did you get water?” The dervish lifted his hand up and said: “From the sky.” He asked him: “Do you get water whenever you are in need, without a well, and rope to draw water? O king of the religion, pray solve our problem, so that your situations may grant us confidence in God. Please open up one of your secrets upon us, so that we may cut off the zunnar that we have tied around our waists.” (zunnar is a cotton thread that Brahmins and Zorastrians tie around the chest or waiste as a token of their faith, belief and hope on God).

The man of desert turned his eyes towards the sky to pray to God to accept the prayers of the hajis and said: “I am in the habit of searching for my food in the upper world, as You have opened for me the door of that world. O the One, You have shown to a man this special world, the world beyond space and exposed to him the meaning of: ‘And in heaven is your sustenance’: “Wa fissamaa’i rizqukum”: (Zaariyat: 51: 22).

During the course of this supplication, a thick cloud resembling an elephant full of water appeared. It started flowing water as though from a goatskin which filled up the caves and pits in the area. Cloud was felling water like tears and all the hajis opened their goatskins. Another group started tearing off the zunnars from the waists upon looking at this strange observation. [Perhaps some converts from Zorastrians to Islam still continued the habit of wearing zunnars ― Translator].

Another group was strengthening its confidence in God with this strange scene as God knows best in the matter of giving guidance. Yet, there were some people who were immature and of sour taste, who were not impressed. They were the eternally defective ones. The discourse is concluded.

A Bedouin was carrying a bag of wheat on his camel on one side, and on the other side he hanged a bag full of sand. He sat upon both of them. A person asked him about his country and put many other questions stringing pearls of wisdom; and then asked him about the contents of the bags, advising him to tell truly. The Bedouin said: “One contains wheat and the other sand, which is not food for mankind.” He asked him as to why he filled one bag with sand. He said: “So that it may not be a single bag, so as to balance the weight on both sides.” The wise man said: “You may shift half of the wheat in the other bag after emptying it of sand, and maintain the balance on both sides, so that the bags may be of lesser weight, and the burden upon the camel is reduced.”

The Bedouin said: “O wise, capable and noble man! How great of you! You have such subtle understanding and good advice. But you are without proper clothing and tired and walking on foot.” He felt pity for him and decided to make him sit on his camel. Then he told him: “O sweet tongued, tell me in detail about yourself. You have such great ability. Tell me the truth! Are you a king or a vazir?”
The wiseman said: “I am none of them. I am an ordinary common man. Look at my dress and my condition.” The Bedouin said: “How many camels and cows do you have?”
He said: “I have neither camels nor cows. Do not enquire too much.”
The Bedouin asked: “What are the commodities in you shop?”

He replied: “Where do I have a shop, and so also my house? I do not have any food to eat, clothing to wear and other jobs to do. I do not have any means of livelihood, no kitchen and no materials to cook.”

The Bedouin said: “I am asking about your cash and money. You are walking alone; and you have very good advising capacity. You have the alchemy to convert copper into gold. And, you have the pearls of wisdom and intelligence in layers upon layers. You might have kept treasures at home. There is none wiser than you in the world.”

The wiseman said: “I swear upon God. I do not have all this, O leader of the Arabs! My entire wealth consists of a means of spending the night, with naked feet and body. I roam about; and I go to anybody who gives me bread. Excepting thoughts and headache, I do not get anything else form my wisdom, excellence and art.”

sections.heading: Wisdom Without Application Is Useless:
paras: Then the bedouin told him: “Go away from me so that your misfortune may not fall on my head. Take your accursed wisdom away from me. Even your words are unfortunate for the people. Either you may go that way and I go this, and if you have to go forward, I shall go backwards. My one bag of wheat and another of sand, are much better than your mean worthless suggestions. My bags of wheat and sand are certainly better than your wisdom. My foolishness is a very prosperous foolishness that my heart is safe and secure from difficulties with materials that I have. If you want that these difficulties of yours are reduced, better try to reduce your wisdom.”

sections.heading: Experts and Specialists:
paras: Wisdom that comes out of our choice and personal inclinations is devoid of the grace of the light of God. Wisdom of the worldly matters increases doubts and speculations, and that of the faith takes one to the heavens. Cunning foxes of the later days have taken themselves ahead of the earlier wise men. Cunning and expert foxes of one art and subject have imposed themselves upon those men, who know the truths of matters. Tricksters have spent their lifetimes to learn more tricks and tricky devices. They have destroyed their sense of service to others, generosity of character and gracefulness. These qualities are the providers of profits and gains and are their alchemies. But they have destroyed them by their narrow selfishness.

sections.heading: Real and Pseudo Intelligence:
paras: Intelligence is that which widens the ways. And ways are those that take the passers to the kings of virtues. The king is one who is a king on his own, independent of treasuries and armies. They are the leaders of nobilities, and masters of noble acts. They go after and possess the everlasting kingdom of morals like the kingship and honour of the faith of Muhammad, the Prophet. There is no decline to the laws of Muhammad till the doomsday. Impacts of evil eyes are far away from this kingdom.

It is reported from the life of H.Ibrahim Ad-ham that, once he was sitting on a road adjacent to the bank of a river. The king of this world who had turned into the king of that world by discarding his kingdom, was stitching his old-patched-garment. One of his old regional leaders came over there. He was one among his slaves. He recognised the old master and fell down in prostration before him. He found the physical conditions and conduct of the king as having been completely changed and was astonished at this condition and his patched-garment; and on the fact that he has discarded a wonderful large kingdom and resorted to this poverty which was on very subtle lines of lack of material grandeur but full of spiritual, esoteric matters of mysticism and gnosticism. He thought it strange that after leaving such grand kingdom, he is using a needle to stitch torne garment. He has discarded the kingdom of seven continents and put on a beggar’s garment.

sections.heading: Knowledge of Inner Feelings:
paras: The shaikh came to know of his inner thoughts. Shaikhs are like lions whose forests are the hearts of people. Lions, which move about in these forests of hearts full of hopes and fears. Hidden secrets are not hidden from them. O poor fellows, though rich of wordly attainments, take care of your hearts and tutor them in the gatherings of the men of hearts. Apparent devotion of the body is required before the worldly lords, because they can see only the apparent acts, and are ignorant of their inner feelings about them. God keeps their feelings hidden from them. As against this, discipline and good behaviour of the heart is required before the men of hearts as their hearts look at the hearts of those before them.

sections.heading: Kings of This and That World:
paras: But people behave in an opposite manner. They go before these great men of blind hearts with respect to get great status and sit in a lower place before them. But they ignore to behave well before these men of bright hearts who can see their inner self. Similar to them, you also do this because you are made as fuel for fire. As you do not possess the light of intelligence and guidance, you polish your face to attract the attention of the worldly people who are blind at heart. But before those bright-hearted great men, this polishing is not necessary. You may ignore your outward appearance. Yet, you go to them with artificial uncleanliness to impress upon them that you are not bothered about apparent cleanliness. Do not be proud of this artificial behaviour.

sections.heading: Kingdom of That World:
paras: Upon coming to know of the inner feelings of this visitor, the shaikh threw away his stitching needle in water and loudly called upon the needle to come back. Instantly, thousands of fishes of God, came up. Each one of them had a needle of gold in its mouth as though telling the shaikh to take the needles of gold. They raised their heads from the ocean of truth and offered them to him. The shaikh said: “O my God! I have asked for my needle. Show the proper sign of acceptance of prayer, My Lord, with Your kindness.” Suddenly another fish came holding his needle in its mouth. He looked at it and said: “O leader, tell me which kingdom is better? Kingdom of the heart or the kingdom of this worthless world. What you see is a sign of the apparent world. It is of no worth. Search for the hidden matters and do not keep your eyes on the visible things.

sections.heading: Greatness of That World:
paras: This world is like a city to which branches of the tree with flowers are brought form the garden. They bring only the branches and not the garden. This city is too small to accommodate that large garden. In particular, a garden which, inspite of its vastness is so small that its sky is only, a leaf of the garden of heaven. Rather, it is the pulp and this world is like its rind. If you dare not take your steps towards that garden, at least search for its spread-out-fragrance and cure yourself of the cold which has spoiled your sense of smelling. So that, this fragrance may become a cause of attraction for your soul. So that, it may become a light for your eyes. So that, it may drag you toward that garden, and show you the path of guidance. So that, it may brighten your blind eyes and connect your heart to Mount Sina, where H. Musa saw the light of God and heard His voice. H. Yusuf, son of prophet Yaqub, sent his shirt through his brothers telling them to put it on the face of his father, so that he might smell its fragrance. About this fragrance, Prophet Muhammad said in his sermons: “The coolness of my eyes is in my salat.”

sections.heading: Interconnections Respectively of the External and Internal Senses:
paras: All the five respective external senses: seeing, hearing, touching, tasting and smelling are inter connected. They have all risen form a highly placed root. The food of one sense becomes a cause of power of all the others by providing sips of its water for them all. Similarly, there are five other inner entities: heart, soul, self (nafs comprising of commands, repentance and satisfaction), the fourth, hidden knowledge of the essences of all things, and the fifth, capacity to keep secrets as secrets. When one of these inner entities receives any information, the other four also share it. For example: when the eyes see something, the heart receives its impacts, and this creates the feeling of attraction for the seen object, which results in the purity and sincerity of love, which is kept as a secret to keep up the dignity of the beloved object as what is beautiful and lovable for one need not be so for others. Others may not consider it beautiful, in which case its dignity and honour as held by the lover may be reduced in the view of others. Therefore, sincerity (of keeping) and truthfulness become the cause of waking up of all other inner senses, which also become friendly to all the five senses ― the taste to enjoy the pleasure attached to the beloved object.

sections.heading: Interconnection of Internal Senses:
paras: Apart from what is stated in the preceding lines relating to the external senses, there are similar situations to the internal senses of heart, soul etc. When one sense opens the ties of movements, the other senses also change. When one of these five inner senses feels such senses which cannot be sensed by external senses, the subtle heavenly spiritual realities appear on the other senses. This is like the jumping of the sheep in the steam, one after another, by all other sheep, following one that jumps first. Thus, it becomes necessary for a seeker to consider all these five subtle senses as sheep and take them to the meadow of the unseeable spiritual world for pasture, provided by God, as stated in the Quran: ‘And Who brings out the (green and luscious) pasture’: “Wallazii akhrajal mar‘aa”: (A‘laa: 87: 4). So that, they may graze upon the ears of prosperous grain and sweet smelling plants, so that they may find the paths towards the gardens of realities and truths of matters.

sections.heading: Each Sense Is a Messenger to All:
paras: Each one of your senses is a messenger to other senses to instantly take them toward paradise. Your senses reveal the secrets known to them to the other senses, without a tongue, freely, by remaining independent of all means of communications, and without posing intelligential or spiritual examples. Informations given through words are liable to be interpreted differently, but in this case, as there are no words, there are no scopes for interpretation. Whatever is cognised is by direct and clear observation. That is the capital for all further observations. That clear reality has no scope at all for any interpretation.

sections.heading: Control of Own Senses and of Others:
paras: When all senses come under the control of your senses, even heavens will not remain out of your control. This control relates to the senses of other people also. Sky is like the rind and the light of the soul is the pulp. When there is a dispute as to whom the rind belongs, the fair judgement is that, it belongs to the one who owns the pulp. Similarly, when there is a dispute on a bundle of grass, the judgement is that, it belongs to the one to whom the grains belong. On this analogy, sky which is like the rind belongs to the soul which is the pulp. The only difference is ― sky is open, clear and visible, but the soul is not. Great misunderstandings come about in this matter. Similarly, man’s body is apparent, but his soul is hidden. Body is like the sleeve, within which the hand is hidden.

sections.heading: Wisdom Is More Hidden Than Soul:
paras: And, wisdom is all the more hidden. It is more hidden than the soul. Senses understand the soul more easily than they understand wisdom. When you see movements in the body, you easily conclude that there is soul in the body, but there is no such way to understand wisdom. Wisdom cannot be understood by merely looking at the movements of the body. Movements have to be proper and balanced to prove wisdom. With proper acts of wisdom, copper can be converted into gold. Proper movements prove the existence of wisdom. With proper actions of the hand, you can recognise wisdom. All this is said in respect of the connections between the soul and wisdom.

sections.heading: Inspiration (Wahii) Higher Than Wisdom and More Hidden:
paras: But above them is the spirit of inspirational knowledge (wahi) which is more hidden than wisdom. This is for the reason that it entirely belongs to the hidden world. Soul and wisdom have already come into the human body and become a part of this world, even though they are far above other things ― material and sensory. But inspiration entirely belongs to the hidden world, and it exists only there. For example, wisdom of the noble Prophet was not hidden from anybody. Everybody could understand it. But his capacity of receiving inspiration could not be understood by everyone. Still there are signs which can establish its existence; but wisdom cannot understand it, because it is very strange and out of the normal way. Wisdom gets confused about it. Sometimes wisdom calls it as madness and sometimes it gets wonderstruck. Wisdom can understand inspiration only when there is total parity with it, having the capacity to alternate itself with it.

sections.heading: Wisdom of H.Musa; Inspiration of H.Khizr:
paras: For example: Actions of H. Khizr did not have parity with the wisdom of H.Musa; and H.Musa’s capacity was not at the level of H.Khizr. There was no parity between H.Musa’s wisdom and H.Khizr’s actions. H.Musa’s wisdom failed to understand H.Khizr’s actions. His wisdom was like the wisdom of a rat.

sections.heading: Acquired Knowledge (Taqliidii) Is Saleable:
paras: Knowledge acquired from others is always for sale. It shines only when a purchaser comes forward. But the knowledge acquired after due meditation, research, testing and enquiries is real and confirmed (tahqiiqii). This is not purchased by everyone, but certainly by God. Its sale-point is always bright and attractive, which keeps itself silent by shutting its mouth, yet engaged in both sale and purchase. It purchases fresh spiritual goods every moment. Its purchaser is Unlimited and Unbounded God, as has been stated in the Quran: ‘God has purchased of the believers their persons and their goods for theirs (in return) is the garden of Paradise’: “Innal laahash taraa minal mu’miniina anfusahum wa amwaalahum bi anna lahumul jannatan”: (Taubah: 9: 111).

The lessons given by H. Adam were purchased by the angels. Satans and fairies are not aware of these lessons. God told H. Adam to teach the angels and inform them of the mysteries, one after another, by saying: ‘O Adam! Tell them their names (the nature of all things)’: “yaa Adamu ambi’hum biasmaa’ihim”: (Baqarah: 2: 33).

Such of those short-sighted fellows who possess knowledge acquired from others including from wisdom (taqliidii knowledge), are sunk in colourfulness and show, and have no regular status and place. They hold only timely and temporary status. I have called them like rats, because they roll in mud and the place of residence of the rat in mud. The rat knows the paths that are below the mud and makes holes all along in the mud. It needs only food and therefore it is given food proportional to it. Because, God does not give anything to anyone other than what one needs.

sections.heading: Needs Provided as Required:
paras: Had not the world been in need of clay in the earth, God would not have created it. This earth was shaky, requiring something to stabilise it, and therefore lofty, large-sized mountains were created. Had the earth been not in need of skies, He would not have created the seven skies from out of nothing and nowhere. Sun, moon and stars would not have come into existence without there being purposes in their creations. All creations are in accordance with the needs of mankind both in quality and quantity as decided and provided by God. Therefore, as you are in need, and have to fulfil your needs, increase your needs so that, the ocean of God’s grace may rise high.

sections.heading: More Needs, More Grants by God:
paras: You may see this in this world also. Beggars and those in need exhibit their need and deprivation before the people to meet them. No beggar speaks of his richness and comforts while seeking the help of others. They show their blindness, crippleness, sickness and troubles so that the mercy of the people may come into action to meet their needs. No one says: “O people, give me food as I have wealth, materials and means of livelihood.” Every one speaks of his miseries and troubles.

God has not given eyes to the bat as its catching of its prey is better in its blindness. It can live without eyes and light, and does not need eyes in moist land. It does not come out for other than to commit theft. Similar is the situation of the people who are attached to the material world (Nasoot). They remain confined to materials and devote all their capacities for them. If they develop need for non-material things of higher levels, God rids them of the greed of materials, upon which they gain wings and become flying birds so as to fly high in the heavens like angels. Every moment, they sing the songs of thanksgiving like bulbuls in the God’s garden of gratefulness. They sing songs like:

“O the one who has rid me of vices! You are the converter of hell into paradise! You have created light and brightness in a lump of fat, as in the case of eyes. You have given the potentiality to the soft bones of the ears to hear and catch sounds.”

sections.heading: Words Are Only Sounds Heard by Body:
paras: What the ears hear are only sounds and words and not meanings. Because they are muscles of the body; and body has nothing to do with the understanding of meanings. Words are like the nests in which the birds reside, and birds are like the meanings of words. Only this much of difference can be understood between a name or meaning and the thing named.

sections.heading: Words Are Paths of Streams, Meanings Like Water:
paras: If there is any further understanding of word and meaning, it is that the words are like a path of stream carved out in stationary soil, while meanings are like flowing water. Again, path of the stream is the body and flowing water is its soul. The surface of the flowing water is like thoughtfulness or thinking. It carries all the good and bad things like grass, scraps, leaves, fresh and rotten fruits. Similarly thoughts also cannot remain constant but move like flowing water along with good and bad ideas. Similarly, soul is flowing, but you do not see its flow. It is running fast but you say, it is stationary. So also, the surface of water appears to be stationary. It is the scraps and floating materials on its surface that indicate to you that water is flowing. Motion of one scrap from one place and its place being occupied by another scrap, establishes the motion of the water of the stream.

sections.heading: Soul in Motion to Higher Levels:
paras: Similarly, the soul is on its motion to the higher levels of the world of angels. And thoughts are in continuing flow with new and newer offshoots. Flow of the stream of thoughts in the soul cannot remain without good and bad ideas, like scraps on the surface of water. Scraps on this flowing water of soul come about from the fruits of the garden of the unseen (invisible-to-the eye) world of meanings. They are the rinds of fruits. You may search for the pulp of the fruits by thinking over the shapes and colours of the rind. You have to search for the pulp in the invisible-to-the-eye-garden-of-the-world-of-meanings, as it is from there only, that water of meanings is flowing into your soul.

sections.heading: Overflowing of the Stream of Thoughts:
paras: If you cannot see the flow of this water, look at the flow of the stream of your thoughts and think deeply over them as to from where they come. Inevitably there must be some place of their origin. When the stream of water increases in quantity, it flows faster. So also, the stream of thoughts passes off fast. In such a case those well aware of the secrets of God (gnostics), cannot find sorrows and anger remaining in their hearts for longer time. They too pass off fast, because they are also like scraps that flow fast in the stream. When the stream gets too much water, it overflows and moves very fast. In such a situation nothing remains in the stream, except water, and the scraps wash off here and there and get scattered. The souls of the perfect masters of gnosticism do not allow any vicious thought to enter them.

An ill-witted fellow passed a remark on a master saying: “He is vicious and not on the right path. He is drunkard, treacherous and unclean. How can he hold on the hands of his disciples and guide them?”

One of the disciples said: “Hold on to good manners! Such thoughts about the great men are not ordinary matters. Such remarks are so far away from him and his character that his clean water can be polluted by a little dirty water. Do not make such false allegations upon the truthful men. What you say is only your speculation. Turn over the page of your book. There cannot be such vices in him, and even if there are, there is no fear of pollution of an ocean with a rotten dead animal. They are not lesser than two pots of water or a small pond which can be spoiled by a drop of dirty water.”

sections.heading: Matters Change as per Circumstances:
paras: Matters become different according to circumstances. H. Ibrahim faces no harm form fire set by Nimrod. Tell all such Nimrods to be afraid of H. Ibrahim. Man’s vicious self is like Nimrod and wisdom and soul are like H. Ibrahim. Nimrod’s arrogance is like fire, and wisdom and soul are like the garden of H. Ibrahim. There are different commands for the self and for the soul. Soul remains engaged in direct observation of the Absolute Truth, but the self depends upon arguments and reasonings. Arguments and reasonings are like guides for the one in journey, as there are possibilities for him to get lost in the forest. But these are not required for those who have reached the destination of the observance of God. They have their own eyes and lamps to see, and not the guides of arguments and reasonings.

sections.heading: Great Men Go to Low Levels to Teach:
paras: In spite of this, they sometimes bring forth arguments and reasons, not for their purpose, but for the purpose of explanation of matters for the sake of others. If such persons take recourse to arguments, it is for the benefit of the arguing lot. A father talks to his young child in a childish manner, even when his wisdom has seen the entire world. This is done by him for the sake of the child. Similarly, a teacher's excellence comes down form high level saying lowly things like: alif has no dots. This, he does to make the child open his mouth. Then he teaches the child such elementary things as alphabets and numbers. He feels it necessary that these things should enter into his mouth and get out of it, so that they are learnt by the child for going up to higher studies. He ignores his high level and status and behaves like a child to teach him about higher arts and sciences. Similarly, all the people are like children for the great teachers and they have to keep all this into consideration, while giving them instructions.

sections.heading: Lowly Should Not Accuse the Great:
paras: The disciple of the shaikh told the accuser full of infidelity and misguidance: “Do not take yourself before a sharp sword. Be careful not to enter into fight with such kings and sultans. If a small pond dashes against a large ocean, it puts itself to destruction from its base. He is such an ocean which has no end, and a dead rotting body like yours, cannot pollute it. Infidelity has an estimate and limit, but a master and his brightness have no end. One with limited scope does not exist before the unlimited. He gets annihilated. Everything except God is to be annihilated as the Quran says: ‘Everything (that exists) will perish except His own Face’: “kullu shai’in haalikun illaa Wajhahu”: (Al Qasas: 28: 88)

sections.heading: Man Is Great Because of Knowledge:
paras: There is no difference of faith and infidelity in the place to which the shaikh has reached, because that place is the pulp and faith; and infidelity is its rind. These are destructible things and have become a curtain before God like the lamp kept hidden under a bowl. This physical head of ours is a curtain for that spiritual head; and this head of ours is an infidel before that head. It is this head of ours that is accused of infidelity and of many ills. Who is an infidel? It is the fellow who is unaware of the faith of the shaikh. Who is dead? It is a fellow who is unaware of the shaikh’s life. Existence of life is proved after a trial of the acquired knowledge. Whoever has greater knowledge, has a greater and more worthy life. Our life is more valuable than that of the animals. It is only because of its having more knowledge than the animals. Man is aware of the entireties and parts, whereas animals know only of the parts. From the parts, man has the capacity to know about the whole. The soul of the angels is greater than our souls as it is without the physical senses that dominate men and animals. For this reason, angels are higher in status than us. But the soul of the men of God is greater than that of the angels. It is for this reason that the angels prostrated to H. Adam. His soul was far above the souls of the angels, as otherwise God would not have asked the elevated angels to prostrate to H. Adam. It is because of the fact that man is higher than angels that God ordered them to prostrate to man.

God’s benevolence and equity would not direct the flowers to prostrate to the thorns, as flowers are greater in excellence than thorns. When human soul elevated further and reached its end, the souls of all things became obedient to man. Birds, fishes and even men become obedient to elevated man, as he has greater potentials and others are deficient. Fishes became the makers of needles for stitching of his torne garment, and threads became obedient to the needle.

When the regional leader saw the enforcement of the shaikh’s command with the appearance of the fishes, he went into a state of stupor and said: “What a pity, fishes are aware of the saints; and fie upon me, for having been dismissed from the court of God. Fishes know a master but we are far away from him. We are deprived of this wealth, whereas they have obtained it.” So saying, he fell down before the saint, started crying, became broke and left the place. He became mad upon the opening of the door of secrets.

sections.heading: What About the Accuser:
paras: Now, the other fellow, who had called the shaikh as drunkard and vicious. In what thoughts are you, the ugly-faced one? For whom do you have your quarrels and jealousy? You want to play with the lion’s tail and attack the angels. Why do you consider the absolutely good ones as bad? Be careful! Do not consider this downfall as great. What is lowly is the worthless, ignoble copper. Know this, that the shaikh is a limitless alchemy. If copper was not capable of receiving the impacts of alchemy and become gold, alchemy will never become lowly copper. Who is vicious? He is the one with rebellious, fiery acts. Who is a master? He is a perfect river from the beginning itself. Bad is that fellow who increases darkness. As against this, the shaikh is a reflection of the light of God. Bad is what is full of smoke and burning fire! Shaikh is a water of Kauth(s)ar of the rainy season. Water has always been used to put out fire. Water is never afraid of blazing fire.

sections.heading: Do Not Find Fault with Great Men:
paras: You are trying to find fault in the moon and search for thorns in paradise. If you go and search for thorns in paradise, you will find yourself alone like the thorn. You are trying to hide the sun in mud and find a hole in the full moon. Sun, that shines upon the whole world, cannot hide itself for the sake of the bat. Defects have come about because of the rejection of the saintly elders. Secrets of the hidden world are hidden because the saintly elders wanted them to remain hidden. Many great jobs became defective because of their dislike for them, and certainties became doubtful because they did not believe them to be true. Be ashamed of remaining away from their courts, at least now, and become smart with the sense of deprivation so far, and make yourself useful and worthy, so that, the morning breeze may come to you from this direction. Do not stop the water of benevolence because of your jealousy for them. Though you are far away from them, you may still wag you tail of approval from this distance itself. That is the meaning of: ‘and wheresoever you are, Turn your face that side’: “wa haisu maa kuntum fawalloo wujoohakum shatrahu”: (Baqarah: 2: 150).

sections.heading: Refusal to Get Out of Troubles:
paras: When the donkey gets trapped in slush because of its fast running, it moves from this and that side vigorously to get up. It does not think of this as a place of comfort and therefore it never attempts to make it worth residing. Because of your wrong acts, your sense is worse than that of a donkey, as your heart has not come out of the slush. Instead of coming out, you think of arguments to continue to remain in slush. You say that it is proper and permissible for you to be in sinful life, as you are helpless, and God does not hold the helpless responsible for their acts. You are engaged in sins, but you do not know that you can be caught treacherously by the treacherous searchers who catch petty foolish criminals by standing outside their hiding places talking together as though they are outside, when actually they are inside. They say that they have gone outside toward the pond to drink water. Thus, they cheat and confuse them and when they come out, they catch it. This is a confusion created by cheats and you are a victim of these cheating words. And you are victim of your own confused and treacherous words.
During the times of H.Shuaib, a person used to say: “God has seen many wrongs in me. He has seen many crimes and sins in me. He is so generous that He would not catch me for my sins”.

sections.heading: Sinning Itself Is Punishment:
paras: God sent a message into H.Shuaib’s inner ear to tell him clearly about this message form the hidden world: “You say that you have committed many sins, yet God has not caught you. You are a fool to think like this. What you say is perverse and opposed to facts. You have already been misguided and put into the desert of Tia, in which the Israelites roamed about for forty years. I have been holding and catching you time and again, but you are not aware of it. From head to foot, you are in chains. You are like a blackened cauldron which is covered in layers upon layers of smoke, which have spoiled its colour. Your heart is covered with rust upon rust to such an extent that it cannot realise the secrets of matters. If a new cauldron gets stuck with smoke, it shows it blackish signs even though it is as small as the size of a grain of millet. This is because, everything appears in the presence of its opposite. Black colour gets dishonoured before the white. When the cauldron has already become black, no one cares to look at the effects of smoke on it. A black negro engaged in blacksmithy gets his face blackened by the smoke of his profession, which cannot be seen. But a fair coloured Roman blacksmith’s face becomes multicoloured by smoke which is visible. When you make a profession of sins insisting upon them continually, you get the eyes of your thinking filled up with dust. A regular sinner does not think of repentance. Sins become sweet for him. And they slowly dominate upon him to such an extent that he loses even his faith.

sections.heading: Writing upon Written Words:
paras: That sense of shame upon sins and calling of God for forgivance vanishs from him. Sixty layers of dust gather upon the mirror of his heart. His iron is eaten away by rust and the lustre of his gems becomes dull. When you write on a plain paper, the writing can be clearly seen and be readable. But if you write on an already written paper, your reading becomes wrong and you fail to understand the writing. This is because, your ink has fallen upon earlier ink, making both the writings unreadable and the meanings get lost. If you write upon them for the third time, you make the paper completely black like the heart of an unbeliever.

“Such accumulated sins have no scope to be wiped off other than by the treatment provided by the Rescuer. There is no need to be hopeless and desperate in this regard. Hopelessness is like copper and its treatment is by alchemy. Keep your hopelessness before God, The Rescuer, so as to get out of this incurable sickness.”

When H. Shuaib spoke of all this, his heart received a blow of spiritual impacts and it blossomed like a flower. His soul heard a heavenly inspirational voice, and he asked him: “If that is the case, what are the signs of the sins having been wiped off?” H. Shuaib said to God: “O God, he is getting doubts upon what was told. He wants to know of the evidence for this relief!”

sections.heading: Tasteless Prayers and Good Acts:
paras: God said: “I am a hider. I cannot reveal his secrets, excepting through a single sign to put him to trial. One sign of it is that a sinful fellow performs acts of worship like salat and fasting and pays zakat in charity and does other good acts, yet he does not get one particle’s worth of taste in them. He performs prayers and worship of high levels but does not get any pleasure and taste in them. His apparent acts of limbs and muscles are good but spiritually they are not. There are many apricots but without nuts. A taste of worship is required to get the fruits of worship. Seeds are required to germinate into a tree. A fruit without seed does not germinate into plant. A painting is only a product of thought, which has no life.”
When H. Shoaib spoke to him of all these points, that fellow went into deep thinking like a donkey caught in slush.

That senseless fellow was talking nonsense about the shaikh. Cross-eyed fellows always see things in a crossed manner. He said: “I am witness to all the misdeeds of the shaikh. He is drunkard, vicious and spoiler of all acts. I have seen him in a gathering. He is devoid of piety and is poor of character. If you do not believe me, come with me tonight to see his signs in all clarity.”

sections.heading: No Place for Sins in Annihilated Body:
paras: He took the hearer to a window and showed his sins and indulgences in pleasures, and said: “He appears noble during the day and indulges in sins during the night. He is like Prophet Muhammed during the day and like Abu Lahab at night. During the day, he is called as the obedient servant of God and at night, God forbid, he has wine glass in his hand.”

They saw a glassfull and he said: “O Shaikh, you have also been trapped. Have you not said that in a glass of wine, satan passes urine every moment?” The shaikh said: “My glass is so full that there is no place for the satan’s urine, and even for a small black grain’s smoke by burning which devils are chased away through its smoke. See, whether even a particle can occupy it.” The misguided heard this statement in a perverse manner.

sections.heading: Appearances Misguide:
paras: The shaikh meant by glass, not a glass of wine but of his own body. This is not a visible glass with visible wine. Keep the shaikh, the seer of hidden things away from him. Do not be senseless. There is no place in it for the satan’s urine. He is full of God’s light and of all spiritual wealth. The glass of his body is crushed and he exists with light in full. He is now in a state of annihilation in God. Sun’s light falls upon the dirty dust bin also. Its dirt does not make the sun dirty.

The shaikh further said: “This is neither glass, nor wine. O you rejector, come down and see and smell it.” He came down and saw that the glass was full of honey. That fellow was a blind, blue enemy. Then the shaikh said to his disciple: “O my boy! Go and bring some wine for me, as I am in pain and helplessness. My pain has become more than that of hunger. In times of adversity the impermissibles (haraam) become permissible (halaal). This is a clear statement of God in the Quran. Fie upon the fellow who refuses to accept this.”

sections.heading: Wine Converted into Honey:
paras: The disciple went towards the liquor shops and tasted the wine from every container for the sake of the shaikh. But it contained honey in all the liquor shops. He did not find any wine. Everywhere he saw the containers of wine full of honey. He told the drinkers there: “O good people appearing to be bad! What is it that is being done? I do not see any wine in any of the containers.” All the drunkards came over to the shaikh with tearful eyes, beating their foreheads in sorrow and said: “O shaikh, you came into the liquor bars, the place of sins, and because of your coming, all kinds of wines became honey. You converted the unclean wine into clean material. Convert our unclean souls also into clean ones devoid of all sins. God provides clean food for His noble servants. Even if the whole world becomes full of blood, the sincere servants of God do not eat anything other than the permissible.

One day, H. Ayesha said to the Prophet: “O Messenger of God, whether it is congregational or individual prayer, you perform your salat as per the situation without your prayer carpet, in lowly and unclean places. Please tell me the secret behind this. This you do, even when you know that an unclean child, wherever he goes, make it dirty.”

The Prophet said: “God has made unclean things clean for the great people. That is a way, God, with His grace, has made the place of my prostration clean upto the seven stages of the heavens, which are one above the other.”

Therefore, be warned not to feel jealous of such spiritual kings, as otherwise, you will become an Iblis in the world. If they eat poison, it becomes honey for them, but if you eat honey, it becomes poison for you. Because, Allah has said: ‘Allah will change the evils of such persons into good deeds’: “yubad dilul laahu saiyi aatihim hasanaat”: (Al Furqan: 25: 70). They get changed and what they do also gets changed. They become love and their fire becomes light. God had given that power to tiny birds which killed the elephants. A large army was defeated by the tiny birds, to make you understand that hardness and strength are from God [These birds had dropped tiny pebbles from above upon the army of king Abraha of Abyssinia, who had come to Ka’aba to demolish it with the might of elephants]. If you have any doubt on this, you may read surah Al Fiil (The Elephant: 5: 105) in the Quran, about the companions of the elephants. If you claim parity with great men, quarrel with them and win over them, and you may consider me as making a claim of infidelity.

A rat caught hold of the rope of the nose-ring of a camel in its hand and went on with all pride and rancour. When the camel walked fast along with it, it felt that it has become a strong wrestler. The reflection of its thought fell on the camel and it said to itself: “Be happy. I shall show you your worth.”

On the way, they came to a large river in which even huge elephants would fear to enter. The rat stood on the river bank and got dried up of all its pride. The camel told it: “O companion of mine in forest and hills! Why have you stopped? What is your worry? Go forward with courage and enter into the river. You are my guide and leader. Do not stop on the way and move forward.”
The rat said: “This is a very deep and frightening river. My friend, I am afraid of getting sunk into it.”

The camel said: “Just wait, I shall enter into water and find its depth.” And the camel put its step into water and said: “O blind rat, the water is only upto the thigh. Why do you fear and lose your sense?”
The rat said: “What is an ant for you is a python for us, as there is a great difference between your thigh and ours. If it is up to your thigh, O great one, then it is upto my scalp.”

sections.heading: False Pride Destroys:
paras: The camel said: “Then, do not show your misconduct, as its spark may not burn down your body and soul. You may compete with rats like you. It is not proper for the rat to talk to the camel.”
The rat said: “I repent now on my wrong! Take me beyond this death-causing water.”
The camel felt pity and said: “Okay, jump up on me and sit on my saddle. My crossing of the river is certain. I can take lakhs like you to the other side.”

When man is not aware of the ways of life, he should seek from others so that he may come out of the depths of the wells and proceed towards greater stages. You should become a subject, when you are not a king, and when you are not a boatman, you should not take your boat deep inside water. When you are not an experienced businessman, you should not open a shop. Learn the art of business by following other experienced businessmen, as flour becomes worthy of baking only after it turns into dough. So long as you do not know to live independently, be a slave to someone. Be careful not to wear silk garments and be satisfied with rough clothes. Hear the command “Ansitu: hold your peace, and pay heed when you hear the Quran”: (A‘raaf: 7: 204). Hear the advice and keep quiet. When you have not become the tongue of God, be like an ear to hear. You should hear sermons and advice in silence with respect. When you have doubts on matters, you should ask others in a humble, decent and direct manner (not by leading and misleading questions). You should address the kings in humble manner like the poor.

sections.heading: Habitual Arrogance and Jealousy for Leadership:
paras: Arrogance and jealousy start with the desires of the vicious self and they become a habit on continuing. Because of repeated following when they become hard, you get angry with anyone who tries to protect you from them. This leads you to be a lowly mud-eater, and you become inimical to anyone who tries to take you away from mud. Idol worshippers get habituated to idol worship and become enemies of those who prevent them from it. Iblis had become habituated to his leadership of the angels and therefore, with his foolishness, looked at Adam with contempt. He thought, how can there be another leader like me that he should be obeyed like me.

Leadership is worthy only for those souls, which have a strong antidote like the one available in the hills of Laan (which is considered to be the most effective and fastest antidote for snake poison). A man with strong antidote need not fear if he is in a hill full of snakes, as he has plenty of antidote. When leadership dominates your mind, you become inimical to everyone who challenges you. When someone tells you about your bad habits, many vicious thoughts come to your mind about him ― he is trying to keep me away from my nature; he wants to dominate over and become my leader. His opposition to the adviser itself is an evidence of the fact that he has bad habits. When the bad habit is not strong in him, there would not be a scope for the blazing fire of opposition in the furnace of his heart. As against this, he would be thankful to the adviser, and the advice penetrates into his heart.

sections.heading: Nip the Bud of Mischiefs Early:
paras: Kill the snake of passions in the beginning itself, as otherwise it will become a big python. But man thinks that his serpent is an ant. You may enquire about it with a wise, hearty man. Killing it in the beginning itself is necessary, before it becomes a python. Until there is improvement of character in you, you will not know that what you possessed earlier was wrong. Copper realises its lowly worth after becoming gold. Until a heart becomes rich like the king, it will not realise about its earlier poverty. Be obedient to the alchemy-like-character of the great men and bear with the pains of their service. Find out as to who is that great benevolent one for you! He is a man of heart, who runs away from the material gains of this world just as the day which runs away from the night, and the night that runs away from the day. Do not try to find faults with such masters and do not accuse the kings of the offence of theft; as otherwise you will become worthless among the worthless, as every lowly fellow becomes a follower of the devil.

A dervish, whose possession and support were nothing but contentment with only one garment boarded a ship. When he was asleep someone’s bag full of gold coins was lost. The luggage of everyone was checked and he was also woken up to search his luggage by the owner of the lost bag who was in great pain of loss. He was told: “A leather bag has been lost in the ship. We have searched the possessions of all. You cannot be left without searching. Remove your garment and be nude, so that people may be rid of their suspicion upon you.”

The dervish addressed to God and said: “O God! Your slave is accused of theft by the mean fellows. I leave the matter to You to decide. O Hearer of the complaints of all those in trouble! O Protector of mine in my pains! O Answerer of my callings! O My Supporter in all my needs!”

sections.heading: A Marvel Occurs:
paras: When the heart of the dervish suffered, instantly from all around, countless fishes raised their heads from the depths of water. All of them had wonderful pearls of unmatchable brilliance in their mouths. Each pearl was equal in worth to the revenues of a kingdom. This was because, it was directly form God Who has no partners. The dervish took a few pearls from their mouths and threw them in the ship and himself took a high jump, made a chair of the air and sat upon it. He sat flat on the chair just as the kings sit upon thrones. He was high aloft in the air and ship was in front of him. He said: “That ship is yours, and mine is God, as it is not proper for a thief to be with you. See, who is in a loss due to this separation. I am happy here, in loneliness, away from the people. Neither my Master would have accused me of theft, nor would He have given me in the hands of the accuser.”

The shipmates shouted: “O great man! How did you achieve this high state?” He said: “Because of your making a false accusation on a faqir. That too for a petty thing, and causing trouble to him.” Then he continued: “May God pardon me! It was because of my honouring those great kings of honour, upon whose greatness, I did not have any doubt. Those clean faqirs with clean breaths in whose honour the surah ‘Abasa’ was revealed to the Prophet. [This surah no. 80 was revealed in the honour of a blind faqir, Abdullah ibn-e-Maktum, who visited the Prophet to ask about some matters, at a time when the Prophet was engaged in talks with the leaders of Quraish. This faqir’s interruption was not liked by the Prophet, and he turned his face from him. God addressed to the Prophet with disapproval: “Why did you turn your face away from him. Perhaps your teaching would have benefited him. Instead of him, you engaged yourself with those who consider themselves to be quite self-sufficient. There is no blame upon you if people do not take you well. But you were unmindful of the one who came to you with fear in his heart” ― Free translation by Translator].

sections.heading: Wisdom Cannot Know Everything:
paras: Poverty of the godly men is purely for the sake of God Who Alone is everything and all in all. It is not to deceive or confuse people. How can I make accusations against those whom God has made the trustees of the treasures of the seven heavens? Any accusation has to be made upon my own vicious self that thinks in this manner. It is wrong to think ill of them. It is the perception of the vicious self, not of pure wisdom; nor of the special subtle light from God. Pure wisdom guides to conclusions in a proper manner. So also, special subtle light, which shows the reality of things. These can be seen and felt but cannot be explained in words. It is impossible to explain them to others. Only one who sees, feels and experiences understands them. The perceptions of the vicious self are subjective to its satisfaction not supported by pure wisdom and godly light. It is this ego that has made sophists say that every material thing, as well as space and time are illusions. That is, they do not really exist outside but exist only in the mind. It is impossible to convince them. They require to be ignored, condemned and even beaten and not engaged in arguments, because when they are beaten, they feel the pain which also cannot be explained in words but can only be felt. [ Rumi has written the Math(s)navi in the 13th century between 1258 and 1273. His conclusion that sophists or illusionists cannot be argued with and convinced is well explained in an event between two intellectual giants, Bishop Berkeley (1685 – 1753), the philosopher, and Dr. Johnson (1709 – 1784), the English Lexicographer, as late as in the eighteenth century. Johnson was told of Berkeley’s opinion, that everything is in the mind and not in reality, he cried out: ‘I refute it thus!’ and stabbed his toe on a large stone, and felt the pain which was real and not illusion, (A brief History of Time: Stephen Hawking, page 20). This theory was not Berkeley’s. It prevailed from the earliest days of the evolution of philosophy. It received a modern form through Berkeley.

In the haiography of a sufi saint, it has come that a rationalist asked, as to how to believe in the unseen god and the infliction of pain to Iblis by the fire of hell, when he is himself made of fire. The sufi took a lump of hard mud and pelted at him. He cried in pain and asked the sufi: “Why, instead of answering him, he has hit him.” The sufi said: “I have answered your question. Mud has caused you pain though you are made of mud. So also, Iblis will suffer pain with fire” Then he said: “You cannot see or show you pain to others. But you feel it. So also, God has to be felt by the inner senses and not by mind – Translator].

They look at the miracles and get astonished but later say: “It is only illusion. It is a game of tricks.” And ask, if it is real why does it not appear every time and everywhere. [They ask, if H. Musa’s staff was a snake, it should have appeared as such always. If the moon had really split on H. Muhammad’s pointing at, it should have been so always]. These miracles remain always in the visions of the clean-hearted even after the passing off of a long time after their occurrence, but not in the eyes of those possessing only animal soul and physical eyes. Those with elevated human soul and inner eyes see them always, because they are strange sights. How can beautiful peacocks remain in the dark wells of earth? Do not call me as too-talkative. I am not so. I talk very little out of a hundred and that is full with meanings.

A few sufis spoke of another sufi before the chief sufi of the khanqah: “Do justice to us in the matter of this sufi, our master!” He asked them: “What is your grievance?” One of them said: “This sufi has three hard-to-bear-wrong-habits. While talking he talks continuingly like the bell. He eats so much as twenty men would eat. And when sleeping he sleeps like the companions of the Kahaf who slept for years together.”

sections.heading: Moderation and Harmony:
paras: The shaikh turned towards him and said: “In every matter you should follow the middle course. There is a noble hadith(s) from the Prophet ― “Moderation and harmony between the humours (blood, phlegm, black bile and yellow bile) are good and maintain health. If one humour is more in the body, man falls sick.”

Do not go to possess more qualities than your friend has, as ultimately, it results in separation. Speaking of H. Musa to H. Khizr was moderate, but it was much more in comparison with him, and became a cause of separation. He told him: “You talk too much, O Musa! Excuse me! You may go away from me. The time of our separation has come! You should not talk too much when you are with me. You should become deaf and dumb like me. If you do not go away and insist upon being with me, you will be physically with me, but away and separate from my heart.”

sections.heading: Ablution for Salat:
paras: If by chance you lose your cleanliness during your salat, it tells you to go fast and clean yourself. If you do not go and continue to perform, you are doing only physical exercise. Do not be misguided. When there is no cleanliness which is a precondition for salat, there is no salat from your side.

sections.heading: Be with the Like-Minded:
paras: Go to the people who are of your level, who love and appreciate your talks, and remain thirsty for them. Watchmen watch upon men in sleep, and fishes have no need for watchmen. Those who wear showy clothes think of washermen, and those with inner beauty do not need them. Either you may give up the company of the such showy people or you may also put on showy clothes to be with them. If you do not dare do this in full, you may reduce the size of your garment, and adopt the middle path.”

That sufi said to the Shaikh about the allegations made by his friends, point by point: “The answers given by H. Khizr to H. Musa were very good and appropriate, which he had received form the all-knowing Lord. All the doubts of H. Musa were cleared, and further, he got the key answer to other questions.”

sections.heading: Middle Path in Excessive Eating:
paras: The dervish had inherited the property of wisdom through which he gave proper answers to the shaikh on what all he had said. He said: “Though the middle path in everything is good and wise, but anything being moderate is relative and not absolute. The water of a narrow stream, from the camel’s consideration is very little, but for the rat, it was large (as was the case of another camel referred to earlier). A man in need of four breadrolls daily, keeps the middle path if he eats two or three breadrolls. If he eats all the four, he is away from the middle path. He is a victim of greed like the duck which continuingly eats. One whose hunger is for ten breads, upon eating six, follows the middle path. As I have a hunger for fifty breads, I cannot be equated with one who gets satisfied with six. You get tired upon performing of ten rak‘ats of salat but I do not get tired even with five hundred rak‘ats. One can go upto the Ka’aba by walk, and another gets out of control upon going to the nearby masjid. A clean-hearted-courageous man sacrifices his life for others, but a miser feels like dying by giving just one bread to a beggar. This kind of moderation goes properly in respect of limited things which have a beginning and end. My food, relative to them is more, but from my own consideration, it is on the middle path.

sections.heading: Excessive Talking:
paras: “But as regards talking, there cannot be a beginning and end and therefore, its middle position cannot be thought of. The unlimited one like the ocean has no two boundaries. There is no scope of excess and deficiency for it. Nobody has given the clues to its beginning and end. [How true! This verse being taken as the vast expanse of the ocean. Its boundaries were not known in the 13th century (Rumi’s days). This became known much later. In 1519, Explorer Ferdinand Magellan left Spain and went west words and crossed Atlantic Ocean, passed through the strait of South America (Magellan Strait) and entered into the Pacific Ocean and then sailed to the Philippines where he and some of his captains were killed by the natives. Three years later, one of them, with eighteen Europeans and four blacks returned to Spain establishing that the vast expanse of the sea has no east-west boundaries. An outline of the world: H.A.Davies, Oxford University Press, 1967 – Translator’s note].

Thus, for the physical ocean which has no boundaries on two sides (east and west), there is no question of excessive, deficient and middle position. Its beginning and end are not known to anyone. As regards the explanation of God, the Quran said: ‘If the ocean were ink (therewith to write out) the words of my Lord, sooner would the ocean be exhausted than would the words of my Lord would be finished, even if we added another ocean like it, for its aid’: “laow kaanal bahru midaadal li kalimaati Rabbii lanafidal bahru qabla an tanfada Kalimaatu Rabbii wa laow ji’naa bimislihii madadaa”: (Al Kahf: 18: 109). That is, even if all the seven oceans become ink, there is no hope of the exhaustion of the words of the Lord. Even if all the gardens and forests become pens to write with, the fact would not alter to the slightest extent. All the ink and pens will come to end but these uncountable matters remain unconcluded.

sections.heading: Excessive Sleep:
paras: “As regards my sleep, at times, my condition appears like sleep, which is considered to be misguiding as sleep. You may consider my eyes to be in sleep but my heart as awake. My inactive body may be taken to be active inside. The noble Prophet has said: “My two eyes are in sleep but my heart does not sleep from the Lord of all creatures.” Again, he said: “My eyes sleep, but my heart does not sleep.”

The eyes of the objector are open, but his heart is in sleep. My eyes are in sleep but my heart is engaged in the affairs of the hidden world. My heart has five other inner senses apart from the external physical senses. These five inner senses are busy in observing both the worlds. Do not look at me with your weakness. What is a night for you is a day for me. What you consider as a prison for you, is a garden for me. You are throughout engaged in your personal affairs, but I am rid of my personal affairs. Your feet are caught in slush, but the same slush is a flower for me. I am with you in one place upon the earth, but I run around upon the seventh heaven like Saturn. I am not sitting along with you; and what is sitting with you is my shadow. My state is higher above than what can be thought of, because I have gone much above thoughts and their master. I have full control on my thoughts. I am not a slave of thoughts. A builder of a building lords upon it and not vice versa.

sections.heading: Victims of Thoughts and Free Thinkers:
paras: “All the people are victims of their thoughts and therefore, they are always heart-broken and sorrowful. I do not remain as a victim of my thoughts under compulsion. I deliberately offer myself to them, but whenever, I desire, I go out of them. I am as a bird flying high in the vast expanse of the sky and my thoughts are like houseflies. Houseflies cannot ride upon me. Sometimes, I come down from the high levels to the low levels, so that people may come around me to seek solace as they do with prophets and saints. But when I feel aggrieved in the company of lowly inclinations, I fly up like the birds to the skies. My feathers have grown out of my own ambitions. I have not fixed my feathers artificially on myself. The feathers of Ja‘far-i Tayyaar are active feathers, whereas the feathers of Ja‘far-i Tarraar are borrowed and showy.

sections.heading: Ja‘far-I Tayyaar and Ja‘far-I Tarraar:
paras: [Ja‘far-i Tayyaar was a paternal cousin of the Prophet. In the battle of Muuta in 8 AH, he lost both of his hands and died. The Prophet said that he has been provided with such feathers with which he can fly anywhere of his choice: He was named Ja‘far-i Tayyaar; Ja‘far the great flyer and Zul Janaahain; one with two wings.

As against him, there was another Ja‘far-i Tarraar, who was a very cunning theif who had fixed artificial feathers on his shoulders. He was called Tarraar, meaning a pick pocket and fast speaker ― Qazi Sajjad Husain]

sections.heading: Food for Body and Soul:
paras: “What all I am saying are mysterious for those who have no spiritual taste, and for those with this taste, they are very meaningful and guiding towards reality like of those who live in the horizons of the meetings of this and that world. These are only matters of meaningless claims for the crows and houseflies. For them, both empty and full cauldrons of delicious invigorating food are the same, because they need very little food, Even licking of the empty cauldron is enough for them. When you come to a stage, when a morsel of food becomes a pearl for you, you may eat how much ever you want. It becomes profitable for you.”

One day, the faqir who had said all this, in order to eliminate suspicions, vomited his food in a dish, and it was all of pearls. Food getting converted into gems is rationally impossible, but it becomes full of light in the stomach of the saints. And, he did this to show as a marvel to the less-witted companions.

But this is certain that whether it is the stomach of a saint or of the common folk, food becomes unclean. Therefore, it is necessary that you, as a novice should shut the door of your throat and put a lock on it and hide its key from others. But tell the one for whom food becomes God’s Light, to eat how much ever he wants. It is permissible for him.

If you are well aware of the truth, you will accept and put in your heart whatever claim I make without asking for proof. If I tell you at midnight that I am before you and do not fear me because of the darkness, you will consider both these claims as true. Both these claims are established as true by you just as you recognise the voice of your close-ones. Being present before you is one claim and that I am related to you is another claim. For a man of good sense, both these claims are true. Closeness of the voice itself is coming from a friend and known person.

sections.heading: Claims That Do Not Require Proof:
paras: The pleasure of hearing the voice of a close-one gives the proof that the voice also contributes, as a further proof of it being his. Those fools who are deprived of the enlightenment from God, out of their ignorance, cannot understand the difference between the voices of their close-ones and strangers. Speaking to them of the words of great men means only words. They do not understand their meanings and reject them. Their entire capital is their ignorance. But the wise whose inside is full of light, find out that the voice is, in fact, true and correct. It is like a man knowing Arabic, claiming in Arabic itself, giving a proof of his knowledge of Arabic. His saying that he knows Arabic is only an unwanted claim. Or like a writer writing on paper claiming that he is a writer. He can read written matters and he is aware of alphabets. What all he says about his writing capacity is a claim and what is written by him is its proof. Or like a sufi telling you that the person with a prayer carpet on his shoulder that you saw in your dream who gave such and such advice to you was he, you will accept his claim without seeking any proof of it, because you have seen him in the dream as well as physically in front of you. Keep his advice firmly in your ear as you do with an earring. Make his words as your guide. Whenever you think of this dream, what you saw and heard will be like a miracle for you. Though what he said was a claim, but what really happened is the proof.

sections.heading: Claims Coupled with Actions:
paras: When the statement of wisdom, which is the lost property of the faithful (as stated by the Prophet) comes, you will believe in it and accept it when you hear it. Because, when you see it right before you, there is no scope for any doubt. If you suspect, it means that you are suspecting yourself. When you tell a thirsty person that you have water in your vessel, he should come fast and take it. There is no scope for the thirsty person to say that it is only a claim and that he should be given a proof of the claim, that it is a worth-drinking water. He will instantly come and take water which is the proof of claim. Or of a mother who calls her baby and says: “O my son, I am your mother.” Will the baby say: “Give me a proof of your being my mother, so that I may drink your milk.”

sections.heading: Claims Accepted by the Faithful Soul:
paras: Those followers of the Prophet with a taste of truth, take the Prophet’s face and voice as miracles. When the Prophet calls them from outside, their souls prostrate inside, because the ear of the soul does not hear any other voice in the world other than his voice. That journeyman of this or that world with a taste of the Prophet’s voice simply falls in prostration and goes nearby to God. When he falls in prostration with all his heart and soul, he hears the voice of God saying: certainly I am nearby to you, as stated in the Quran: ‘When My servants ask you concerning Me, I am indeed close to them’: “Wa izaa sa’ alaka ‘ibaadii ‘annii fa innii qariibun”: (Baqarah: 2: 186).

When H. Yahya’s mother was pregnant with him, she was sitting in front of H. Maryam (Mary). She said in low tone to H. Maryam before delivery: “I feel certain that you are pregnant with a great king who would be of great state and well-informed prophet of God. When I came before you, the baby within me prostrated to the baby in your womb, because of which I felt pain. H. Maryam said: “I also found within me the prostration of that child.”

The ill-witted say that: “A line should be drawn on this incident to score it off as it is false and wrong because, at the time of her delivery, H. Maryam was away from both her relatives and strangers. She was not with anybody during the period of her pregnancy. She had not come back to the city. That one with sweet breath did not come back until after delivery. The Quran says: ‘She conceived him (baby Jesus in her womb), and she went with him to a remote place’: “Fahamalat hu fantabazat bihi makaanan qasiyyaan”: (Maryam: 19: 22). Only after delivery she came to her tribe with the baby in her arms. Where had H. Yahya’s mother seen her, that she spoke to her as per this narrative?”

sections.heading: Purport and Meanings, Not Sounds and Words:
paras: The purport and meanings of such narratives can be understood by one for whom the hidden world is clearly visible. He sees both H. Maryam and H. Yahya’s mother right before him, even though they are far away from him both in space and time. One who has made a mess of his body and skin through penances and meditations can see anything he wants by closed eyes. Do not think of actually seeing them but go after the hidden meanings within the narrative. Has it not happened that you have heard some stories only for entertainment but considered them as lessons of wisdom. Sheen (sh) is an alphabet in the Persian language. There is also a word naqsh in which it is joined with another letter, noon. You cannot consider the alphabet (Sheen) as just shape when it is in combination with other letters. It appears differently in different combinations.

sections.heading: Similies and Metaphors:
paras: You have heard a large number of statements in the narratives of Kalila and Damna, spoken by them to each other. Both of them are jackals, who cannot speak, but in the narratives, you see them speaking of many points of wisdom. They have actually not said or heard any words. But they were supposed to convey something to each other without words. But when statements of wisdom were to be understood by men, they had to be through spoken or written words. These are narrated as incidents in which Damna acts as a messenger between the lion and cow and casts its spell on both. A fat ox became a minister of lion and an elephant got frightened by the reflection of moon in wavering water. Both of them, Kalila and Damna are not real, but only imaginary. All stories narrated about them are imaginary. The crow has been shown as being in the company of a crane, which have no comparison with each other. [Notes about Kalila and Damna have been given in an earlier part of the book ― Translator].

You should know a narrative or story is only like a measure to know the quantity of grains. The requirement and need are of the grain and not of the measure. Where there is no grain, there is no need of the measure. A wise man goes for the grains of meanings and not the measures.

You hear of dialogues between the bulbul and the flower though there is no exchange of words between them. Similarly, you hear the stories of the moth and lamp and know what they mean. There is no talk between them. What is attributed to them is full of meanings. Be alert and fly high above in the sky and not hop like the owl. Someone while playing chess said: “This is the house of a chessman.” Another said: “From where did he get a house? Did he purchase it or got in inheritance?” The fellow who asked these questions goes after words and not the meanings. Fortunate is the one who goes after the meanings.

sections.heading: Incapacity to Understand:
paras: The grammarian said to his pupil: “Zaid beat Amru.” He wanted to teach about the subject and object in the grammatical sentence to show that Zaid is the beater (subject) and Amru is the object (beaten). Instead of trying to understand this, the pupil said: “Why did he beat him for no wrong. What was his mistake? It is highly wrongful that Zaid has beaten the innocent Amru like a slave.”

The grammarian said: “This is an example as a measure to understand the meanings. These are words which are only a measure of meanings. You must take the meaning. Once you take the meaning, the measure is of no use. Both Zaid and Amru are imaginary persons to make a sentence to convey a meaning to you. Even if they are non-existents, you should take the meanings and not go after names.”

The pupil said: “I do not know all this. All I want to know is, why did Zaid beat Amru for no mistake or wrong.” The grammarian realised the inability and helplessness of the pupil to understand and silenced him by saying: “Amru was actually Amr, but he stole an alphabet ‘U’ and became Amru. Zaid came to know of this, and as he had gone beyond the limit, Zaid beat him for chastisement.”

Then the pupil said: “Now, this is right. I am satisfied.” A wrong statement appears right to the wrong persons. If you tell a squint-eyed that the moon is one, he will say: “No, there is a doubt in its being one.” If, someone out of fun, tells him there are two moons, he will believe him to be truthful. This is the punishment for a defective person. Liars get pleased with lies. Unclean women are worthy for unclean men. Generous people have generous hands. Even a soft path appears full of stones to the blind, and they stumble. One in the habit of telling lies, will not find truth to be trustworthy. A truthful person is free of lies and uncleanliness.

A wise man to decorate his words said as a narrative: “There is a tree in India, the fruits of which upon eating would give everlasting life. Its eater neither dies nor becomes old.” A king heard this from that wise man and fell in love with that tree and its fruits. He sent a person from among his disciplined, wise courtiers to India to search for that tree. This man searched for it all over India for years together. He left no city, island, mountain and forest unsearched to meet his object.

Whomsoever he asked about it made fun of him thinking that such a search cannot be made by anyone other than a mad fellow worthy of being confined as a lunatic. Many people slapped jokes on his face, but many called him as an innocent fool, saying that the searches made by a clean, hearted wise man like him cannot go waste and useless. This kind of good consideration was another slap on his face. This hidden slap was worse than the open slaps. They used to tell him in fun: “O great man, there is a very frightening land of large expanse, in which there is a green tree, very tall and full of leaves with very thick branches.”

The king’s agent was determined to search for that tree, but from everyone he used to hear a different version. He searched for it for years together and the king sent money for his expenses. At last, he got tired when he found great difficulties in this hard search. He did not find his object and what he got was only taunting words. He lost the chain of his hopes, and his search itself became unsearchable. He decided to return to the king and shed tears from his eyes on the way.

There was a great learned man of the level of the pole of knowledge (Qutub) in a camp, who was surrounded by many desperate men. The searcher said to himself: “I am also desperate having lost all hopes. Perhaps form his place, I may find the proper way to proceed, and his blessings may be my companions as I have no other hope.”

With tears in his eyes he went before the great master (shaikh). Tears were falling from his cloudfull eyes. He said to the shaikh: “O Shaikh, the time of showing benevolence and mercy has come. I am desperate. This is a time for showing concern to me.” The Shaikh said: “Tell me clearly as to what has made you lose hopes. What is your object and what do you want to achieve?” He replied: “My king selected me out of others to search for a tree in the surroundings, the fruit of which is the capital of the life-giving-water. I searched for it for years, but could not find it. I became the victim of laughter of punsters and jokers.”

sections.heading: Knowledge Is the Tree of Life:
paras: The shaikh laughed and said: “O simpleton, the tree you searched for is the tree of knowledge in the heart of the scholar, which is very high, wonderful and much spread over. It is the life-giving-water from the coastless ocean of God’s knowledge. You went over its shape, without knowing its reality, because you are without the knowledge of the meaning of its branches and fruits.
