Sometimes it is called as tree, and sometimes as sun as it gives light. Sometimes, it is called as ocean as it has no limits; and sometimes as cloud, which fells rain and brings about freshness and life. It is one, but it has lakhs of products, and as such it has numerous names.

sections.heading: Different Aspects of the Same Thing
paras: “A man is a father for you, and for another, he is a son. So also, uncle, brother and so on. For one, he is tyrannous and inimical and for another, he is good and benevolent. For one, he is uncle and for another, he is unworthy and just only as a passing thought. He is one, but he has many of names. Everyone knows some qualities of the tree of knowledge and ignorant of others. One who goes in search of honour only, however good he may be, will be hopeless and worried like you. Why do you attach yourself to the name of that tree? Do not do so, as otherwise, you will be unsuccessful and unfortunate. Do not search for the apparent face.

“Go and search for the meanings and be successful like a brave man. Apparent face is like the rind and skin and the meaning is the pulp. Do not remain attached to the rind. Go for the qualities and through them to the essence of matters. Then, you may penetrate into the essence, when you will be lost to yourself. Then your eyes will see the good and bad as the same, as names indicate only the states which are different from each other. When you go into the depths of things, everything is the same.”

People are away from each other because of the differences of names, but they become peaceful and one, when they understand the meanings. Hear a good example in connection with meanings so that you may not remain entangled with names.

A person gave one dirham to four persons, who had all assembled together in the city having come from different places. They were Persian, Turk, Roman and Arab. All of them were hungry and quarrelsome with each other. The Persian asked as to what should be done with the dirham. Then he said: “I shall give to the seller of Angoor.” The Arab said: “No, you are a treacherous fellow. Give it to the one who is selling Inab, not angoor.” The Turk said: “You are a fool. I have no desire for Inab, I want awzam.” The Roman said: “Forget all this. I want Istafill.”

In this manner they quarrelled with each other, as they were not aware of the meanings of all these names. They started exchanging blows. They were all full of ignorance and devoid of common sense. Had there been a learned man knowing a hundred languages, he would have brought peace among them telling: “With this one dirham, I can fulfil the desires of all of you. If you give this one dirham to me without any ill will for each other, your single dirham can meet the objects of all of you. Your one dirham would become worth four, and with unity four enemies will become friends.”

sections.heading: Difference of Languages:
paras: Different languages of all of you are creating separation and quarrels amongst you. My words will bring about unity. Therefore, be quite and do not talk so that my words may become your common language. If your language were to be the same, this anger and quarrel would not have resulted. You were all one and together when you received the coin and you quarrel now, on an ordinary point, even though what all you say is reliable and the same. This resulted in quarrels and disputations.”

sections.heading: Temporary Effects of Borrowed Causes:
paras: Barrowed warmth does not cause lasting effect, but original heat is very effective. Even if you heat vinegar with external heat on fire, it will certainly increase your cold as its hotness is temporary and borrowed. This is because, its real nature is to cause cold and sharpness. Syrup of grapes causes heat in the liver, even if you cool it down to the level of ice, because its real nature is to cause heat. Similarly, the showiness and ostentation of the master is better than our sincerity, because he resorts to it from out of his inner sight, and our sincerity is out of blind followership. Words of the shaikh bring about unity but the words of the jealous cause disunity, because the shaikh brings together his disciples of different tastes.

sections.heading: Peace Comes Under a Great Man:
paras: As H. Sulaiman ran towards the court of God, he learnt the languages of all the birds. Under his justice system, the deer developed love for the jaguar and there was no quarrel between them. The pigeon got protected from the clutches of vulture, and the lamb did not bother to protect itself from the wolf. He became a third, neutral party among the enemies. All birds were one under him. You go after a grain like the ant. Do not do so, but go after a great person like H. Sulaiman. For the one who goes after the grain, grain itself becomes a trap and he gets trapped in it. But the one who goes after H. Sulaiman, gets both Sulaiman and the grain. In your days, if you go after a great shaikh, you will get the shaikh as well as other things. In these days of the last period, people’s lives are different form each other like birds, and have no peace form each other, even for a little time.

sections.heading: Every Nation Has Its Leaders:
paras: In our days also there is a H. Sulaman, who can bring about peace amongst us and eliminate cruelties. Learn by heart, this statament of the Quran: ‘And there is no nation, but a warner has passed among them’: “wa inna min ummatin illaa khalaa fiihaa naziirun”: (Fatir: 35: 24). God has said: “No nation will be without a man of inner qualities as vicegerent of God. He will make the souls of the people one, and with his clean spirit make them clean-hearted, without ill-will. They will love each other as the mother loves children and will make all Muslims with one heart. They will become one soul, as the Prophet has called them as single soul: ‘Nafsun waahidatun’. They all became one soul under his impacts, as otherwise, earlier, they were enemies of each other. The unity that is devoid of mutual participation, will become one when ‘you’ and ‘us’ come about in singleness.

There were two tribes – Aws and Khazraj, in Arabia who were always at loggerheads, and thirsty of each other’s blood. Their age-old ill will for each other was wiped off by H. Mustafa, and they got engaged in the light and purity of Islam. First, these enemies became brothers just as in the grapevines. Each grape has its identity, inspite of being in the same cluster and then, they all progress under the spell of the verse of the Quran: ‘The believers are but a single brotherhood’: “Innamal mu’minoona ikhwatun”: (Hujaraat: 49: 10). They broke off all separateness and became one body. They were brothers like the grapes, which upon being crushed, became one syrup.

sections.heading: Fate Decided in the Beginning Itself:
paras: The tender grape and ripe are opposed to each other in quality, but when the tender grape ripens, it becomes a good friend of the ripe one. The tender grape that dried up remained as such as God decided its fate well before the beginning itself (Azal) to be as such. It does not become a brother of the other grapes nor it becomes one with others upon crushing. It remains as an infidel and rejector of goodness because of its hardness and misfortune. Similar in the case of the infidels and atheists whose fate is decided at the time well before creation itself (Azal). This was the case of men like Abu Jahl and Abdullah bin Ubbi, who neither became Muslims nor their brothers. They were Kaafar e-Azali (predestined rejectors).

sections.heading: Secrets of Infidels Not to Be Told:
paras: The fate of one who is a kaafar (rejector) from well before the beginning itself and the one who is a faithful as such, is better not explained about as there is a great secret behind this decision of God. If I reveal that secret, it will lead to a great trial and mischief to wisdom and understanding. It is better that the secret of the blind rejector is kept untold, as the smoke of hell must remain away from the garden of Iram (the model of paradise that Shaddad, the king of ‘Aad had built in this world).

Raw grapes with capacity to develop into ripe ones, ripen along with others and attain all potentialities of ripe grapes and remain together. They move fast with others to become full-fledged grapes, resulting in the elimination of their separateness, individuality and indifference. They become one with others and all separating tendencies vanish. After ripening, they all tear off their skin and become one in the syrup, and oneness alone is their quality.

sections.heading: Duality Liable to Create Enmity
paras: So long as there is duality, two friends being different from each other as independent individuals are liable to become enemies, but upon their becoming one, there is no scope for enmity. On the contrary, love comes between them. No one fights against himself. Love is a great master needing all appreciation, which brings about unity of hundreds of thousands of particles, as can be seen when the dust particles of the roads become a pot in the hands of a potter. This example of particles of dust and water becoming a single body of a pot is imperfect as it is a unity of the physical bodies. It is not comparable with the unity of souls. If I go on explaining the examples of the hearts of the faithful people, I am afraid, lots of confusions would arise in the minds.

sections.heading: Causes of Unity Ignored by All:
paras: There is a Sulaiman even now, who can make us all one, but we have all become blind to see him because of our selfish desires. Too much far-sightedness about the worldly matters makes men blind just a man in sleep is ignorant of and blind to the house in which he is sleeping. He passes form east to west, but remains unaware of his friends and colleagues by his side. We are experts in explaining the intricate matters of worldly affairs and take great pleasure in resolving their subtitles. We think over new problems of life and solve them and make rules and guidelines in this connection.

sections.heading: Birds Unknotting Nets:
paras: In this matter, we are like the bird caught in a net, which opens a knot of the net, and then puts a knot again and becomes an expert in this job of unknotting and knotting, but never succeeds in getting out of the net. It is always deprived of the forests and meadows and spends its whole life in the knotting and unknotting job. The net never breaks at its efforts. On the contrary, its feathers break off. Therefore, it is better that you are engaged less in this unknotting, so that your feathers and wings may remain intact and not break off in your efforts of grandeur and glory of this life. Lakhs of birds got their feathers and wings broken, but they could not put an end to the attacks on life. Read about their affairs, O greedy fellow, in the Quran: ‘And how many a generations we destroyed before them, - mightier in power than they? And they wander through the land: was there any place of escape (for them)?: “Wa kam ahlaknaa qablahum min qarnin hum ashaddu minhum batshan fanaqqaboo fil bilaad, hal mim mahees”: (Qaaf: 50: 36).

sections.heading: H. Sulaiman Is Being Ignored:
paras: From the quarrels of these four ― Persian, Turk, Roman and Arab, difficulty of angoor and inab was not solved. It continues in various other forms. This will not end until H. Sulaiman, the truthful knower of all languages does not come forward. O, all the quarrelling birds, hear the sound of the drums made to call back the falcon by the king upon hearing which the falcon returns. Be careful! Give up all quarrels and go toward unity from all directions with all pleasure as directed in the Quran: ‘And wherever you are, turn your face in that direction’: “wa haith(s)u maa kuntum fawalloo wujoohakum shatrahu”: (Baqarah: 2: 144). We are like blind birds and incomplete in stature. We have not seen the Sulaiman of our time even for a moment. Like the owls, we are the enemies of the falcon and therefore we have fallen backward toward destruction. With our foolishness and blindness, we cause troubles to the dear ones of God.

sections.heading: Birds Under the Guidance of H. Sulaiman:
paras: Such of the birds whose hearts are brightened by H. Sulaiman do not snatch the feathers and wings of other innocent birds. Rather they take grains to feed the helpless. And they are all happy without any mutual controversies and ill-will. Hoopoes among them open the door for hundreds like Bilqises (Queen of Sheba) to go toward holiness. The crow (zaagh in Persian) among them is a crow to look at; but it is not like what is said about Prophet Muhammed in the Quran as the Arabic word zaagh (swerving): ‘His sight never swerved, nor did it go wrong!’: “Maa zaaghal bașaru wa maa taghaa”: (Najm: 53: 17) as was the case of the Prophet. The crane (laklak in Arabic) which creates the sound laklak (for you in Arabic) is in praise: “You, O God.” Their pigeons do not fear the falcons, rather the falcons submit before them. Their bulbuls get ecstatic by having a garden within themselves, and not outside. Their parrots do not need sugar as they have everlasting sugar within themselves. The feet of their peacocks are better to look at than the feathers of the other birds. Their doves laugh at hawks and fly high in the path of the Illiyiin (highest place). The sounds of khaqani’s book − “Mantiq u ttair” (words of the birds) containing many wise statements made by the birds, is just one statement as against their words in H. Sulaiman’s words. You cannot understand the sounds of the birds, because, you have not seen H. Sulaiman even for a moment.

sections.heading: Powers of H. Sulaiman’s Birds:
paras: The bird, the sounds of which enthral, comes from outside the confines of east and west. Every wish of such birds reaches form the underneath of earth to the place high above the ‘Arsh’ (area beyond the space), with all grandeur and grace. The bird that goes without the guidance of H. Sulaiman is like the bat, which is a lover of darkness. Therefore, be with H. Sulaiman and do not get rejected like the bat, so that you may not live in darkness for ever. If you just go toward him by one yard, you will become a yardstick for the measurement of everything around you. And when you walk like a lame and cripple toward him, you will cease to be lame and cripple.

You are a duckling hatched by a domestic hen, which reared you under her wings and feathers. Your mother was a bird form the river, but your caretaker was a land bird. Inspite of this the inclination of your heart is towards the river and this has come to you from your mother. You have a little inclination toward land also but this is due to the impact of your caretaker. But you ignored it as she was on the wrong side. You should totally ignore her and run towards the river which is the right place for ducks. If your caretaker creates fear of water, you should ignore her and run toward water. You are a creature, which can live both on land and water, not like the domestic hen, which sticks to land only.

sections.heading: Man to Conquer Land, Sea and Air:
paras: So also, is the nature of man who steps upon both land and water. God has said: ‘We have honoured the sons of Adam; provided them with transport on land and sea’: “Wa laqad karramnaa Banii Aadama wa hamalnaahum fil barri walbahri”: (Bani Israil: 17: 70). Because of the soul’s power, you go upon the sea also, but generally, you go about on land with your body. Sea is like the soul of God which embraces all other souls and you have to go to it. Angels have no place upon land; other animals also do not know of the qualities of the sea. But you are a land animal form the body’s side and angel from the soul’s side. Thus, you are enabled to go in the heavens like angels apart from on land. This is the unique greatness of man that he is superior to other animals and angels. Both land, oceans and air are under his command.

sections.heading: Man Blessed with Spiritual Power:
paras: In external appearance you are man as was told to the Prophet by God: “Say: ‘I am but a man like yourselves, (but) the inspiration has come to me, that your God is one God’: “Qul innamaa ana basharum mith(s)lukum yoohaa ilaiya annamaa ilaahukum illaahun Waahid”: (Al Kahf: 18: 110). But from the point of view of: “inspiration has come to me”, that is, upon the heart, you are one with great inner sight. Man’s body being made of earth lives upon earth, but his soul roams about upon the high, elevated heavens, just as the noble Prophet’s soul moved around on the upper world. So also your soul moves there.

sections.heading: Protective Shields Provided by H.Dawood:
paras: We are like the aquatic birds and the sea understands us in full. This is about the water birds. And H.Sulaiman is like the ocean, and we are like the birds under his control, and he has his impacts on us. So also is the case with our spiritual guide (shaikh). Step into the ocean of the gnosis of God along with the shaikh (Sulaiman), so that H. Dawood may make thousands of iron shields to protect you from unwanted attacks. The rings that move around you when you step into water in the form of water waves are like the iron shields made for you by H. Dawood in whose hand iron melted like wax.

sections.heading: Look at Causer, Not the Causes:
paras: Sulaiman is right before everyone of us. But our ignorance and arrogance blindfold our eyes and cast magic spells. We do not care to see him because of our confinement in sleep and absurdities. Sounds of thunder create headache in an ignorant thirsty fellow, who does not know that they open the gates of the clouds of prosperity and provide water to meet his thirst. He is in search of flowing water. He thinks of the stream alone as the source of water. He does not have the knowledge that the source of water are the clouds is the sky. He drives the horse of his wisdom towards the cause and remains unaware of the Creator of the causes. One who looks at the Causer of causes in clarity, will never look at the various causes in the world. He finds a clear morning of deliverance, success and victory from the Causer of causes. He receives from the Causer so much of information within a few moments, which others get in a hundred years of struggle.

There was a godly man deeply sunk in worship sitting upon the hot sand of a desert like the people of Abbadan, (which is a very hot place). Many hajis from different places came over to that place and their eyes fell on this thin, weak person. His place of sitting was dry hot sand but he was fresh and wet. The hot wind of the desert was as though a cold wind for him. The hajis were astonished at his loneliness and his remaining safe in that troublesome sorroundings. He was standing up for salat on the sand, which was so hot that it could boil water.

In such a difficult situation, you would feel him to be in a garden of greenery and flowers. Or, he was in flight upon burraq sitting upon which the noble Prophet had gone towards the heavens; or, proudly riding upon duldul, the mule that the king of Alexandria had sent as present to the Prophet. Or, he has kept his feet upon soft silk and wearing silk garments. Or, the hot air was better than the cool morning breeze of the gardens. He was standing with a fresh face for salat full of humility, submission and devotion. He was in secret conversation with his Beloved and completely sunk in his long, deep surroundings.

The group of hajis stood up in all respect waiting for him to finish his prayer. When that dervish came out of his depths of commitments, one haji with a bright conscience in the group, saw that water was dripping from his face and hands and his clothes were wet with water as though he has just then performed ablution. So, he asked him: “From where did you get water?” The dervish lifted his hand up and said: “From the sky.” He asked him: “Do you get water whenever you are in need, without a well, and rope to draw water? O king of the religion, pray solve our problem, so that your situations may grant us confidence in God. Please open up one of your secrets upon us, so that we may cut off the zunnar that we have tied around our waists.” (zunnar is a cotton thread that Brahmins and Zorastrians tie around the chest or waiste as a token of their faith, belief and hope on God).

The man of desert turned his eyes towards the sky to pray to God to accept the prayers of the hajis and said: “I am in the habit of searching for my food in the upper world, as You have opened for me the door of that world. O the One, You have shown to a man this special world, the world beyond space and exposed to him the meaning of: ‘And in heaven is your sustenance’: “Wa fissamaa’irizqukum” (Zaariyat: 51: 22).

During the course of this supplication, a thick cloud resembling an elephant full of water appeared. It started flowing water as though from a goatskin which filled up the caves and pits in the area. Cloud was felling water like tears and all the hajis opened their goatskins. Another group started tearing off the zunnars from the waists upon looking at this strange observation. [Perhaps some converts from Zorastrians to Islam still continued the habit of wearing zunnars ― Translator].

Another group was strengthening its confidence in God with this strange scene as God knows best in the matter of giving guidance. Yet, there were some people who were immature and of sour taste, who were not impressed. They were the eternally defective ones. The discourse is concluded.
